system_overview.platform_name: MART - Marketing Autonomous Response & Telemetry Platform
system_overview.one_line_definition: A closed-loop marketing intelligence system that ingests every UA, monetization, product and finance signal for a mobile game portfolio, materializes them into a cohort-grain semantic layer, runs 21 specialized autonomous agents plus a chief orchestrator on top of that layer, and converts detections into explained, guardrailed, auditable actions on live ad networks and remote config.

problem_statement.current_state: Marketing teams operate 8-15 disconnected dashboards (network UIs, MMP UI, BI tool, spreadsheets). Decisions are made on D0-D3 signals (CPI, installs) because cohort economics (D30 ROAS, payback) arrive 7-30 days late. By the time a bad cohort is visible, 3-14 days of spend is already sunk.
quantified_pain: Detection latency: median 4.5 days between a cohort-quality regression starting and a human noticing it. At a portfolio spend of $250k/day with 12% of spend on the regressed segment, that is ~$135k of misallocated spend per incident.
Root-cause latency: median 2-3 analyst-days per incident to answer 'which dimension broke'.
Coverage gap: humans review roughly the top 20 campaigns by spend; a 600-campaign x 40-geo x 300-creative portfolio has ~7.2M metric-dimension time series, of which <1% is ever looked at.

Local optimization: network optimizers and UA managers optimize CPI/installs; ad monetization optimizes eCPM; product optimizes session length. Nobody owns blended cohort payback, so the three teams routinely make each other's numbers worse.
problem_statement.why_a_dashboard_is_not_enough: A dashboard requires a human to (a) look, (b) at the right slice, (c) at the right time, (d) know the baseline, (e) know the causal model, (f) have permission to act, (g) actually act. MART removes (a)-(f) and gates (g) behind explicit, per-agent, per-action-type autonomy policy.

system_overview.mission: Continuously understand portfolio marketing performance at cohort grain, detect opportunities and regressions within minutes of the underlying data landing, determine the most probable root cause with an explicit confidence score, recommend a specific corrective action with quantified expected value, and - only where explicitly permitted and inside hard financial guardrails - execute that action and measure whether it worked.

design_principles.meaning: Every economic decision is evaluated on the acquisition cohort (install-date grain), never on reporting-date grain. A 'spend day' and a 'revenue day' are never divided by each other to produce ROAS.
design_principles.enforced_by: The semantic layer physically forbids joining spend_by_report_date to revenue_by_event_date; ROAS is only exposed via the cohort_daily fact table keyed on (cohort_key, days_since_install).

design_principles.principle: No alert without a cause hypothesis and a dollar number
design_principles.meaning: An emitted finding must carry: what changed, when it changed, which dimensions carry the change, the ranked candidate causes with posterior probabilities, estimated 30-day P&L impact, and a proposed action.
design_principles.enforced_by: Event bus schema validation rejects any FINDING event lacking root_cause_candidates[], impact_usd_30d, and recommended_actions[].

design_principles.meaning: Confidence is a computed composite of statistical strength, data completeness, sample adequacy, cross-agent corroboration, model backtest quality, and the historical hit-rate of this agent on this action type. It is recalibrated weekly against realized outcomes.
design_principles.enforced_by: decision_engine.confidence_model; Scholar agent (AGT-LRN-21) refits calibration and can globally down-weight an agent.

design_principles.principle: Autonomy is a per-action-type grant, never a global mode
design_principles.meaning: An agent is not 'autonomous'. A tuple (agent, action_type, entity_scope, dollar_band, confidence_band) is autonomous. Everything else is Recommend or Observe.
design_principles.enforced_by: governance.autonomy_matrix evaluated by the Warden agent + OPA policy bundle at the Action Gateway; default deny.

design_principles.principle: Every automated action is reversible and pre-committed to a rollback trigger
design_principles.meaning: Before execution, the action record stores prior_state, rollback_procedure, rollback_trigger_conditions and rollback_deadline. If the trigger fires, reversal is automatic and does not require the agent that caused it.
design_principles.enforced_by: action_execution_layer two-phase commit + Rollback Daemon reading the action journal independently of agent processes.

design_principles.meaning: A local KPI improvement that degrades portfolio contribution margin is blocked. The orchestrator holds the objective function; agents hold only their subgoal.
design_principles.enforced_by: chief_orchestrator.global_objective_function + conflict resolution; no action reaches the gateway without an orchestrator-issued execution token carrying a portfolio-level impact estimate.

design_principles.principle: Data quality is a first-class blocker
design_principles.meaning: Agents cannot act on data that is stale, partially loaded, or failing contract checks. Freshness and completeness are inputs to every decision, not a separate ops concern.
design_principles.enforced_by: Janitor agent (AGT-DQ-14) publishes DATA_FRESHNESS_STATE; the Action Gateway hard-denies execution when any upstream dataset in the action's lineage is degraded.

design_principles.meaning: Every new agent, model version, or playbook runs 30 days in Observe, then 30 days in Recommend with human accept/reject logged, before any autonomy grant is even eligible.
design_principles.enforced_by: governance.promotion_gates; the autonomy matrix will not accept a grant for an agent whose shadow_days or precision_at_action_type thresholds are unmet.

design_principles.meaning: Explanations are structured objects (evidence[], counterfactual, contribution decomposition, model version, data snapshot id). The LLM renders prose from the object; the object is the record of truth.
design_principles.enforced_by: explanation_artifact schema in governance.explainability; the LLM never invents a number - it may only reference fields present in the evidence bundle, validated by a numeric-grounding checker.

design_principles.principle: Determinism where possible, LLM where necessary
design_principles.meaning: Detection, thresholds, statistics, and action limits are deterministic code. The LLM layer is used for hypothesis generation, cross-source narrative synthesis, unstructured input (creative content, store reviews, network changelogs), and natural-language interrogation - never for arithmetic or for authorizing an action.

business_context_assumptions.note: All absolute dollar guardrails in this spec are expressed as formulas over these parameters so the spec ports to a different spend scale without rewriting limits. Change these in config, not in agent code.

economic_targets.cash_constraint_note: Payback beyond 120 days is a cash-flow decision, not a marketing decision - requires Finance role approval regardless of LTV.

scaling_parameters.derivation_rule: Every guardrail dollar cap in this spec is written as a percentage of S_daily, S_title, or S_campaign. Config service resolves them nightly at 00:05 UTC from the trailing 7-day actuals.

north_star_objectives.primary: Maximize portfolio 180-day contribution margin subject to (a) payback <= 120 days, (b) monthly spend <= budget envelope, (c) no single-day spend variance > 15% of plan.
north_star_objectives.objective_function: maximize  SUM_over_cohorts[ pLTV_180(cohort) * installs(cohort) * (1 - rev_share) ] - SUM[ spend(cohort) ] - fixed_opex,  s.t. payback_days(cohort_group) <= 120, |spend_day - plan_day| / plan_day <= 0.15, monthly_spend <= envelope
supporting_objectives: Minimize time-to-detection (TTD) of any material regression to < 60 minutes for real-time metrics and < 6 hours for cohort-maturing metrics.
Minimize time-to-correct-action (TTA) to < 4 hours for Mode 3 actions and < 1 business day for Mode 2 actions.
Keep false-positive rate of emitted findings < 15% (measured by human adjudication + realized outcome).

mode_1_observe.name: Observe
mode_1_observe.definition: Agent detects, investigates, quantifies, explains, and publishes findings to the event bus and dashboard. It proposes nothing and touches nothing.
mode_1_observe.when_used: New agents in shadow period; any agent operating on a dataset flagged degraded; any agent whose 30-day precision has fallen below its promotion threshold; all agents during a declared change freeze; all agents on a title in the first 14 days after a major release.

mode_2_recommend.name: Recommend
mode_2_recommend.definition: Agent produces a fully specified, executable action proposal - exact entity ids, exact parameter deltas, expected value, downside, rollback plan - that a human approves or rejects with one click. Approval executes through the same Action Gateway as Mode 3, with the same guardrails.
mode_2_recommend.when_used: Default for all financially material actions; anything above the agent's autonomous dollar band; anything below the agent's autonomous confidence threshold; anything touching a strategic account, a partner-managed campaign, or a title in soft launch.
mode_2_recommend.human_burden: approve/reject/modify; rejections are captured with a reason code and feed the learning loop as negative labels.

mode_3_autonomous.name: Autonomous
mode_3_autonomous.definition: Agent executes a pre-approved action type without human involvement, inside a granted (entity_scope, dollar_band, confidence_band, rate_limit) envelope, with mandatory pre-registered rollback triggers and an immutable audit record.
mode_3_autonomous.when_used: Only for action types on the autonomy matrix that have passed promotion gates (>=60 days shadow+recommend, >=30 executed analogues, precision >= threshold, zero Sev-1 incidents in 90 days).
output_artifacts: audit record with prior_state + rollback plan
mode_3_autonomous.human_burden: none at execution time; daily autonomous-action digest at 09:00 local; instant Slack notification for any action > 0.5% of S_daily; one-click undo for 72h.

mode_transitions.promotion: Observe -> Recommend requires 30 days shadow + finding precision >= 0.70. Recommend -> Autonomous requires 30 days recommend + >= 30 human decisions on that action type + approval rate >= 0.80 + realized-vs-predicted MAPE <= 0.35 + zero Sev-1.
mode_transitions.demotion_automatic: Any of: 3 consecutive auto-rollbacks on the same action type; realized impact sign opposite to prediction on >= 30% of last 20 actions; agent-caused Sev-1 or Sev-2; data source in its lineage degraded > 6h; weekly calibration Brier score > 0.25.
mode_transitions.demotion_effect: Agent drops one mode for a mandatory 14-day cooling period and re-enters the promotion gate; Warden posts an incident record; no manual override below VP Growth + Head of Data joint approval.

capability_summary: Cohort-grain economics for every acquisition slice down to (campaign x geo x creative x platform x day) with pLTV, ROAS curves and payback.
Sub-minute anomaly detection on ~7.2M metric-dimension series using a tiered ensemble (cheap screening -> expensive confirmation).
Automated multi-dimensional root cause: changepoint localization, dimension contribution attribution, upstream-variable correlation with lag, and causal-DAG-constrained hypothesis ranking.
Multi-agent investigation choreography: the orchestrator can dispatch 3-6 agents on a single incident and merge their findings into one causal narrative.
Guardrailed write access to Meta, Google, TikTok, Unity, AppLovin, Mintegral, Pangle, LevelPlay and Firebase Remote Config via a single idempotent Action Gateway.
Prediction registry + counterfactual measurement, so every recommendation is scored against what actually happened.
Natural-language interrogation of the whole semantic layer ('why did T1 US ad ARPDAU drop on Tuesday?') answered with grounded, cited numbers.
explicit_non_goals: MART does not replace the MMP as the attribution system of record - it reconciles and challenges it.
MART does not do creative production. It scores, clusters, fatigues and rotates creatives; generation is out of scope for v1 (a v3 optional module).
MART does not autonomously change app store pricing, IAP price points, or legal/compliance settings under any mode.
MART does not autonomously create new campaigns or new ad accounts in v1 (Recommend only) - only modifies existing entities.
MART does not autonomously act on any title in soft launch (T4 class) - Observe/Recommend only until 90 days post global launch.
MART is not a bidding algorithm competing with network optimizers - it operates at budget/target/allocation level, above the auction.

metric_dictionary.note: Canonical definitions. The semantic layer exposes exactly these; no dashboard or agent may compute a variant. Every metric declares grain, formula, source system of record, freshness tier, and the trap it avoids.

spend.formula: SUM(cost) from network cost API, currency-normalized to USD at the daily ECB fiducial rate stamped at ingest
spend.grain: report_date x campaign x adset x ad x geo x platform
spend.sor: network cost API (fallback: MMP cost aggregation)
spend.trap: Network cost is restated for up to 72h (invalid traffic credits, currency settlement). Store cost as a versioned fact with restatement_generation; never treat T-0 cost as final.

impressions.trap: Meta counts an impression on render; some SDK networks count on fill. Do not compare CPM across networks without a normalization note.

clicks.trap: Click definition varies (clicks vs link clicks vs taps). Store both raw and normalized 'billable_clicks'.

cpi.grain: cohort_date x campaign x geo x platform
cpi.trap: Spend is report-date grain, installs are install-date grain. They agree only when the attribution window is short and delivery is stable. Canonical CPI joins spend and installs on the SAME date and is labeled 'reported CPI'; 'cohort CPI' uses spend allocated to the install cohort by click-time and is the one used for ROAS.

ipm.usage: primary creative-efficiency metric; less noisy than CTR because it captures store-conversion quality

installs.trap: SKAdNetwork/AdAttributionKit installs on iOS are not user-level and arrive with 24-72h postback delay plus crowd anonymity thresholds. iOS installs = deterministic (Android/consented) + modeled (SKAN) and MUST be labeled with attribution_certainty.

retention_dN.formula: COUNT(DISTINCT user_id with >=1 session where floor(session_ts - install_ts in days) = N) / COUNT(cohort installs)
variant_supported: rolling (any session on or after day N)
retention_dN.maturity_rule: D_N is only reportable when now() >= cohort_install_ts + (N+1) days; before that it is NULL, never 0.

session_duration_median.formula: median(session_end - session_start) excluding sessions < 3s and > 4h (bot/leak filter)

dau.formula: COUNT(DISTINCT user_id with >=1 session in UTC day)

iap_revenue_gross.formula: SUM(purchase price in USD) from store receipts
iap_revenue_gross.trap: Never use client-reported price; always validated receipts. Refunds are negative facts posted on the refund date but attributed back to the original cohort.

iap_revenue_net.note: store_commission_rate is per-account and per-year (small business program, subscription year-2 rates); store it as a dimension, not a constant.

ad_revenue.formula: SUM(estimated_revenue) from mediation user-level ad revenue (ULAR) where available, else SUM(network reported revenue) allocated to users by impression share
ad_revenue.sor: AppLovin MAX / LevelPlay / CAS ULAR -> MMP ad_revenue events
ad_revenue.trap: ULAR is an estimate reconciled by the network T+1 to T+3. Store estimate and reconciled as separate columns with a variance monitor; agents use reconciled for financial decisions and estimate only for intraday detection.

arpdau.decomposition: arpdau = ad_arpdau + iap_arpdau ; ad_arpdau = impressions_per_dau * eCPM/1000 * fill_rate_effect ; iap_arpdau = payer_conversion * arppu_daily

arppu.formula: iap_revenue_net / COUNT(DISTINCT paying users in window)

ecpm.grain: day x network x geo x ad_format x placement

fill_rate.note: track show_rate = impressions / fills separately; a fill that never shows is a UX or integration bug, not a demand problem

impressions_per_dau.note: primary lever the product team controls; the single most common cause of ad ARPDAU movement

ltv_actual_dN.formula: cumulative total_revenue per install through day N / installs in cohort

roas_dN.note: always cohort-grain; equivalently cumulative cohort revenue / cohort spend

payback_days.formula: min N such that cumulative_net_revenue_per_install(N) >= cpi_cohort; when unreached within observed window, extrapolate with the fitted LTV curve and label 'projected'

churn_probability.formula: model output P(no session in next 14 days | features at t)
churn_probability.usage: aggregated to cohort as expected_churn_rate; individual scores drive remote-config/CRM segments, never UA decisions

attribution_discrepancy.acceptable_band: abs <= 0.10 for most networks; > 0.15 sustained 3 days is a finding

blended_cpi.warning: reported for finance only; never used for campaign decisions because it hides the organic uplift attribution problem

organic_uplift_factor.formula: organic_installs / paid_installs, modeled per title x geo via time-series regression with paid spend as regressor; used to adjust true effective CPI

emde_score.formula: Expected Marginal Dollar Efficiency = d(revenue_180)/d(spend) estimated per campaign from the fitted spend-response curve; the core allocation metric used by Ledger and the orchestrator

6_month: Median time-to-detection of a material cohort regression < 6 hours (from 4.5 days).
>= 60% of UA budget decisions originate as MART recommendations.
Zero Sev-1 incidents caused by an autonomous action.
12_month: Portfolio D30 ROAS +8% vs pre-MART trailing baseline, measured via a geo-holdout where a 10% spend slice is managed manually.
Wasted spend (spend on cohorts that finish below 0.6x target D30 ROAS) reduced 35%.
>= 40% of eligible action volume executing in Mode 3 with < 5% rollback rate.
Analyst hours on manual reporting reduced 60%, redeployed to experimentation.
platform_success_criteria.measurement_method: Persistent 10% managed-manually holdout at (title x geo) level, refreshed quarterly, plus a switchback design on action-eligible campaign sets for the subset of actions where a holdout is impractical.

dashboard_layout.design_philosophy: Three-layer information architecture: (L0) Decision Surface - what needs a human right now; (L1) Module Cockpits - operational depth per function; (L2) Explorer - arbitrary slicing and SQL. A user should never need L2 to answer a question that L0/L1 should have answered. Every number on every screen is click-through-able to the exact rows that produced it (lineage-backed drill).

elements.behavior: multi-select; 'Portfolio' aggregates with correct weighted math (ratios recomputed from numerators/denominators, never averaged)
Global and sticky. Switching re-renders every metric with the correct definition and shows a persistent banner explaining which grain is active. Mixing is impossible by construction.

options: Net of store + network rev-share + tax

elements.behavior: Changes ROAS/LTV denominators across the app; annotates every affected tile with the active model.
Click opens the data_quality_observability module filtered to breaching datasets. When red, all Mode 3 action badges show 'paused'.
Live count of agents running / findings in last hour / pending approvals. Click opens the Agent Ops console.
Natural-language query bar (cmd-K). Answers grounded in the semantic layer with citations to the exact query and row count; can render an ad-hoc chart and pin it.

left_nav.personalization: Nav order and default landing module are set per role (personas map in system_overview.primary_personas); users may pin up to 5 modules.

right_rail_agent_panel.content: Context-aware agent feed: findings scoped to whatever the user is currently looking at (title, date range, dimension filters). Each card shows severity, confidence, dollar impact, the one-line cause, and action buttons (Approve / Reject / Snooze / Investigate deeper / Ask why).
right_rail_agent_panel.interaction: 'Investigate deeper' spawns an orchestrator-coordinated multi-agent investigation and streams progress into the panel; 'Ask why' opens a threaded chat grounded in that finding's evidence bundle.

l0_command_center.purpose: The 90-second answer to 'is the business OK, what broke, what did the system do, what needs me'.
l0_command_center.layout: Four horizontal bands, mobile-responsive to a single column.

bands.content: 8 live tiles: Spend today (vs pace), Installs today, Blended CPI, Revenue today, ARPDAU, D7 ROAS of the maturing cohort, Forecast-to-month-end vs budget, Contribution margin MTD.
bands.tile_anatomy: Big number + sparkline (48h for realtime, 30d for cohort) + delta vs comparison + significance marker (a delta inside the metric's historical noise band is rendered grey, not green/red) + freshness dot.
bands.refresh: realtime tiles 60s push via SSE; cohort tiles on materialization (every 15 min)

bands.content: Ranked list of at most 7 items, sorted by decision_engine priority_score. Item types: pending approval, unacknowledged Sev-1/2 incident, guardrail breach, forecast breach, expiring recommendation.
bands.item_anatomy: [severity chip][module icon] Headline (<=90 chars) | $impact_30d | confidence % | age | primary CTA
bands.rule: If the list would exceed 7 items, the orchestrator collapses correlated items into a single parent incident. Never paginate this list - unranked overflow lives in Incidents.

bands.content: Chronological feed of autonomous actions in the last 24h: entity, change, why (one line), predicted effect, current measured effect, rollback status, one-click undo.
bands.rule: Every Mode 3 action appears here within 30 seconds of execution. Actions above 0.5% of S_daily also push to Slack.

bands.content: Two charts: (a) 90-day actual + 30-day forecast of spend, revenue and contribution margin with 80% prediction bands and plan overlay; (b) cohort ROAS maturation curves for the last 8 weekly cohorts vs target corridor, so a cohort degrading in-flight is visible before it matures.

l0_command_center.mobile_variant: Bands 1 and 2 only, plus push notifications for Sev-1 and for approvals with SLA < 2h. Approve/reject is available on mobile for actions below 0.25% of S_daily; above that requires desktop with a typed confirmation.

l0_approvals_queue.purpose: Single funnel for every Mode 2 proposal in the system.
l0_approvals_queue.row_expansion: Shows the full explanation artifact: evidence table, the counterfactual ('if we do nothing, expected -$X by day 30'), the dry-run diff of exactly what API calls will be made, the rollback plan, and the agent's historical precision on this action type.
l0_approvals_queue.bulk_operations: Group-approve is allowed only within a single action type and only when every item is below the role's per-item cap; the system computes and shows the aggregate blast radius before confirming.

sla.on_breach: escalate per governance.escalation_matrix; proposal expires and is re-evaluated rather than executed stale

l0_approvals_queue.reject_flow: Rejection requires a reason code (Wrong data / Wrong cause / Right cause wrong action / Timing / Business context the system lacks / Too risky). These become labeled training signal in the learning loop and are shown on the agent's scorecard.

l0_incidents.purpose: Incident-centric view where correlated findings across modules are merged into one investigation with a timeline.
views: Timeline (all events, agent messages, human comments, actions, in one stream)
Causal graph (interactive DAG of the hypothesized cause chain with per-edge confidence)
l0_incidents.post_incident: Auto-generated post-mortem at resolution: detection latency, whether prediction matched outcome, what the system missed, proposed detector/threshold change (which becomes a PR-style suggestion for the Data/Agent team).

l1_module_cockpit_template.note: Every module cockpit follows the same 9-zone template so a user learns one layout and knows them all. modules_data defines the content of each zone per module.

zones.content: primary_realtime_kpis rendered as tiles with delta + noise-band significance + freshness
the module's agent findings, ranked, with actions
the module's core metric(s) with comparison overlay, forecast band, annotation markers (releases, experiments, network changes, actions taken, holidays)

pivotable table across the module's required dimensions with conditional formatting, contribution-to-change column, and per-row sparkline; contribution column answers 'which rows caused the aggregate move'
module-specific: waterfall of metric change decomposition, treemap of spend/revenue share, histogram of the unit-level distribution
maturation curves (retention, ROAS, LTV) for the selected slices vs benchmark corridor
model forecast with prediction interval, backtest accuracy badge (MAPE over last 30d), scenario controls where applicable
the active alert rules affecting this module, current state, mute controls, threshold editor (with a preview of how many alerts the new threshold would have fired historically)
recommended actions for this module, autonomy status per action type, recent action log with measured outcomes

universal_interactions.drill_path: Any tile -> dimension breakdown -> entity detail -> user/event sample -> raw row + query (with a copy-as-SQL button). Maximum 4 clicks from any KPI to the raw rows behind it.
universal_interactions.cross_filter: Selecting a row anywhere applies a global filter chip; chips are shareable via URL (deep-link state includes filters, date range, grain, attribution model, comparison mode).
universal_interactions.annotations: Any user can annotate any point on any chart; annotations are global objects and appear on every chart covering that timestamp for that entity. Agents also write annotations (release detected, network policy change, action executed).
universal_interactions.explain_this: Right-click any datapoint -> 'Explain this move' triggers an on-demand RCA run scoped exactly to that metric/dimension/time window, returning within ~40s.
universal_interactions.export: Every table exports to CSV/Sheets with its exact query, and can be scheduled as a recurring email/Slack digest.

l1_module_cockpit_template.significance_rendering_rule: A delta is colored only if |delta| exceeds the metric's rolling 28-day MAD-based noise band (k=2.5) AND the denominator exceeds the metric's min_denominator_for_display. Otherwise it renders grey with a tooltip 'within normal variation'. This single rule kills most dashboard-induced false alarms.

components.capability: Build any cohort from the full dimension set, pick any measure set, pick maturity horizon, compare up to 8 cohorts side by side, save as a named cohort object usable by agents and alerts.
Drag-and-drop over the semantic layer with governed metrics only; no raw SQL required, no metric redefinition possible.
Read-only warehouse access with query cost guardrails, saved queries promotable into governed metrics via a review workflow.
One-click export of the current filter state into a Python notebook with the data pre-loaded via the feature store client.

alerting_surfaces.in_app: Right rail + Command Center band 2 + module Z2/Z8

slack.format: Block Kit card with headline, $impact, confidence, cause, primary CTA deep-link, and Approve/Reject buttons for eligible action types

alerting_surfaces.email: Daily 09:00 local executive digest; weekly Monday portfolio review pack; instant for Sev-1 only
alerting_surfaces.pagerduty: Sev-1 only: revenue-impacting incidents > 1.5% of S_daily/day, action-gateway failures, agent-caused rollback storms
alerting_surfaces.mobile_push: Sev-1 + approvals expiring in < 2h + any autonomous action > 0.5% of S_daily
anti_fatigue: Correlated findings are merged by the orchestrator before routing
Per-channel rate limit: max 6 non-Sev-1 messages/hour, overflow batched into a digest
Repeat suppression: identical finding fingerprint within its cooldown is appended to the existing thread, never re-sent
Every alert carries a 'this was not useful' button that decrements that detector's routing weight

realtime_vs_batch_contract.rule: Each tile renders its tier badge. A user must never have to guess whether a number is live or from last night.

accessibility_and_performance.a11y: WCAG 2.2 AA: all state encoded with shape/text in addition to color; colorblind-safe categorical palette; full keyboard navigation; screen-reader summaries auto-generated for every chart from its underlying series.
accessibility_and_performance.performance_budget: p95 < 1.5s realtime tiles, < 4s cohort matrices, < 250ms filter application on already-loaded data (client-side WASM/Arrow slicing), < 100KB JSON per tile via pre-aggregated ClickHouse projections.

cmo_executive_intelligence.primary_purpose: Give portfolio leadership a single defensible view of marketing-driven P&L: where money went, what it bought, what it will be worth, what is off-plan, and what the system is doing about it. Optimizes for decision speed at low information density, not for analytical depth.

realtime_kpis.definition: iap_revenue_net + ad_revenue_net running total UTC day
D7 ROAS of the cohort that turned 7 days old today, portfolio-weighted

realtime_kpis.kpi: Open Sev-1/Sev-2 incidents and $ at risk

secondary_kpis: Payback days (trailing 30d cohorts, projected)
Spend share by title / network / geo tier
Organic share of installs
Marketing efficiency ratio (net revenue / UA spend, trailing 90d cohort-matched)
% spend on cohorts currently tracking below target ROAS corridor
Headroom: incremental spend available at >= target marginal ROAS (from Ledger's spend-response curves)
Autonomous action count + net measured $ effect (last 30d)
Forecast accuracy badge (last 30d MAPE on revenue and spend)

visualizations.spec: Gross revenue -> store commission -> net revenue -> ad network rev-share -> UA spend -> variable infra -> contribution margin. Month-over-month with delta bridge showing which component moved.
90d actual + 30d forecast, dual axis, plan overlay dashed, 80% prediction band shaded, annotation pins for releases and major actions.
Weekly cohorts as maturation lines vs a target corridor (P25-P75 of historical winning cohorts); a cohort exiting the corridor downward turns red at the exact day it exits.
Area = spend, color = projected D180 ROAS vs target (diverging scale), label shows margin $.

Root cause is demand-side, not our integration (our bid request volume and signal completeness are unchanged). Recommend raising the floor tier for backfill instances and opening a partner ticket. rolling 14d MAPE at D30 > 0.30 OR systematic bias > +/-12% for 7 consecutive days OR PSI on the feature distribution > 0.25
alerts.action: Oracle downgrades all pLTV-dependent agents to Recommend until retrained/recalibrated - this is a system-wide safety interlock

alerts.condition: actual CPI > allowable CPI by > 15% for a slice spending > 0.3% of S_daily for 3 days
IAP/ad revenue split changes > 10pp for a cohort vs its slice baseline
alerts.meaning: changes payback timing even if total LTV is unchanged - the cash curve must be re-forecast

alerts.condition: refund rate > 2x 28d baseline with n >= 100

drill_downs: Portfolio ROAS -> title -> source -> campaign -> geo -> cohort day -> the individual revenue events (validated receipts / ad revenue rows)
pLTV prediction -> SHAP feature attribution for that cohort -> the feature values -> their source tables
Payback -> revenue schedule by day -> IAP vs ad split -> the specific payers driving it (whale concentration check)
historical_comparisons: Cohort vs the previous 8 weekly cohorts at the same age (the only valid retrospective comparison)
vs slice historical best/median
vs plan LTV assumptions used in the budget
Model version A vs B on the same cohorts
forecasts: pLTV D180/D365 per cohort with intervals
Portfolio revenue forecast from existing cohorts (locked-in revenue) plus planned acquisition
Payback and cash recovery schedule 12 months forward
Scenario: what LTV would need to be for a proposed CPI to hit target payback
agent_generated_insights_examples: T1 Google iOS US cohorts from 2026-08-18 onward are tracking 22% below their own D7 predictions (predicted 0.41, actual 0.32). Decomposition: ad revenue per install is on-model; IAP revenue per install is 46% below. The first-purchase conversion rate for these cohorts fell from 2.1% to 1.2% while retention held, which points at the paywall, not at traffic quality. Merchant confirms a starter-pack offer expired 2026-08-17 and was not replaced. Estimated impact $47k over 30 days. Recommend restoring the offer (Product action) rather than cutting spend. Confidence 0.85.

pLTV D30 bias for Mintegral Android T3-geo cohorts is +19% (over-predicting) for 9 consecutive days, driven by a feature-distribution shift in ad_impressions_d0. Downgrading all Mintegral-scope autonomous scaling to Recommend and scheduling a retrain with the corrected ULAR reconciliation factor.
recommended_actions: Update allowable CPI / target ROAS per slice (propagates to bid targets - requires Finance approval above a 10% change)
Cut or scale spend on cohort-economics grounds (executed via Hunter/Ledger)
Change the payback horizon policy for a title (Finance approval)
Trigger a pLTV retrain or apply a temporary correction factor
Escalate a product/monetization cause instead of an acquisition action (prevents cutting good traffic for a product problem)

creative_intelligence.primary_purpose: Treat creative as an asset portfolio: measure per-creative efficiency and downstream cohort quality, detect fatigue before CPI degrades, cluster creatives into concepts to learn what actually works, and drive the rotation/production pipeline.

realtime_kpis.kpi: Top creatives by spend today with IPM and CTR
Creative concentration (share of spend on top 5 creatives)
New creatives in testing and their days-to-decision

secondary_kpis: IPM, CTR, CVR (click->install), CPI, CPM per creative
Downstream quality: D1/D7 retention and predicted D30 ROAS of the cohort each creative acquired
Creative fatigue index
Frequency and reach (where available)
Video engagement curve (25/50/75/100% completion, average watch time)
Hook retention (first 3s drop-off)
Time-to-fatigue distribution by concept
Win rate of new creatives vs incumbents
Concept-level aggregates (art style, mechanic shown, character, hook type, language, aspect ratio, duration, UGC vs studio, playable vs video)
Creative production ROI (cost per creative vs incremental margin generated)
dimensions: creative_attributes (auto-extracted: hook_type, first_frame_subject, has_face, has_text_overlay, pacing, duration_bucket, orientation, language, cta_style, gameplay_authenticity)

visualizations.spec: Card per creative: thumbnail/video preview, spend, IPM, CPI, D7 ROAS of its cohort, fatigue gauge, days live, and a status chip (Testing / Scaling / Stable / Fatiguing / Retire). Sortable by any metric, filterable by attribute.

Per creative: IPM and CTR vs cumulative impressions (not calendar days - impressions are the true exposure clock), with the fitted decay curve, the current position, and the projected date at which IPM crosses the retirement threshold.
Produced -> Tested -> Passed test -> Scaled -> Fatigued -> Retired, with conversion rates and median durations per stage; exposes whether the bottleneck is production volume or test throughput.

Attribute combinations x performance, with statistical significance and sample sizes; drives the production brief ('vertical UGC hooks with a face in frame 1 outperform studio renders by 34% IPM in T2 geos').
x = IPM, y = predicted D30 ROAS of the acquired cohort, size = spend. The bottom-right quadrant (high IPM, low ROAS) is the misleading-creative trap and is highlighted explicitly.
Completion rate by quartile vs concept benchmark - a 3s hook problem looks completely different from a payoff problem.
Bayesian A/B on IPM and on downstream ROAS with probability-to-beat-incumbent and expected loss.

creative_fatigue_index.formula: CFI = 0.40 * IPM_decay + 0.25 * CTR_decay + 0.20 * CPI_inflation + 0.15 * frequency_pressure, where IPM_decay = max(0, 1 - IPM_7d/IPM_peak_7d_window), CTR_decay likewise, CPI_inflation = max(0, CPI_7d/CPI_best_7d - 1) capped at 1, frequency_pressure = min(1, frequency_7d / frequency_saturation_threshold)
creative_fatigue_index.requirements: creative must have >= 150k cumulative impressions and >= 7 days live; below that, variance dominates and CFI is not computed
creative_fatigue_index.confounder_control: CFI is computed within (network x geo x placement) and compared against the concurrent performance of other creatives in the same cells, so a market-wide CPM spike is not misread as fatigue

derived_metrics.creative_quality_score: CQS = z(IPM) * 0.35 + z(predicted_D30_ROAS_of_cohort) * 0.45 + z(D7_retention_of_cohort) * 0.20, computed within (geo_tier x platform x network) peer groups

alerts.condition: CFI >= 0.40 for 2 consecutive days on a creative with >= 0.1% of S_daily spend
alerts.action: queue replacement

alerts.condition: CFI >= 0.55 OR IPM down > 35% from peak with impressions >= 150k
alerts.action: auto-rotate if a qualified replacement exists and the autonomy grant covers it

alerts.condition: creative in the top IPM quartile but its cohort's D7 retention is in the bottom quartile of its peer group, n >= 500 installs
alerts.note: high-IPM low-quality creatives are the most expensive failure mode in UA - they scale fast and poison cohorts

alerts.condition: top 3 creatives carry > 55% of a title's spend AND at least one has CFI > 0.35
count of creatives passing test in the last 14 days < the number projected to be retired in the next 14 days
>= 3 creatives rejected by the same network in 24h
alerts.meaning: usually a policy change, not three independent mistakes

alerts.condition: test creative shows P(IPM > incumbent) > 0.90 with >= 30k impressions and its early cohort quality is not below peer P25
alerts.action: propose scaling

drill_downs: Creative -> the campaigns/adsets running it -> their cohorts -> retention and ROAS -> the specific users
Creative -> attribute tags -> sibling creatives with the same attributes -> concept-level performance
Fatigue -> the impression/frequency history that produced it -> the audience saturation estimate
Video creative -> per-second engagement curve -> the frame where drop-off spikes
historical_comparisons: vs the creative's own first 7 days (the fatigue baseline)
vs concurrent creatives in the same cells
vs the concept's historical median lifecycle
vs the same creative in other geos (a creative can be fatigued in the US and fresh in BR)
Seasonal analogues (last year's Q4 creatives)
forecasts: Days-to-retirement per creative from the fitted decay curve
Required creative production volume for the next 30/60/90 days to sustain planned spend (given observed fatigue rates)
Expected IPM of a proposed new creative from its attribute vector (an attribute-based prior, used to prioritize production, explicitly labeled as a weak prior with wide intervals)
agent_generated_insights_examples: Creative cr_88431 ('UGC hook - failed level frustration') hit CFI 0.58 on Meta US iOS: IPM fell 14.2 -> 8.9 over 11 days at 2.1M cumulative impressions, while concurrent creatives in the same cells fell only 6%, so this is creative-specific fatigue, not market CPM inflation. It carries 31% of the campaign's spend. Two qualified replacements exist (same concept cluster, tested IPM 13.8 and 12.9). Recommend rotating 60% of its budget to them over 48h. Doing nothing costs an estimated $8.9k over 14 days in CPI inflation. Confidence 0.84.

Attribute analysis across 412 creatives, last 90 days: creatives whose first frame shows real gameplay have 28% lower IPM but 41% higher D7 retention and 0.14 higher D30 ROAS than stylized-render hooks. Net margin per dollar is 19% better despite worse acquisition metrics. Recommend shifting the production brief and re-weighting the creative test scorecard toward downstream ROAS.
recommended_actions: Pause a fatigued creative and shift its budget to qualified replacements (autonomous within bounds)
Promote a test winner to scale
Kill a misleading creative immediately (high-IPM/low-quality)
Generate a production brief with the winning attribute combination and expected value
Localize/re-cut a winning creative for a new geo
Request a policy-compliant re-edit after a rejection cluster
Re-balance creative test budget allocation across concepts

attribution_measurement.primary_purpose: Guarantee that the numbers every other module and agent depends on are trustworthy: reconcile MMP vs network vs store vs internal counts, quantify and explain discrepancies, manage SKAdNetwork/AdAttributionKit modeling, maintain incrementality multipliers, and expose the uncertainty explicitly instead of hiding it.

realtime_kpis.kpi: MMP vs network install discrepancy % by network
SKAN postback coverage (postbacks received / iOS installs claimed)
Attribution certainty mix (deterministic / probabilistic / SKAN-modeled / organic)

secondary_kpis: Discrepancy % by network x geo x platform
Click-to-install time distribution (CTIT) and its anomalies
Re-attribution and re-engagement counts
Fraud indicators: CTIT outliers, click flooding rate, device-farm clustering score, install hijack indicators, blocked install counts by rule
SKAN conversion-value schema coverage and null-CV rate
SKAN crowd-anonymity tier distribution (how much fidelity we actually get)
Null/low-fidelity postback share
Organic uplift factor by title x geo
Incrementality multiplier per channel (incremental installs / attributed installs)
Store-reported vs MMP-reported install variance
ATT opt-in rate by geo/platform

visualizations.spec: Rows = networks, columns = [network self-reported installs, MMP attributed, store first-opens, internal SDK first-sessions], with pairwise variance % and a color scale against acceptable bands. One screen tells you which of four systems is lying.
Histogram of click-to-install time per network with the healthy reference; a spike at <10s indicates click injection, a flat long tail indicates click flooding.
iOS installs -> postbacks received -> non-null conversion values -> tier-1 (fine-grained) values, per network/geo; quantifies exactly how blind we are.

Same period, same spend, install/revenue credit by channel under last-touch, SKAN-modeled, MMM, and incrementality-adjusted, side by side, with the resulting ROAS per channel. Makes over/under-crediting visible and is the input to the multiplier policy.
Per network/publisher(sub-site): anomaly scores for CTIT, conversion rate outliers, new-device ratio, IP entropy, sensor-data plausibility, with a blocklist action button.
Per network over 90 days with annotation markers for SDK updates, MMP config changes, network policy changes and attribution-window changes.

alerts.condition: |MMP - network| / network > 0.15 for a network with >= 3% install share, sustained 3 days
alerts.investigation: auto-checks in order: attribution window mismatch, SDK version change, deduplication rule change, network-side click-time vs impression-time attribution, timezone misalignment, fraud rejection

alerts.condition: postback coverage drops > 20% vs 14d baseline
alerts.meaning: iOS measurement is failing; all iOS-dependent autonomous actions are suspended by the Warden until resolved

alerts.condition: publisher/sub-site with CTIT anomaly z > 4 OR new-device-ratio > 0.9 with volume > 500 installs/day
alerts.action: auto-blocklist the sub-publisher where the network supports it, and file a claw-back claim packet

alerts.condition: deterministic share of installs drops > 10pp week over week
alerts.impact: widens all downstream confidence intervals; Oracle inflates pLTV prediction intervals accordingly

alerts.condition: organic installs fall > 15% while paid installs rise > 25% in the same geo/title, with the ratio change outside the modeled uplift band
alerts.meaning: paid is buying users who would have come organically; true incremental CPI is much higher than reported

alerts.condition: SAN-claimed installs exceed MMP-attributed by > 20% (double counting across Meta/Google/TikTok claims)

drill_downs: Discrepancy -> per campaign -> per day -> per hour -> raw postback/callback records with timestamps
SKAN -> per conversion-value bucket -> the mapped in-app behavior -> the revenue it implies
Fraud -> sub-publisher -> device/IP clusters -> the specific install records
historical_comparisons: vs 90d discrepancy baseline per network
pre/post SDK version
pre/post iOS release (each iOS release changes attribution behavior)
vs the same period in the previous quarter for seasonality in fraud pressure
forecasts: Expected discrepancy band per network (so a breach is judged against a forecast, not a fixed constant)
SKAN fidelity projection as iOS version mix shifts
Expected organic uplift for a planned spend increase
agent_generated_insights_examples: Mintegral T3 Android discrepancy widened from 6% to 21% over 5 days. CTIT distribution developed a 34% mass below 8 seconds (baseline 4%), concentrated in 3 sub-publishers (ids 4471, 8820, 8823) representing 61% of that spend. This is click injection. Recommend blocklisting those sub-publishers (autonomous - covered by the fraud grant), claiming back an estimated $22.4k, and reducing the campaign budget by the corresponding install volume so pacing does not overcompensate. Confidence 0.91.

Meta iOS SKAN-modeled installs are 31% of T1 iOS volume but produce 18% of measured D7 revenue at matched conversion values. Rather than treating the gap as low quality, the evidence points to conversion-value truncation from crowd-anonymity tier downgrades in low-volume geos. Recommend a CV schema change (coarse-value revenue buckets) and, until then, applying a 1.14 revenue correction factor to SKAN cohorts in pLTV - flagged for Head of Data approval because it changes reported ROAS.
recommended_actions: Blocklist a fraudulent sub-publisher/site id (autonomous within the fraud grant)
File a claw-back claim with the network including the evidence bundle
Change SKAN conversion-value schema (Recommend only - it resets measurement continuity)
Adjust attribution windows or dedup rules (Recommend only, Head of Data approval)
Apply/update an incrementality multiplier per channel (Head of Data approval)
Suspend autonomy for a channel whose measurement is unreliable
Launch an incrementality test to resolve a persistent discrepancy

forecasting_budget_planning.primary_purpose: Turn budget into a continuously re-optimized plan: forecast spend, installs, revenue and margin at multiple horizons, allocate budget across titles/networks/geos at the point of equal marginal return, and detect pacing risk early enough to fix it inside the period.

realtime_kpis.kpi: MTD spend vs plan and projected month-end

realtime_kpis.definition: actual_pace / required_pace to hit the envelope
sum of budget that will be unspent or overspent at current trajectory
portfolio marginal-ROAS dispersion; a healthy allocation has near-equal marginal ROAS everywhere. Dispersion = coefficient of variation of EMDE across campaigns with > 0.1% S_daily.

secondary_kpis: Forecast accuracy (MAPE) at 7/14/30-day horizons per metric and segment
Forecast interval coverage (are the 80% bands actually 80%?)
Spend-response curve parameters and saturation points per campaign/channel
Reallocation opportunity value (USD/day recoverable by equalizing marginal ROAS)
Seasonality indices (weekday, month-phase, holiday)
CPM inflation forecast by geo
Committed vs discretionary budget split
Scenario deltas

visualizations.spec: MTD cumulative spend vs the required pacing line and the projected trajectory with a confidence cone; a divergence cone that misses the envelope is the alert trigger.

Interactive: current allocation vs optimizer-proposed allocation across campaigns/channels, showing marginal ROAS before/after, expected margin gain, and the constraint set (min/max per channel, learning-phase protection, contractual minimums). Users can pin constraints and re-solve.
Per channel: fitted response with the current operating point, saturation knee, and the shaded region where marginal ROAS > target (the headroom).
Spend/installs/revenue/margin with 50/80/95% bands, actuals overlaid, plan line, and a backtest accuracy badge.
Up to 4 scenarios (e.g. +20% T1, -10% T2, shift 15% Meta->TikTok) with projected installs, revenue, margin, payback and risk, plus the assumptions that drive each.
STL decomposition of spend efficiency into trend/weekly/annual/holiday components, used to set expectations rather than react to normal seasonality.

alerts.condition: projected month-end spend outside +/-8% of the envelope, with >= 5 days remaining
alerts.action: propose a pacing plan (daily budget deltas across campaigns) sized to close the gap

alerts.condition: projected underspend > 5% of envelope AND >= $X/day of headroom exists at marginal ROAS >= target
alerts.meaning: leaving profitable volume on the table - as costly as overspending

alerts.condition: marginal-ROAS coefficient of variation > 0.35 across campaigns holding > 60% of spend
actual outside the 95% band for 2 consecutive days
alerts.action: auto-diagnose whether it is a model failure (retrain) or a genuine business change (investigate) by testing whether the residual is systematic across segments or isolated

alerts.condition: rolling 14d MAPE > 1.5x the model's validation MAPE
alerts.action: retrain, and widen intervals until accuracy is restored

alerts.condition: a known seasonal CPM event (Black Friday, Q4, Ramadan, Golden Week) is < 14 days away and no budget adjustment is planned

drill_downs: Portfolio forecast -> segment forecasts -> the model's feature contributions -> the underlying series
Pacing gap -> which campaigns are under/over -> their delivery constraints (budget-capped vs bid-capped vs audience-limited)
Allocation proposal -> per-campaign delta -> the spend-response curve that justifies it -> the historical scaling analogues
historical_comparisons: Forecast vs actual for every past forecast (a persistent, auditable forecast registry)
Same month last year, seasonally aligned
Plan vs actual by budget version (so re-plans are visible, not silently overwritten)
forecasts: Spend, installs, revenue, margin at 7/14/30/90 days with intervals, hierarchical and reconciled (portfolio = sum of titles = sum of campaigns via MinT reconciliation)
CPM/CPI inflation by geo
DAU/MAU projection from cohort retention curves plus planned installs
Cash flow from cohort payback schedules
agent_generated_insights_examples: Portfolio is pacing to $7.14M vs a $7.50M envelope (-4.8%) with 9 days remaining. The gap is concentrated in Meta T1 (delivery is bid-capped, not budget-capped: budget utilization 71% at a $1.90 target CPA). Two options: (a) raise the target CPA to $2.15 on 4 adsets, projected +$210k spend at marginal D180 ROAS 1.19 (above the 1.25 target? no - below, so margin-dilutive); (b) move $180k to Google AC iOS which still has headroom at marginal ROAS 1.34. Recommend (b): +$41k projected margin vs (a)'s +$12k. Confidence 0.76.

Allocation dispersion is 0.44 - $23k/day is recoverable by moving spend from the 12 lowest-marginal-ROAS campaigns to the 7 highest, subject to the 25%/day change guardrail. Proposed as a 5-day staged reallocation package with checkpoints.
recommended_actions: Execute a staged budget reallocation package (autonomous per-step within guardrails, package-level approval for the whole)
Adjust daily budget envelope for a title (Finance approval)
Pre-position budget for a forecasted seasonal event
Raise/lower bid targets to unlock capped delivery (routes to UA)
Freeze discretionary spend when a margin breach is forecast
Trigger a forecast model retrain

anomaly_detection.primary_purpose: Be the always-on statistical nervous system: watch every material metric-dimension series, distinguish real change from noise and from known seasonality, localize the change in time and dimension space, and hand a well-formed, deduplicated, pre-localized incident to the right domain agent. This module deliberately does not diagnose causes - it detects and localizes, then delegates.
secondary_kpis: Recall proxy (share of post-hoc-identified incidents that were detected proactively)
False positive rate by detector and by metric family
Alert volume per hour (with the anti-fatigue budget)
Suppression hit rate (known-event suppression working)
Detector agreement rate (ensemble consensus)
Mean time to acknowledge / to resolve
Cost per detection pass

monitored_scope.series_count_estimate: ~7.2M metric x dimension combinations; tiered so cost stays bounded

tiering.criteria: metrics with direct revenue/spend impact on entities carrying >= 0.5% of S_daily, plus all portfolio-level KPIs
entities carrying 0.05-0.5% of S_daily, all title x geo x network aggregates
the long tail; screened with a cheap detector, escalated to the full ensemble only on a hit

detector_ensemble.weaknesses: blind to trend and multi-day drift

detector_ensemble.use: series with weekly/annual seasonality (nearly all marketing series)
detector_ensemble.params: STL with weekly + annual components; EWMA control chart on residuals, lambda 0.3, L = 3
detector_ensemble.strengths: does not fire on normal Sunday CPM drops

detector_ensemble.use: identifying WHEN a regime changed, not just that today is odd
detector_ensemble.params: hazard 1/168 hourly; report changepoint posterior mode + 90% credible interval
detector_ensemble.value: gives root cause analysis an exact change window to align against deploy/config/network events

detector_ensemble.use: slow drift that never trips a z-threshold (creative fatigue, gradual eCPM erosion)
metrics with strong calendar effects and known regressors (spend as a regressor for installs)
detector_ensemble.params: breach = actual outside 95% PI for 2 consecutive periods

detector_ensemble.use: catching combinations that are individually normal but jointly impossible (CPI normal, CTR normal, but CTR/CVR ratio impossible)
detector_ensemble.params: feature vector of 12 core rate metrics per entity; contamination 0.005

detector_ensemble.use: structural impossibilities: installs > clicks, revenue with zero impressions, fill > requests, D7 > D1 retention
detector_ensemble.params: hard rules; always Sev-2 minimum because they indicate data corruption

detector_ensemble.use: distinguishing entity-specific from market-wide change: compare an entity's delta to the concurrent delta of its peer group (same network x geo x format)
detector_ensemble.params: flag when entity delta - peer median delta > 2.5 * peer MAD
detector_ensemble.value: single most important false-positive killer; a market-wide CPM spike no longer generates 400 campaign alerts

visualizations.spec: Live ranked feed with severity, metric, entity, deviation size, dollar impact estimate, detector consensus count, and status.
The series with the model's expected band, the detected changepoint marked with its credible interval, peer-group overlay, and event annotations (deploys, config changes, network events, actions).
Output of the contribution-attribution pass: a ranked list/treemap of which dimension values carry the aggregate change, with each value's contribution % and surprise score.

Per detector: fire count, precision, mean impact of true positives, and the threshold-tuning simulator ('this threshold would have fired N times in the last 90d, catching M of the K known incidents').

alerts.condition: ensemble consensus >= 2 detectors OR any invariant violation OR a single detector at extreme severity (|z| > 5) - and the entity passes the materiality gate (impact estimate >= 0.05% of S_daily/day or the entity is portfolio-level)
>= 5 correlated anomalies within 30 minutes sharing a dimension value
alerts.severity: escalates to a single Sev-1/2 incident, not 5 alerts
alerts.handling: the orchestrator opens one incident and dispatches a multi-agent investigation

alerts.condition: a post-hoc-identified incident was not detected proactively
alerts.action: auto-generates a detector-tuning proposal and a regression test case

noise_control: Materiality gate before any emission (dollar impact and minimum denominators).

Known-event suppression calendar: releases, staged rollouts, experiment starts, network maintenance, public holidays per geo, marketing pushes, store featuring - suppresses the expected direction and magnitude only, not the metric entirely.
Deduplication by fingerprint (metric + entity + dimension set + changepoint window) with a per-fingerprint cooldown.
Hierarchical rollup: if a parent and its children all fire, only the highest node that fully explains the change is emitted, with children attached as evidence.
Adaptive thresholds per series learned from its own historical volatility rather than global constants.
drill_downs: Anomaly -> series -> raw rows -> upstream pipeline run -> source payload
Anomaly -> localization -> the specific dimension slice -> that slice's module cockpit with filters applied
Anomaly -> correlated anomalies -> the incident graph
historical_comparisons: The series' own history and seasonal analogues
Peer entities
The same metric during previous similar incidents (case-based retrieval from agent memory)
forecasts: Expected band for every monitored series (the detection baseline itself)
Projected impact if the anomaly persists for 7/14/30 days - this number is what drives prioritization
agent_generated_insights_examples: KPI_ANOMALY: T1 ad_arpdau, changepoint 2026-08-26 13:00-14:00 UTC (BOCPD posterior 0.94). Deviation -8.7% vs weekday-matched expectation, 4 of 7 detectors agree. Localization: 82% of the aggregate change is carried by geo=US (contribution 0.61) and geo=CA (0.21) at format=rewarded; other geos and formats are within band. Peer check: other titles in the same geos are unaffected, so this is title-specific. Projected 30-day impact -$186k. Routing to Vault (monetization) with Prism and Pulse on standby.

Invariant violation: T3 fill_rate = 1.14 for network=X geo=ID for 3 hours. Impressions exceed requests, which is structurally impossible - this is a reporting or SDK-integration defect, not a performance change. Sev-2 to data engineering; all downstream monetization metrics for that slice are quarantined from agent decisions until resolved.
recommended_actions: Emit a localized KPI_ANOMALY to the owning domain agent
Open an incident and request an orchestrated multi-agent investigation
Quarantine a data slice from agent decision-making (invariant violations)
Suppress an expected anomaly given a known calendar event
Propose a detector/threshold change with a historical simulation attached

mobile_user_cohort_intelligence.primary_purpose: The cohort microscope: build, compare and interrogate cohorts across the full acquisition and behavioral dimension space, expose the full economic and behavioral profile of any slice, and serve as the shared factual ground that UA, product, monetization and finance all argue from.
primary_users: Every agent (as a service via the cohort API)

realtime_kpis.kpi: Today's cohort size and activation rate
Cohort quality index of today's installs vs 28d baseline
realtime_kpis.definition: composite z-score of early behavioral predictors available at D0 (session count, session duration, core-loop completions, D0 ad impressions, D0 revenue)
realtime_kpis.value: gives a same-day quality read before any retention data exists

realtime_kpis.kpi: Cohorts currently outside their ROAS corridor
Share of today's installs from sources with declining 14d quality trend

secondary_kpis: Full metric set per cohort: installs, activation, D0-D30 retention, sessions, engagement depth, IAP revenue, ad revenue, total revenue, ARPU, LTV actual, pLTV, ROAS, payback, churn probability, whale rate, payer conversion
Cohort similarity scores (nearest historical analogues)
Cohort maturity indicator (how much of the predicted value is realized vs extrapolated)
Segment stability (does this cohort definition produce consistent results over time)
dimensions: Full catalog - see cohort_intelligence.dimension_model. Any combination of acquisition, device, geographic, behavioral, temporal and experimental dimensions, with governed cardinality limits.

visualizations.spec: Faceted builder producing a named, versioned cohort object; shows estimated size and statistical power before running; warns when a slice is too small for reliable inference (n < 500 installs for retention, n < 2000 for revenue).
Up to 8 cohorts x ~30 metrics, with per-metric significance testing, effect sizes, and automatic highlighting of the 5 metrics with the largest standardized differences.
One page per cohort: retention curve, revenue accrual curve (IAP vs ad), ROAS maturation, payback, pLTV with interval, and its position within the corridor of its peer group.
Rolling cohort quality index per media source with change detection, so a deteriorating source is visible weeks before ROAS matures.
Given a young cohort, retrieves the k most similar mature historical cohorts (feature-space nearest neighbours) and shows how they finished - a fast, model-free sanity check on the pLTV prediction.
Lorenz curve of revenue concentration per cohort; a cohort whose LTV depends on 2 whales is fundamentally different from one with broad payer conversion, and must not be scaled on its headline LTV.

alerts.condition: source-level quality index < 28d mean - 2 sigma with n >= 500 installs/day
alerts.value: earliest possible acquisition-quality signal (available at D0)

alerts.condition: cohort tracking > 25% below the median of its 20 nearest historical analogues at the same age
top 1% of payers contribute > 55% of cohort revenue AND the cohort is being used to justify scaling
alerts.action: block scale recommendations that rely on this cohort's LTV; require the median-payer LTV instead

alerts.condition: the device/geo/os mix inside a campaign's cohort shifts > 15pp week over week
alerts.meaning: network optimization has silently changed who it is buying; performance changes may be entirely mix

alerts.condition: any agent proposes an action based on a cohort with n below the metric's minimum
alerts.action: the Warden rejects the action pre-execution

drill_downs: Cohort -> sub-cohorts by any dimension -> individual users (sampled, pseudonymized) -> their event timeline -> the creative/campaign that acquired them
Cohort -> its pLTV prediction -> SHAP attribution -> the features -> the raw behavioral events those features came from
Cohort -> nearest analogues -> what happened to them and what actions were taken at the time
historical_comparisons: Same slice, previous cohorts (weekly and monthly)
Nearest-neighbour historical analogues
Same cohort age across app versions
Paid vs organic within the same geo/period (the cleanest quality benchmark available)
