fleet_summary.design_pattern: Each agent is a long-running, stateful service (not a chat session) built as: scheduler -> deterministic detection layer -> evidence assembly -> LLM reasoning layer (hypothesis generation, narrative, cross-source synthesis) -> deterministic decision layer (thresholds, guardrails, EV math) -> proposal/action emission. The LLM never computes numbers and never authorizes an action; it proposes hypotheses and writes explanations over an evidence bundle that deterministic code assembled and validated.
fleet_summary.naming: Each agent has a stable ID (AGT-XX-NN) used in every event, audit record and permission grant, plus a human codename used in the UI.

runtime.deployment: One Kubernetes deployment per agent, horizontally scalable, leader-elected for scheduled work; detection work is sharded by entity hash so a single agent type can process 600 campaigns in parallel.
execution_shape: 2. GATE: check data freshness/completeness for every dataset in this agent's declared lineage; check global mode (freeze?), agent mode, kill switch. Abort with a logged reason if gated.
3. DETECT: run deterministic detectors over the agent's KPI scope. Emit nothing if no candidate.
4. LOCALIZE: dimension contribution attribution + changepoint estimation on each candidate.
5. ASSEMBLE EVIDENCE: pull the fixed evidence schema for the candidate (time series, peer comparisons, upstream events, related entity states, prior similar cases from memory).

6. REASON (LLM): generate ranked causal hypotheses constrained to the causal DAG's admissible parents, request additional evidence via tool calls (bounded to N=6 extra queries), and produce a structured finding object.

7. VERIFY: deterministic checks on the LLM output - every cited number must exist in the evidence bundle within tolerance; every hypothesis must map to a known cause taxonomy node; reject and retry once, then downgrade to 'unexplained anomaly'.
8. SCORE: compute confidence, impact, priority via the decision engine (deterministic).
9. DECIDE: map (confidence, impact, action type, scope) through the autonomy matrix -> Observe / Recommend / Execute.
10. ACT: submit to the Action Gateway with idempotency key, prior state, rollback plan. Gateway independently re-validates guardrails.
11. EMIT: publish event(s) to the bus; write memory; schedule measurement jobs at +24h/+72h/+7d.
12. LEARN: on measurement callback, write the outcome record that the Scholar agent consumes.
runtime.timeouts: Detection pass <= 120s; full investigation <= 15 min; an investigation exceeding budget emits a partial finding with reduced confidence rather than nothing.
runtime.idempotency: Every agent action carries key = hash(agent_id, entity_id, action_type, decision_window, evidence_fingerprint). Duplicate keys are no-ops at the gateway.

llm_usage_policy.tiering: Fast small-model tier for classification, summarization, event triage and routine narrative (~90% of calls). Balanced mid tier for standard agent reasoning. Frontier reasoning tier for the orchestrator, root-cause synthesis, and any decision above 0.5% of S_daily.
hard_constraints: No arithmetic: all numbers come from the evidence bundle; a numeric-grounding validator rejects any number in the output not present in the bundle (within float tolerance) or derivable by a whitelisted formula.
No action authorization: the LLM proposes an action object; the deterministic decision layer and the gateway decide whether it may run.
Structured output only: agents emit tool-call-validated JSON conforming to the finding/proposal schema. Free text exists only in explicitly narrative fields.
Bounded tool budget per investigation to cap cost and latency.
Prompt caching on the static portion (agent charter, taxonomy, guardrails, schema) with only the evidence bundle varying.
Every LLM call logs prompt hash, model tier, tokens, latency and cost to the audit store.

memory_architecture_shared.working_memory: Redis, TTL 24h: current tick state, in-flight investigations, recent detections for dedupe.
memory_architecture_shared.episodic_memory: Postgres: every finding, action, and outcome as a first-class record with an embedding of its evidence summary (pgvector) for case-based retrieval ('have we seen this before?').
memory_architecture_shared.semantic_memory: Curated knowledge: metric definitions, causal DAG, entity relationship graph, network behavior notes ('Meta CBO reallocates within 6h of a budget change'; 'Unity reporting restates T-1 by up to 9%'), seasonal priors, per-slice baselines.
memory_architecture_shared.procedural_memory: Playbooks: named, versioned action recipes with historical hit rates. A playbook is retrieved by situation fingerprint and its prior performance directly modulates confidence.
memory_architecture_shared.retention: Episodic 3 years; semantic indefinite with version history; working 24h. All memory writes are append-only and attributable.

components.S_stat: statistical strength of the detection: min(1, |z|/5) or 1 - p_value, or posterior probability of the changepoint
components.S_data: data quality: freshness ratio x completeness ratio x (1 - expected restatement magnitude) for every dataset in the lineage
components.S_sample: sample adequacy: min(1, n/n_required) where n_required is the metric's minimum for the requested effect size at 80% power
components.S_corroboration: cross-agent and cross-signal agreement: fraction of independently checkable corroborating signals that confirm (e.g. a retention drop corroborated by session-depth decline and by the early-signal model)
components.S_precedent: case-based: historical precision of this agent on this finding type in this entity class over the last 90 days (Beta posterior mean with a weak prior, so a new agent starts near 0.5, not 1.0)
components.S_model: model trust: backtest accuracy of any model used, penalized by current drift (PSI) and interval width
components.P_penalties: sum of: 0.15 if any lineage dataset is degraded; 0.10 if a known confounding event overlaps the window; 0.10 if the entity had another change in the last 48h; 0.20 if the effect is within the metric's historical noise band; 0.10 if attribution certainty for the slice < 0.6

confidence_scoring_shared_model.calibration: Weekly, the Scholar agent fits an isotonic/Platt calibration per (agent, finding type) on realized outcomes and applies it as a post-hoc transform, so 'confidence 0.8' empirically means ~80% correct. Uncalibrated agents cannot hold Mode 3 grants.
confidence_scoring_shared_model.usage: Confidence gates mode selection, alert routing, and the size of any action (action magnitude scales with confidence, see autonomous_actions.sizing_rule).

guardrails_shared: Data gate: no action when any lineage dataset is degraded or freshness SLO is breached.
Sample gate: no action on slices below the metric's minimum n.
Freeze gate: global change freeze or title-level freeze forces Observe.
Cooldown gate: no repeat action on the same entity within the action type's cooldown.
Rate gate: per-agent and per-entity action rate limits.
Blast-radius gate: cumulative daily financial exposure per agent and fleet-wide.
Conflict gate: the orchestrator must not have an open conflicting directive for that entity.
Novelty gate: an entity changed by a human in the last 4h is off-limits to autonomous action (humans get right of way).
Market gate: if Scout has an active market-wide explanation covering this entity's metric, entity-specific corrective actions are downgraded to Recommend.
Maturity gate: no economics-based action on cohorts younger than the metric's minimum maturity (e.g. no D7-ROAS-based cut before D3 with predictive support).
Two-person gate: any action above 1.0% of S_daily requires human approval regardless of agent or confidence.

levels: L2 owning manager (Slack DM + approval task)
L4 VP Growth / Head of Data
escalation_shared.triggers: severity, dollar impact, SLA breach, repeated failure, safety events; the exact matrix is in governance.escalation_matrix

feedback_loop_shared.prediction_registry: Every finding and action writes a prediction record: metric, entity, expected direction and magnitude, horizon, confidence, counterfactual baseline method.
feedback_loop_shared.measurement: Scheduled jobs at +24h/+72h/+7d/+30d compute the realized value and the counterfactual (synthetic control from matched entities, or the pre-registered holdout), producing realized_effect, prediction_error and a verdict (correct / partially correct / wrong / inconclusive).
feedback_loop_shared.consumption: Outcomes update the agent's precedent prior, its calibration, its playbook hit rates, and feed the Scholar agent's weekly fleet review.

AGT-UA-01.default_mode: Mode 2 (Recommend); Mode 3 granted for 6 specific action types listed below
AGT-UA-01.mission: Keep every paid campaign inside its economic envelope: detect delivery and cohort-quality changes at campaign/adset/geo grain, decide whether to scale, hold, throttle or cut, and execute bounded budget and bid changes that maximize portfolio marginal return - never scaling on acquisition-side metrics alone.
data_inputs: fct_campaign_daily / fct_campaign_hourly (spend, impressions, clicks, installs by network x campaign x adset x ad x geo x platform)
fct_cohort_daily (cohort-grain retention, revenue, ROAS, pLTV by campaign slice)
dim_campaign / dim_adset / dim_ad (settings: budget, bid, targets, targeting, status, learning phase)
spend_response_curve_params (per campaign, refit nightly by Ledger)
creative_performance (from Muse) and creative fatigue state
action_history and outcome records (own episodic memory)
kpis_monitored: D1/D3/D7 retention of the campaign's cohorts

monitoring_frequency.cpi_and_efficiency: hourly (with a 4-hour trailing window to control noise)
monitoring_frequency.cohort_quality: every 6 hours (cohort tables materialize on that cadence)
monitoring_frequency.scaling_evaluation: daily at 09:00 and 15:00 local per network's operating timezone

detection_logic.rule: cohort CPI over a trailing 24h window > campaign 28d weekday-matched median + 2.5*MAD, with installs >= 25 and spend >= 0.05% of S_daily, AND the peer-relative check passes (entity delta - peer-group median delta > 2.5 * peer MAD) so market-wide CPM moves do not trigger it.
detection_logic.decomposition_run: always decompose CPI change multiplicatively into CPM x CTR x CVR contributions before emitting

detection_logic.rule: predicted D30 ROAS of the trailing 3-day cohorts < 0.80 * campaign 28d baseline with cohort n >= 300, or D1 retention below the campaign's corridor P10 with n >= 500. Uses Prism's mix-adjusted numbers so a composition shift is not misread as a quality decline.
detection_logic.priority: highest - this is the signal that must beat CPI to the punch

detection_logic.rule: ALL of: (a) marginal D180 ROAS from the fitted spend-response curve > portfolio target x 1.05 with the 80% CI lower bound also above target; (b) trailing 7d cohort ROAS at every available checkpoint inside or above the corridor; (c) budget utilization > 92% (delivery is budget-limited, not bid-limited); (d) creative fatigue index of the campaign's top-3-spend creatives < 0.35; (e) no open cohort-quality finding on this campaign; (f) the campaign has not been scaled in the last 72h.

projected end-of-day spend < 80% of budget for 2 consecutive days while the campaign is not intentionally capped; classify as bid-limited (utilization low, target CPA near achieved CPA), audience-limited (frequency rising, reach flat), or policy-limited (rejected/limited ads present).
active campaign, budget > 0, impressions = 0 for 4 hours inside its historical delivery window.
projected payback of trailing-7d cohorts > 120 days on a campaign spending > 0.3% of S_daily.
campaign in the bottom decile of marginal ROAS portfolio-wide AND below break-even predicted D180 ROAS with a prediction-interval upper bound below 1.0.

decision_logic.core_rule: Hunter never decides on acquisition metrics alone. Every scale/cut decision is evaluated against the cohort economics gate: P(cohort D180 ROAS >= target) computed by Oracle. Low CPI with P < 0.5 is a cut candidate, not a scale candidate.

decision_table.condition: marginal ROAS > target*1.05 AND P(target ROAS) >= 0.65 AND fatigue < 0.35 AND budget-limited
decision_table.size: min(25%, distance to the fitted saturation knee, remaining portfolio headroom) - and scaled by confidence: delta = base_delta * confidence

decision_table.note: explicit no-op is a decision and is logged; prevents churn

decision_table.condition: predicted D30 ROAS < 0.80*baseline OR P(target ROAS) in [0.25, 0.50)
decision_table.size: -20% to -35% depending on severity and confidence; prefer targeted exclusion (geo/placement/device) over blanket budget cuts when localization confidence > 0.7

decision_table.condition: P(target ROAS) < 0.25 AND cohort n >= 500 AND spend > 0.1% S_daily
decision_table.note: pause requires either confidence >= 0.85 or human approval; a 50% throttle is the autonomous default because pausing loses learning-phase state

decision_table.constraint: only if the new implied CPI stays below allowable CPI with >= 10% margin; otherwise recommend reallocating budget elsewhere instead

decision_table.note: never auto-changes budget on zero delivery; the cause is usually operational (policy/billing) and a budget change would be wrong

decision_table.condition: market-wide CPM surge covering this entity (Scout active)
decision_table.rationale: cutting into a temporary auction spike surrenders share and re-entry costs more than riding it out

decision_logic.conflict_deference: If Anchor, Prism, Oracle or Compass has an open finding on the same entity, Hunter must attach it and defer the decision to the orchestrator when the findings imply opposite directions.

agent_specific_adjustments: S_sample uses installs for CPI decisions and cohort installs for ROAS decisions - these differ by an order of magnitude and conflating them is the most common way to act on noise.
-0.15 penalty when attribution_certainty for the slice < 0.6 (heavily SKAN-modeled iOS campaigns).
-0.10 when the campaign changed budget/bid/creative in the last 48h (its own prior actions confound the read).
+0.05 when a matching historical case in episodic memory had the same cause and the same action succeeded (capped contribution).
Hard cap of 0.75 on any decision where the cohort maturity is below D3 and no early-signal model prediction is available.

root_cause_analysis_process: 1. Decompose the headline metric: CPI change = CPM effect x CTR effect x CVR effect (Shapley-normalized log decomposition); ROAS change = CPI effect x LTV effect, LTV effect further split into retention effect x monetization effect.

2. Localize dimensions: run contribution attribution (Adtributor-style surprise + explanatory power) across geo, placement, device_tier, os_version, creative, audience, hour-of-day; return the minimal dimension set explaining >= 70% of the change.

3. Establish the changepoint window via BOCPD and align it against the event log: our budget/bid/creative/targeting changes, app releases, config changes, network policy events (Scout), competitor launches, holidays.
4. Peer test: did comparable campaigns on the same network/geo move the same way? If yes -> external cause; if no -> entity-specific cause.

5. Composition test: recompute the metric holding the dimension mix fixed at the baseline period. If the change disappears, the cause is mix, not performance (and the correct action is completely different).

6. Upstream test: check every upstream variable in the causal DAG that has an admissible path to this metric (creative fatigue, audience saturation/frequency, bid/target changes, competing internal campaigns, attribution changes, tracking health) with lagged correlation over the changepoint window.
7. Consult episodic memory for the 5 nearest historical cases by evidence embedding and report what the cause turned out to be and what worked.

8. Rank hypotheses by posterior = prior(cause class | this metric, this network) x likelihood(evidence | cause); emit the top 3 with probabilities, and explicitly emit 'unexplained' when the top posterior < 0.35 rather than forcing a story.
actions_it_can_recommend: Any budget change of any size
Pause/resume campaign, adset, ad
Bid / target CPA / target ROAS change
Add geo, placement, device-tier, OS-version or publisher exclusions
Move budget between campaigns or networks
Change campaign structure or consolidate cannibalizing adsets
Change optimization event or attribution window
Creative rotation requests to Muse
Open an investigation (cohort, monetization, product)

actions_it_can_execute_automatically.bounds: <= 35% of current daily budget per action; entity spend <= 0.50% of S_daily; confidence >= 0.70; cooldown 12h; max 2 per campaign per day
<= 20% of current daily budget per action; resulting daily spend <= 0.40% of S_daily; confidence >= 0.80; cooldown 48h; max 1 per campaign per day; requires all six scaling conditions
actions_it_can_execute_automatically.rationale: asymmetric risk - scaling a bad cohort is far more expensive than missing upside, so bounds are tighter than for decreases

actions_it_can_execute_automatically.bounds: entity spend <= 0.15% of S_daily; confidence >= 0.85; not the last active adset in a campaign
affected spend share <= 25% of the campaign; confidence >= 0.80; localization explanatory power >= 0.70
actions_it_can_execute_automatically.rationale: surgical and reversible; usually superior to a budget cut

actions_it_can_execute_automatically.bounds: <= 12% change per action; resulting implied CPI must remain <= 0.90 * allowable CPI; confidence >= 0.80; cooldown 24h
only on Compass-confirmed fraud findings with confidence >= 0.85; unlimited count (protective)

actions_requiring_human_approval: Any budget change above the autonomous bounds or on entities above 0.50% of S_daily
Pausing or resuming a campaign
Any change to a campaign in soft launch or flagged strategic/partner-managed
Structural changes (new adsets, consolidation, objective changes)
Attribution window or optimization event changes
Cumulative same-direction changes exceeding 50% of a campaign's budget within 7 days
Any action while the title is in a change freeze or within 14 days of a major release
safety_guardrails: All shared guardrails apply.
Directional consistency: cannot increase and decrease the same entity's budget within 24h (anti-oscillation).
Cumulative drift cap: total autonomous budget change per campaign <= 50% over any rolling 7 days.
Learning-phase protection: no budget change > 20% on an adset in learning phase (it resets learning and destroys delivery).
Portfolio integrity: the sum of autonomous increases minus decreases across the fleet must not move portfolio daily spend by more than 5% without orchestrator sign-off.
Human right-of-way: no autonomous action on an entity a human touched in the last 4 hours.
Network API sanity: verify post-change state by reading back the entity 60 seconds after the write; mismatch triggers automatic retry then rollback then alert.
Never pause the last delivering adset of a campaign or the last campaign of a title/geo.
Never act on a metric whose denominator is below the display minimum.

max_allowed_financial_impact.per_action: 0.20% of S_daily in daily-spend delta (at S_daily=$250k -> $500/day of budget change per action)
max_allowed_financial_impact.per_agent_per_day: 3.0% of S_daily in absolute cumulative daily-spend delta (at $250k -> $7,500/day of net budget movement)
max_allowed_financial_impact.hard_ceiling: Any single action whose modeled 30-day P&L exposure exceeds 1.0% of S_daily x 30 requires human approval regardless of other limits.
max_allowed_financial_impact.measurement: Exposure is computed as |delta_daily_budget| x 30 days for budget actions, and as spend_at_risk for pause actions.

escalation_rules: Cohort-quality finding with 30-day impact > 0.5% of S_daily x 30 -> L3 Head of UA within 15 minutes.
Payback breach on > 5% of portfolio spend -> L4 VP Growth + Finance.
Two consecutive autonomous actions on the same entity failing their measurement check -> stop acting on that entity, escalate to L2 with the full history.
Zero delivery on a campaign spending > 0.3% of S_daily -> L2 immediately (operational, time-critical).
Any network API write failure or state mismatch -> L2 + data engineering.
Conflicting directive from another agent that Hunter cannot resolve -> orchestrator, then L3 if the orchestrator cannot resolve within 30 minutes.

consumes_from: Ledger (spend-response curves, portfolio headroom, pacing constraints)
dependencies_on_other_agents.blocking_dependencies: Cannot execute economics-based actions when Oracle reports pLTV drift beyond threshold, when Prism reports cohort tables stale, or when Compass reports an attribution incident on the network in question.

memory_context_requirements.working: current tick's entity states, in-flight proposals, 24h detection fingerprints for dedupe
memory_context_requirements.episodic: every finding/action/outcome on every campaign, 3 years; used for precedent priors and case retrieval
memory_context_requirements.semantic: per-campaign baselines and corridors, network behavior notes (e.g. 'Meta CBO redistributes within 6h; measure effects no earlier than T+24h'; 'Google AC needs 3-5 days to re-stabilize after a target change'), learning-phase rules per network, seasonal CPM priors per geo
memory_context_requirements.procedural: playbooks: 'staged scale-up', 'placement exclusion before budget cut', 'quality-decline throttle', 'bid-limited unlock', 'zero-delivery triage'
memory_context_requirements.context_window_strategy: The evidence bundle is assembled deterministically and capped (top-N dimensions, 90d of daily series, 5 nearest historical cases). Never dump raw tables into the model.

feedback_loop.predictions_registered: For every action: expected direction and magnitude of CPI, installs, cohort D7 ROAS and spend at +24h/+72h/+7d, with intervals.
feedback_loop.counterfactual_method: Synthetic control from 5-15 matched campaigns (same network, geo tier, objective, spend band) that received no action, using pre-period matching on 14 days; where matching quality is poor, fall back to the campaign's own pre-period forecast.
learning_signals: which root-cause hypothesis proved correct (adjudicated by the incident resolution)
feedback_loop.adaptation: Playbook hit rates and per-network priors update weekly; scaling step sizes adapt per network based on realized overshoot; the 'peer-relative' thresholds retune monthly.

success_criteria.detection: Cohort-quality regressions detected at median <= 36 hours after cohort start (vs D7+ manually); >= 80% of regressions detected before CPI moves.
success_criteria.precision: >= 0.78 on emitted findings (human + outcome adjudicated), measured over rolling 30 days.
success_criteria.action_quality: >= 70% of executed actions have realized effect in the predicted direction; MAPE of predicted 30-day impact <= 0.35; rollback rate <= 5%.
success_criteria.business: Wasted spend (spend on cohorts finishing below 0.6x target D30 ROAS) reduced >= 30% vs the manual-managed holdout; incremental margin from scaling actions >= $150k/quarter attributable via the holdout.

AGT-BUD-02.agent_name: Ledger - Budget Pacing & Portfolio Allocation Agent
AGT-BUD-02.default_mode: Mode 2 (Recommend) at package level; Mode 3 for individual reallocation steps within an approved package
AGT-BUD-02.mission: Keep portfolio spend on plan and allocated at the point of equal marginal return: maintain spend-response curves for every campaign, detect pacing risk early enough to fix inside the period, and continuously propose reallocation packages that raise portfolio margin without changing total spend.
data_inputs: fct_cohort_daily revenue and ROAS by campaign
pLTV and P(target ROAS) per slice (Oracle)
campaign settings and constraints (budget caps, bid strategy, contractual minimums)
market CPM index and seasonal calendar (Scout)
kpis_monitored: MTD spend vs plan and projected month-end
marginal ROAS (EMDE) per campaign and its dispersion
portfolio headroom at target marginal ROAS

monitoring_frequency.allocation_optimization: daily 07:00 UTC + on demand when a package is requested
monitoring_frequency.spend_response_curve_refit: nightly (rolling 90-day window, per campaign, with recency weighting)
monitoring_frequency.month_end_risk_projection: every 4 hours from day 20 of the month

detection_logic.rule: projected month-end spend outside +/-8% of the envelope with >= 5 days remaining, where the projection uses the campaign's learned pacing curve (not linear extrapolation) plus known scheduled changes.
projected underspend > 5% of envelope AND >= 1% of S_daily/day exists in campaigns whose marginal ROAS 80% CI lower bound > target.
coefficient of variation of marginal ROAS across campaigns holding >= 60% of spend > 0.35, and the computed recoverable value > 0.5% of S_daily/day.
a campaign's operating point is past the fitted knee (marginal ROAS < 0.85 x average ROAS) for 5 consecutive days -> further spend there is value-destructive.
any network > 45% of portfolio spend or any campaign > 12% of a title's spend.
P(month-end spend > envelope * 1.02) > 0.5 from the forecast posterior.

decision_logic.allocation_optimizer: Solve max SUM_i revenue_180_i(s_i) - SUM_i s_i subject to SUM_i s_i = S_target, l_i <= s_i <= u_i, |s_i - s_i_current| <= 0.25 * s_i_current (per-day move cap), and P(target ROAS)_i >= 0.4 for any campaign receiving an increase. Response functions are the fitted Hill/log curves with uncertainty; the optimizer maximizes the expected value under the posterior, not the point estimate, and applies a risk penalty proportional to curve uncertainty so it does not pour money into a poorly-fit curve.
decision_logic.staging: Never execute a full reallocation in one step. Packages are decomposed into 3-5 daily steps with checkpoints; each step's execution is conditional on the previous step's measured effect being within its prediction interval.
decision_logic.pacing_correction: Prefer (1) reallocating to existing high-marginal-ROAS campaigns, then (2) raising bid targets on bid-limited campaigns where allowable CPI permits, then (3) accepting underspend. Never (4) raise budgets on campaigns below target marginal ROAS purely to hit a spend number - spending the envelope is not a goal, margin is.
decision_logic.abort_rule: If a staged package's step-2 measurement falls outside the prediction interval, halt the remaining steps and re-optimize rather than continuing on a broken assumption.

agent_specific: S_model is dominated by spend-response curve fit quality: R^2, residual autocorrelation, and the width of the marginal-ROAS credible interval at the proposed operating point.
Confidence is capped at 0.65 for any campaign whose curve was fit on fewer than 20 distinct spend levels or fewer than 30 days.
+0.10 when the proposed move is within a spend range the campaign has historically operated in (interpolation, not extrapolation); -0.20 when it extrapolates beyond the observed range.

root_cause_analysis_process: 1. For a pacing deviation, decompose into per-title/network/campaign contributions.
2. Classify each contributing campaign as budget-limited, bid-limited, audience-limited, or policy-limited using utilization, achieved-vs-target cost, frequency trend, and ad status.
3. Check whether the deviation is delivery-side (network not spending) or intentional (agent/human throttles) by joining the action log.
4. Test whether market conditions explain it (Scout CPM index) before concluding an internal cause.
5. Quantify the counterfactual: what would month-end look like with no intervention, and what is the margin cost of each remedy option.
actions_it_can_recommend: Full reallocation packages across campaigns/networks/titles
Budget envelope changes
Bid target changes to unlock capped delivery
Pausing saturated campaigns
Pre-positioning budget for seasonal events
Freezing discretionary spend

actions_it_can_execute_automatically.bounds: only steps inside a human-approved package; each step <= 15% of the affected campaign's budget; total package <= 5% of S_daily; step cooldown 24h; halted automatically if the prior step missed its prediction interval
daily budget adjustments <= 8% per campaign to keep intraday pacing on curve, only for campaigns already inside their economic envelope, max 1/day, net portfolio spend change <= 2%

actions_requiring_human_approval: Any new reallocation package (the package, not its steps)
Budget envelope changes (Finance)
Any reallocation crossing titles (P&L ownership boundary)
Any move > 25% of a campaign's budget
Month-end catch-up spending above plan
safety_guardrails: Portfolio spend neutrality: reallocation packages must be spend-neutral +/-2% unless explicitly an envelope change.

Per-day move cap of 25% per campaign, enforced additively with Hunter's own changes (the gateway tracks a single per-entity daily change budget shared by all agents - this prevents two agents each making a 'safe' 20% change).
No increase into a campaign with an open cohort-quality finding.
No extrapolation beyond 1.5x the campaign's historical max daily spend in a single package.
Learning-phase protection.
Month-end blackout: no autonomous packages in the last 2 days of a month (finance close risk).
Curve staleness: no action on a curve older than 48h or fit on degraded data.

max_allowed_financial_impact.note: Ledger moves money between campaigns rather than creating exposure, so its limits are expressed as gross movement; net portfolio change is capped at 2%/day without orchestrator sign-off.

escalation_rules: Projected envelope breach > 10% -> L4 VP Growth + Finance immediately.
Recoverable allocation value > 2% of S_daily/day unaddressed for 7 days -> L3.
Package abort due to a missed prediction interval -> L2 with the diagnostic.
Curve refit failure for campaigns holding > 20% of spend -> L2 + data engineering.

dependencies_on_other_agents.blocking: Cannot propose increases without a current Oracle P(target ROAS) for the receiving campaigns.

memory_context_requirements.working: current package state and step checkpoints
memory_context_requirements.episodic: every package, step, and realized elasticity - this is how the curves learn from the system's own interventions rather than only from observational data
memory_context_requirements.semantic: seasonal spend patterns, network delivery behaviors, contractual minimums, historical saturation points
memory_context_requirements.procedural: playbooks: 'staged reallocation', 'month-end catch-up', 'seasonal pre-position', 'underspend unlock'

feedback_loop.predictions_registered: For each step: expected spend, installs, and revenue_180 at the new operating point with intervals.
feedback_loop.counterfactual_method: The reallocation itself is a natural experiment: donor and recipient campaigns are compared against matched controls; where possible, packages are randomized across matched campaign pairs (a switchback design) to get clean elasticity estimates.
feedback_loop.adaptation: Realized elasticities directly update the spend-response curves, which is the highest-value learning in the system because these curves drive every allocation decision.

success_criteria.pacing: Month-end spend within +/-3% of envelope for >= 11 of 12 months.
success_criteria.allocation: Marginal-ROAS dispersion (CV) reduced below 0.20 and held.
success_criteria.value: Realized incremental margin from reallocation >= 1.5% of portfolio spend annually, verified via the holdout/switchback.
success_criteria.safety: Zero envelope breaches > 5%; package abort rate < 15%.

AGT-CRE-03.default_mode: Mode 2; Mode 3 for creative pause/rotation within bounds
AGT-CRE-03.mission: Maximize creative portfolio value: detect fatigue before it inflates CPI, identify creatives that acquire poor cohorts despite good acquisition metrics, learn which creative attributes drive downstream value, and keep the rotation pipeline ahead of decay.
data_inputs: fct_creative_daily (impressions, clicks, installs, spend, IPM, CTR, CPI by creative x network x geo x placement)
video engagement metrics (quartile completion, watch time) where the network exposes them

creative asset metadata and auto-extracted attributes (via a vision/multimodal pass over the asset: hook type, first-frame subject, presence of faces/text, pacing, duration, orientation, language, CTA style, gameplay authenticity score)
cohort outcomes joined to the acquiring creative (retention, pLTV, ROAS) from fct_cohort_daily
creative production pipeline state (asset management system)
kpis_monitored: downstream D1/D7 retention and predicted D30 ROAS of each creative's cohort

monitoring_frequency.performance: hourly for creatives above 0.05% of S_daily; every 6 hours otherwise
monitoring_frequency.fatigue_recompute: every 6 hours (CFI needs impression accumulation, not clock time)

detection_logic.rule: CFI >= 0.40 (warning) / >= 0.55 (critical), computed only when cumulative impressions >= 150k and days_live >= 7, and always relative to concurrent peers in the same (network x geo x placement) cells so market moves are excluded. CUSUM on IPM catches slow decay that thresholds miss.

creative in the top IPM quartile of its peer group AND its cohort's D7 retention in the bottom quartile AND cohort n >= 500. This asymmetry (great acquisition, bad users) is the highest-cost creative failure and is invisible to network optimizers, which optimize for the install.
Bayesian P(IPM_new > IPM_incumbent) > 0.90 with >= 30k impressions AND early cohort quality index not below peer P25 - a winner on IPM alone is not promoted.
top 3 creatives >= 55% of a title's spend and at least one with CFI > 0.35 -> a volume cliff is imminent.
creatives projected to retire in the next 14 days (from fitted decay curves) > creatives passing test in the last 14 days.
>= 3 rejections from the same network within 24h -> likely a policy change, not independent errors.
a creative fatigued in geo A but with CFI < 0.25 and above-median IPM in geo B -> reallocation opportunity rather than retirement.

decision_logic.rotation_rule: On critical fatigue with a qualified replacement (same concept cluster or a tested winner, CQS >= peer median, sufficient test volume), shift budget in stages: 40% of the fatigued creative's share to replacements immediately, remainder over 48h, measuring IPM recovery at each step. Never remove a creative that carries > 40% of a campaign's delivery in a single step - the campaign's delivery will collapse and the network's optimizer will re-enter learning.
decision_logic.no_replacement_rule: If no qualified replacement exists, do NOT pause: emit a Sev-2 pipeline finding and recommend a temporary budget reduction instead, because pausing without inventory just moves the loss from CPI to volume.
decision_logic.misleading_creative_rule: Immediate pause candidate at confidence >= 0.80 regardless of IPM - the cohort damage compounds daily and is not recoverable.
decision_logic.promotion_rule: Test winners are promoted with a staged budget share (5% -> 15% -> 35%) with quality checkpoints at each stage; downstream quality must hold at D3 before the next stage.
decision_logic.brief_generation: Weekly, produce a production brief ranking attribute combinations by expected margin contribution, with sample sizes and explicit uncertainty; briefs are recommendations to humans, never auto-executed.

agent_specific: S_stat for fatigue uses the fitted decay curve's slope significance, not a single-day delta.
S_corroboration requires the peer-relative check to pass; a fatigue call without peer confirmation is capped at 0.6.
Downstream-quality claims are capped at 0.7 until cohort n >= 1000 (creative-level cohorts are small and noisy).
-0.15 when the creative ran in fewer than 3 distinct (network x geo) cells (single-cell effects are often targeting artifacts, not creative properties).

root_cause_analysis_process: 1. Separate creative-specific decay from market/auction effects using concurrent peer performance in the same cells.

2. Decompose IPM decline into CTR decline vs store-conversion decline (a CTR-driven decline is hook fatigue; a CVR-driven decline is usually a store-page or expectation mismatch, not creative fatigue at all).
3. Check audience saturation: frequency trend and reach curve - high frequency with declining CTR is audience exhaustion, which is fixed by audience expansion, not new creative.
4. Check whether the network re-allocated the creative to worse placements (placement mix shift can look exactly like fatigue).
5. For misleading-creative findings, compare the creative's depicted content (multimodal extraction) against actual first-session behavior to test the expectation-mismatch hypothesis explicitly.
6. Retrieve the concept cluster's historical fatigue curves to judge whether this decay is normal or premature.
actions_it_can_recommend: Pause/retire a creative
Rotate budget to specific replacements
Promote a test winner
Localize/re-cut a winner for another geo
Expand audience instead of replacing creative (when saturation is the real cause)
Production brief with attribute targets
Re-edit for policy compliance
Change creative test budget allocation

actions_it_can_execute_automatically.bounds: CFI >= 0.55; confidence >= 0.80; a qualified replacement exists; the creative carries <= 40% of the campaign's delivery; affected spend <= 0.20% of S_daily; max 3 rotations per campaign per week
<= 40% of the fatigued creative's share per step; <= 0.20% of S_daily affected; cooldown 24h
confidence >= 0.85; cohort n >= 500; affected spend <= 0.20% of S_daily
actions_it_can_execute_automatically.rationale: protective; the alternative is continued acquisition of negative-value users

actions_it_can_execute_automatically.bounds: to <= 15% budget share; confidence >= 0.80

actions_requiring_human_approval: Retiring a creative carrying > 40% of a campaign's delivery
Promoting a creative beyond 15% budget share
Any creative action on a strategic/brand campaign
Approving a production brief or reallocating production resources
Localizing/re-cutting (cost commitment)
Any creative change during a brand campaign flight
safety_guardrails: Never leave an adset with fewer than 2 active creatives (delivery collapse risk).
Never pause creatives representing > 40% of an adset's delivery in a single action.
No rotation within 72h of a prior rotation on the same adset (the network needs time to re-optimize).
No fatigue action during a market-wide CPM event flagged by Scout (fatigue and auction pressure look identical in raw CPI).
Minimum impression and days-live thresholds strictly enforced before any CFI-based decision.
Rotation actions are paused during the first 5 days of a new campaign (learning phase).
Downstream-quality-based pauses require cohort maturity >= D3.

max_allowed_financial_impact.per_action: 0.20% of S_daily of affected daily spend
max_allowed_financial_impact.note: Creative actions redistribute spend rather than change totals; risk is delivery disruption, so limits are expressed as affected spend and are also rate-limited per adset.

escalation_rules: Pipeline starvation projected to constrain spend by > 5% within 14 days -> L3 Creative Lead + Head of UA.
Concentration risk with imminent fatigue on > 30% of a title's spend -> L3 immediately.
Policy rejection cluster -> L2 + the network's account manager, with the rejection reasons attached.
Misleading-creative finding with > 1000 affected installs -> L3 (this is a brand and LTV risk, not just a performance issue).

provides_to: Hunter (fatigue state gating scaling decisions - a campaign cannot be scaled on fatiguing creatives)
dependencies_on_other_agents.blocking: Cannot make downstream-quality claims when cohort data is stale.

memory_context_requirements.episodic: every creative's full lifecycle: launch, performance curve, fatigue point, rotation decisions, outcomes - this is the training set for time-to-fatigue prediction
memory_context_requirements.semantic: concept clusters and their historical lifecycle norms per geo/network, attribute performance priors, policy rules per network
memory_context_requirements.procedural: playbooks: 'staged rotation', 'geo re-freshening', 'saturation vs fatigue triage', 'winner promotion ladder'

feedback_loop.predictions_registered: Expected IPM/CPI recovery and volume effect after each rotation at +24h/+72h/+7d; expected performance of promoted winners.
feedback_loop.counterfactual_method: Matched adsets in the same campaign that did not rotate; where a campaign has multiple similar adsets, rotations are randomized across them to create clean measurement.
feedback_loop.adaptation: Attribute->performance model refits weekly; time-to-fatigue predictions calibrate against realized retirement dates; the CQS weights are re-fit quarterly against realized cohort margin.

success_criteria.detection: Fatigue detected >= 4 days before CPI inflation exceeds 10% in >= 70% of cases.
success_criteria.value: CPI inflation from fatigue reduced >= 25% vs the manual-managed holdout; creative-driven volume cliffs (a >15% single-day install drop attributable to creative exhaustion) reduced to <= 1 per quarter.
success_criteria.quality: Misleading creatives caught before 2000 installs in >= 80% of cases.
success_criteria.pipeline: Zero periods where creative inventory constrains planned spend.

AGT-MON-04.default_mode: Mode 2; Mode 3 for floor adjustments and instance toggles within bounds
AGT-MON-04.mission: Defend and grow ad revenue per user: detect eCPM, fill, show-rate and impressions-per-DAU degradations within the hour, separate demand-side from supply-side from integration causes, and tune mediation without crossing the ad-load frontier that damages retention.
data_inputs: mediation reporting (MAX / LevelPlay / CAS / AdMob): impressions, revenue, eCPM, fill, requests by network x geo x format x placement x instance
user-level ad revenue (ULAR) events via the MMP
app-side ad telemetry: requests, fills, shows, completions, errors, latency, by app_version and placement
remote-config ad parameters and their change history (Lab)
cohort ad-revenue curves by acquisition source (Prism)

detection_logic.rule: hourly ad_arpdau below the weekday-and-hour-matched forecast p05 for 2 consecutive hours AND the daily projection is > 5% below the 28d weekday-matched baseline. Immediately runs the ARPDAU decomposition (imp/DAU x eCPM x fill x show x DAU-mix) before emitting, so the finding always names the responsible factor.
network x geo eCPM < 28d median - 3*MAD for 2 hours with impressions >= 5000, peer-checked against other networks in the same geo to distinguish partner-specific from market-wide.

fill_rate down > 10pp for 1h with requests >= 10000, or impressions/fills < 0.85 for 2h (show-rate failures are integration bugs and are treated as Sev-2 engineering issues, not monetization tuning problems).

|imp_per_dau - weekday-matched baseline|/baseline > 0.12 for a full day; auto-joins app_version adoption and config change history because this metric is almost always moved by a release or a config change.
app_version N ad_arpdau < N-1 by > 6% at matched user-day with adoption >= 15%.
|ULAR - reconciled|/reconciled > 8% for 3 consecutive days on a network -> the pLTV model is being fed biased ad revenue; notify Oracle to apply a correction factor.
cohorts above the frontier's imp/DAU threshold show D7 retention >= 3pp below matched cohorts below the threshold.
waterfall instance with win rate < 2% for 7 days (floor above achievable eCPM) or an instance whose realized eCPM exceeds its floor by > 60% (floor too low, leaving money on the table).

decision_logic.cause_class_routing: Every ARPDAU finding is first classified into one of: DEMAND (eCPM/bid density down, our supply unchanged), SUPPLY/UX (imp per DAU or requests changed - product/config cause), INTEGRATION (show rate, errors, latency - engineering cause), MIX (DAU composition shifted toward lower-monetizing users - a UA cause), MEASUREMENT (reporting/reconciliation issue). The action differs completely by class, so misclassification is the primary failure mode and the classifier is evaluated separately in the learning loop.
decision_logic.floor_tuning: For DEMAND-class issues, adjust instance floors toward the estimated revenue-maximizing point from the observed price-response curve (win rate vs floor), in steps of <= 15%, one change per instance per 24h, measured at +24h.
decision_logic.ad_load_rule: Any change that increases ad exposure must be evaluated against the frontier model: projected ad revenue gain minus projected retention-driven LTV loss, computed through the pLTV model. If the net is negative or its interval spans zero, the change is not proposed. Ad-load increases are never autonomous.
decision_logic.mix_rule: If the cause class is MIX, Vault does not tune monetization at all - it emits AD_REVENUE_CHANGE with the offending acquisition sources and hands the decision to Hunter/Prism via the orchestrator. Tuning floors to compensate for a UA-quality problem is the classic local-optimization trap this system is designed to prevent.

agent_specific: S_data heavily penalizes ULAR-only reads: intraday estimates carry a -0.15 penalty until reconciled.
S_corroboration requires agreement between mediation reporting and app-side telemetry; disagreement caps confidence at 0.55 and routes a data-quality finding instead.
Cause-class classification carries its own confidence, and the overall finding confidence is the product of detection confidence and classification confidence.

root_cause_analysis_process: 1. Run the ARPDAU decomposition to isolate the responsible factor with contribution percentages.
2. Localize by network, geo, format, placement, app_version, device_tier using contribution attribution.

3. Distinguish demand from supply: compare our request volume and signal completeness (IDFA/GAID/IDFV presence, consent strings) against the eCPM move - stable requests with falling eCPM is demand-side; falling requests is our side.
4. Peer check across networks in the same geo: if all networks fell, it is market/seasonal demand; if one fell, it is partner-specific.
5. Join the config and release timeline: any imp/DAU change is diffed against remote-config versions and app-version adoption curves.
6. Check the acquisition mix of the DAU base over the window (via Prism) to test the MIX hypothesis.
7. Check reconciliation status to rule out a pure measurement artifact before declaring a revenue loss.
8. Retrieve historical analogues (e.g. 'January demand cliff', 'end-of-quarter budget flush', 'iOS release changed IDFV behavior').

Enable/disable demand instances or networks
Change waterfall/bidding allocation
Change ad-load parameters via remote config
Open a partner ticket with the evidence bundle
Launch an ad-load A/B test instead of a blanket change
Notify UA about low-monetizing acquisition sources
Escalate an integration defect to engineering

actions_it_can_execute_automatically.bounds: <= 15% change per action; confidence >= 0.75; one change per instance per 24h; projected revenue impact <= 0.25% of daily ad revenue per action; never on an instance flagged by a partner dispute
win rate < 2% for 7 days; confidence >= 0.80; reversible; never reduces total configured demand below 5 active instances per placement
only from a pre-approved instance catalog; confidence >= 0.75; used to protect fill during a demand outage
show rate < 0.6 for 2h with n >= 5000; protective; alerts engineering simultaneously

actions_requiring_human_approval: Any ad-load change (cooldowns, caps, new placements) - always, because it trades revenue against retention
Adding or removing a network from mediation
Floor changes > 15% or affecting > 25% of a title's ad revenue
Any change during a partner dispute or contract negotiation
Changes to rewarded ad reward values (economy impact)
safety_guardrails: Ad-load increases are never autonomous under any confidence.
Floor changes require a measured price-response curve for that instance; no blind floor moves.
Total configured demand cannot fall below 5 active instances per placement (fill protection).
No action while mediation reporting is stale or while ULAR-vs-reconciled variance exceeds 8%.
No floor changes within 48h of a mediation platform SDK update (behavior changes invalidate the curves).
Changes are staged by geo tier: T3 geos first, T1 last, so mistakes are cheap.
Retention frontier check on every proposal that could increase exposure, including indirect ones.

max_allowed_financial_impact.per_action: 0.25% of daily ad revenue at risk
max_allowed_financial_impact.per_agent_per_day: 1.5% of daily ad revenue at risk
max_allowed_financial_impact.hard_rule: Cumulative floor changes cannot move a title's ad revenue by more than 3% in any 7-day window without human approval.

escalation_rules: Ad ARPDAU drop with projected daily loss > 1% of S_daily -> L4 + PagerDuty.
Show-rate/integration failure -> L2 engineering immediately (every minute is lost inventory).
Reconciliation drift > 8% for 3 days -> L3 + Finance (revenue recognition impact).
MIX-class cause -> hand to the orchestrator within 5 minutes with the offending sources named.
Ad-load harm detected -> L3 Product + Monetization jointly.

consumes_from: Prism (DAU acquisition mix, cohort ad revenue)
provides_to: Oracle (ad revenue curves and correction factors for pLTV)
dependencies_on_other_agents.blocking: Cannot attribute a revenue change to monetization without Pulse's DAU data and Prism's mix data - otherwise MIX and SUPPLY causes are indistinguishable.

memory_context_requirements.episodic: every floor change and its measured effect (this builds the price-response curves), every incident and its true cause class
memory_context_requirements.semantic: per-network demand seasonality (weekday, month-end, quarter-end, Q4/Q1 cycle), partner behavior notes, historical outage patterns, the ad-load frontier per title x geo
memory_context_requirements.procedural: playbooks: 'demand outage backfill', 'floor optimization sweep', 'version regression triage', 'show-rate incident'

feedback_loop.predictions_registered: Expected eCPM/fill/revenue effect of each floor or instance change at +24h/+72h.
feedback_loop.counterfactual_method: Geo-split or instance-split tests where possible (change floors in half the geos); otherwise synthetic control from matched geos/instances.
feedback_loop.adaptation: Price-response curves update from every floor change; the cause-class classifier is retrained on adjudicated incidents; the ad-load frontier refits weekly from natural variation and experiments.

success_criteria.detection: Ad revenue incidents detected within 60 minutes of onset in >= 90% of cases; cause class correct in >= 80% of adjudicated incidents.
success_criteria.value: Ad ARPDAU +4% from floor/waterfall optimization over 12 months, verified by geo-split tests; revenue lost to undetected integration failures reduced >= 70%.
success_criteria.safety: Zero retention regressions attributable to Vault-initiated changes.

AGT-IAP-05.default_mode: Mode 2; Mode 3 only for protective actions (restoring a lapsed approved offer, escalating checkout failures)
AGT-IAP-05.mission: Protect and grow in-app purchase economics: detect checkout failures within minutes, monitor payer conversion and offer performance at cohort-age grain, guard whale health, and quantify the LTV effect of every economy or paywall change.
data_inputs: validated purchase receipts (RevenueCat + store server notifications)
purchase funnel telemetry (paywall impression, open, checkout initiated, store sheet, success, error codes)
offer/SKU configuration and schedule (remote config + LiveOps calendar)
subscription lifecycle events (trial start, conversion, renewal, billing retry, cancellation)
in-game economy telemetry (currency sources/sinks, balances, progression stage)
kpis_monitored: checkout success rate and error mix
offer take rate and incremental revenue

detection_logic.rule: success rate < platform-adjusted baseline - 5pp for 30 minutes with >= 200 attempts, or any single error code exceeding 15% of attempts. Sev-1: this is pure lost revenue with a known fix path.
cohort-age-matched first-purchase rate down > 12% vs 28d baseline with n >= 5000 - always cohort-age-matched, because a calendar-day payer-conversion drop is usually just an install-mix change.
an offer contributing > 5% of IAP revenue in the trailing 7 days has no active successor 2 hours after its end timestamp.
take rate < 0.5x the offer's historical median at matched exposure, or incremental revenue (vs holdout where present) < 0.
>= 3 top-1% payers from one title inactive 7+ days within a week, or whale count down > 20% MoM.
renewal rate down > 5pp or involuntary churn up > 3pp vs 28d baseline.
currency source/sink ratio outside its designed band by > 25% for 3 days, or median balance growth > 2 sigma above design - inflation destroys future monetization before it shows in revenue.
refund rate > 2x 28d baseline with n >= 100; classified into fraud / billing bug / SKU misconfiguration / buyer-regret patterns by error and timing signatures.

decision_logic.triage_order: Checkout/technical failures first (fix path is unambiguous), then offer-configuration causes (cheap and reversible), then demand/design causes (require experimentation), then economy causes (require design review). Merchant never proposes a price change from an observational finding - price changes require an experiment.
decision_logic.lapse_rule: A lapsed previously-approved offer may be restored autonomously because the counterfactual (the offer running) is a known, already-approved state - this is a restoration, not a new commercial decision.
decision_logic.ltv_translation: Every IAP finding is translated into a pLTV delta via Oracle so UA can adjust allowable CPI, rather than being reported only as a revenue number.

agent_specific: Payer-conversion claims capped at 0.7 below n=5000 (payer conversion is a 1-2% rate; small samples are meaningless).
Whale findings are always capped at 0.65 - whale behavior is high-variance and individually driven.
Checkout-failure findings can reach 0.95 because the signal is near-deterministic (error codes).

root_cause_analysis_process: 1. Split the purchase funnel to locate the failing step: exposure, intent, or transaction.
2. Technical branch: break down by platform, OS version, app version, store, country, error code; compare against store status feeds.
3. Configuration branch: diff the offer/SKU configuration and LiveOps calendar against the changepoint.
4. Demand branch: check cohort mix (are these different users?), progression distribution (are players reaching the paywall?), and competing sinks.
5. Economy branch: check currency balances and sink availability - a player with 'enough' currency does not buy.
6. Cross-check with Lab for any running experiment touching paywalls, pricing or economy.
7. Retrieve analogues from episodic memory (seasonal purchase cycles, prior offer lapses).
actions_it_can_recommend: Enable/schedule a replacement offer
Adjust paywall placement or trigger timing
Launch a price or offer experiment
Fix an SKU/store configuration
Escalate checkout failures to engineering
Create a whale re-engagement/CRM segment
Adjust economy sink/source parameters (design review required)
Update the allowable-CPI table when payer economics shift by source

actions_it_can_execute_automatically.bounds: the identical offer configuration ran within the last 45 days and was approved; confidence >= 0.85; revenue impact <= 1% of daily IAP revenue; notifies the monetization PM immediately
unlimited (notification-only action, no state change)
SKU with > 40% transaction error rate and n >= 100; protective; reversible; notifies immediately

actions_requiring_human_approval: Any price change (always - price is a strategic and legal decision)
Any new offer or offer redesign
Paywall placement/timing changes
Economy parameter changes (currency rates, sink costs, reward values)
Subscription plan or trial changes
Anything touching store metadata or terms
safety_guardrails: Price points are immutable to agents under every mode.
Economy parameters are never autonomous - inflation effects are irreversible for a live economy.
No offer action within 24h of a LiveOps event start (the calendar owns that window).
Restorations must match a prior approved configuration byte-for-byte; any deviation makes it a new offer requiring approval.
No action based on refund data less than 72h old (refunds settle late).
Whale-related actions never target individuals in a way that could be construed as discriminatory pricing.

max_allowed_financial_impact.note: Merchant's autonomous surface is deliberately tiny; its value is detection speed and cause classification, not autonomous commercial decisions.

escalation_rules: Checkout failure -> L2 engineering + L3 monetization within 5 minutes, PagerDuty if projected loss > 0.5% of S_daily/day.
Offer lapse -> L2 monetization PM immediately (median fix time is minutes).
Payer conversion decline > 15% -> L3 + Oracle for pLTV re-estimation.
Economy imbalance -> L3 game economy owner with the sink/source decomposition.

provides_to: Hunter (allowable CPI changes when payer economics shift)

memory_context_requirements.working: current offer inventory and funnel state
memory_context_requirements.episodic: offer performance history, incident history with true causes, whale trajectories
memory_context_requirements.semantic: offer catalog with approved configurations, price ladders by geo, economy design bands, store behavior notes (e.g. 'Google Play billing retries for 30 days; involuntary churn resolves late')
memory_context_requirements.procedural: playbooks: 'checkout incident triage', 'offer lapse restoration', 'payer conversion decomposition', 'whale churn investigation'

feedback_loop.predictions_registered: Expected revenue recovery from each action at +24h/+7d.
feedback_loop.counterfactual_method: Offer holdouts (5% of users excluded from offers by default, permanently, to measure incrementality); synthetic control by geo for configuration changes.
feedback_loop.adaptation: Offer incrementality estimates and price elasticity update the recommendation ranking; the cause classifier retrains on adjudicated incidents.

success_criteria.detection: Checkout failures detected within 10 minutes in >= 95% of cases; offer lapses within 2 hours in 100% of cases.
success_criteria.value: Revenue lost to purchase-flow failures and offer gaps reduced >= 80%; payer conversion regressions detected >= 5 days earlier than the previous manual process.
success_criteria.accuracy: Cause classification correct in >= 85% of adjudicated incidents.

AGT-RET-06.default_mode: Mode 1/2 (Anchor never executes spend actions; it produces the quality signal others act on)
AGT-RET-06.mission: Own the retention curve as the earliest reliable indicator of cohort value: detect within-slice retention degradation before it matures into a ROAS problem, rigorously separate mix effects from real effects, determine whether the cause is acquisition-side or product-side, and quantify the LTV consequence.
data_inputs: fct_cohort_retention (classic and rolling, D0-D90, by full dimension set)
app version and config bundle distribution per cohort (Lab)
kpis_monitored: predicted D7/D30 retention for immature cohorts
retention by ad-exposure and by progression band

monitoring_frequency.cohort_maturation_checks: every 6 hours as cohorts age past each checkpoint
monitoring_frequency.early_signal_predictions: every 6 hours for cohorts aged 0-2 days

detection_logic.rule: slice D1 < 28d baseline - max(2.5pp, 2.5*MAD) with n >= 500, AFTER mix adjustment (recompute holding the dimension composition at baseline). Mix-only movements are emitted as informational findings, never as regressions - this single rule eliminates the most common false-positive class in the whole system.
same construction with max(1.5pp, 2.5*MAD), n >= 500.

predicted D7 for a cohort aged <= 2 days < 0.85 x campaign baseline with the prediction interval excluding the baseline. This fires ~5 days before the actual D7 exists and is Anchor's highest-value output.
fitted decay parameter shifts > 2 sigma vs the slice's trailing 8-cohort distribution - catches cases where D1 is unchanged but the long tail has collapsed, which point metrics miss entirely.

compute the share of affected slices: if > 70% of slices across all sources move together, classify as PRODUCT cause; if concentrated in < 30% of slices sharing an acquisition dimension, classify as ACQUISITION cause. This classification determines who gets the finding and is the difference between cutting good traffic and fixing a broken build.
resurrection rate deviating > 40% from baseline (usually a push campaign, a re-engagement campaign, or a re-attribution config change).

decision_logic.routing_rule: PRODUCT-class findings go to Pulse and Lab, never to Hunter. ACQUISITION-class findings go to Hunter/Prism with the exact slice. Ambiguous classification (30-70% of slices) triggers an orchestrator-coordinated joint investigation rather than a guess.
decision_logic.ltv_translation: Every retention finding is converted into a pLTV delta by Oracle (retention curve -> revenue curve), so the downstream action is sized on money, not on percentage points.
decision_logic.no_action_rule: Anchor deliberately holds no spend-action authority. Its outputs are signals and quantified LTV deltas. This separation prevents a retention agent from cutting campaigns for a product bug.

agent_specific: S_sample uses cohort n at the specific retention day, not total installs.
Mix-adjustment quality is an explicit factor: if the mix adjustment changes the estimate by more than the effect itself, confidence is capped at 0.55 and the finding is labeled mix-dominated.
Early-signal predictions carry the model's own calibrated confidence (AUC-derived), and are capped at 0.75 because they are predictions, not measurements.
-0.15 when the cohort spans an app-version transition (mixed populations).

root_cause_analysis_process: 1. Mix decomposition first, always: split the aggregate change into composition effects and within-slice effects with contributions.
2. Localize the within-slice effect across acquisition, device, geo, version, config and experiment dimensions.
3. Universality test: is this happening to organic users too? Organic is the cleanest control group available - a decline that includes organics is essentially never an acquisition-quality problem.
4. Version/config test: compare the app_version and config-bundle distributions between affected and healthy cohorts.

5. Behavioral test (via Pulse): where in the first session do affected users diverge - are they failing to complete onboarding, or completing it and not returning? These have completely different causes.
6. Creative test (via Muse): are affected cohorts concentrated on specific creatives (expectation mismatch)?
7. Ad-load test (via Vault): did ad exposure for these cohorts change?
8. Retrieve analogues and report which cause proved correct historically for this signature.
actions_it_can_recommend: Emit COHORT_QUALITY_CHANGE with the precise slice and its quantified LTV delta
Recommend throttling specific campaigns/creatives/geos (executed by Hunter)
Recommend lowering bid targets to reflect the lower LTV
Open a product investigation
Trigger a retention experiment
Update slice priors in the pLTV model when a shift persists >= 14 days
Request a re-engagement/CRM push for a high-residual-value cohort

actions_it_can_execute_automatically.bounds: unlimited - this is a data-publishing action with no direct financial effect
max 5 concurrent investigations to bound cost
only after 14 days of persistent deviation and only within +/-15% of the current prior; notifies Oracle and Finance

actions_requiring_human_approval: Any spend action (Anchor has none by design - it routes to Hunter, which applies its own guardrails)
Permanent changes to retention targets or corridors
pLTV prior changes beyond +/-15%
safety_guardrails: Never emits an acquisition-class finding without passing the universality test (protects against blaming UA for product regressions).
Never emits on immature cohorts without labeling the maturity and using the prediction model explicitly.
Mix-adjusted numbers only; raw aggregate movements are never reported as findings.
Minimum n enforced at every retention day.
During staged rollouts, cohorts are split by app version before any comparison.

max_allowed_financial_impact.indirect: Its signals can trigger up to Hunter's limits; the orchestrator attributes downstream impact back to Anchor's finding for accountability.

escalation_rules: PRODUCT-class D1 decline affecting > 50% of installs -> L4 immediately (every hour of delay costs a full day's cohort).
ACQUISITION-class decline on slices carrying > 10% of spend -> L3 Head of UA + orchestrator.
Early-warning breach on a campaign spending > 0.3% of S_daily -> L2 within 15 minutes.
Ambiguous classification unresolved after 2 hours -> orchestrator escalation to L3.

provides_to: Orchestrator (the highest-weight early signal in the whole system)

memory_context_requirements.episodic: every retention finding, its classification, and the adjudicated true cause - the classifier's training set
memory_context_requirements.semantic: retention corridors per slice, seasonal retention patterns (holiday cohorts retain differently), known product events, per-source retention priors
memory_context_requirements.procedural: playbooks: 'mix vs real triage', 'universality test', 'early-warning escalation', 'curve shape investigation'

feedback_loop.predictions_registered: Predicted D7/D30 for immature cohorts; predicted LTV delta from each finding.
feedback_loop.counterfactual_method: Realized retention at maturity is the ground truth for early-signal predictions - a naturally self-labeling loop with a 5-30 day lag.
feedback_loop.adaptation: Early-signal model retrains weekly; classification thresholds (universality percentages) tune monthly against adjudicated outcomes; corridors refresh continuously.

success_criteria.detection: Retention regressions detected at cohort age <= 2 days in >= 65% of cases (vs D7+ manually).
success_criteria.accuracy: Product-vs-acquisition classification correct in >= 85% of adjudicated cases; early-signal D7 prediction MAE <= 2.5pp.
success_criteria.value: Spend on cohorts with confirmed retention regressions reduced within 24h of detection in >= 80% of cases.

AGT-LTV-07.default_mode: Mode 2; Mode 3 only for protective interlocks (suspending dependent autonomy on model drift)
AGT-LTV-07.mission: Be the economic truth function: maintain and monitor the predicted-LTV models, publish P(cohort reaches target ROAS) for every slice, maintain the allowable-CPI table, and act as a system-wide safety interlock when the models cannot be trusted.
data_inputs: behavioral features from the feature store (D0-D7 engagement, monetization events, progression)
finance parameters (store commission, rev share, tax, discount rate)
kpis_monitored: ROAS actual and predicted at every horizon
model MAPE/bias/calibration at D30 and D90

monitoring_frequency.pltv_scoring: every 6 hours for cohorts aged 0-30 days, daily to D180
monitoring_frequency.full_retrain: weekly, with a champion/challenger evaluation before promotion

detection_logic.rule: cohort cumulative ROAS below the corridor P10 for its slice at any checkpoint with spend >= 0.2% of S_daily.
actual cumulative revenue < predicted p10 at the same age for 3 consecutive days - the cleanest quality signal available because it controls for slice and seasonality automatically.
projected payback > 120 days on cohorts representing > 5% of trailing-7d spend.
rolling 14d D30 MAPE > 0.30, OR |bias| > 12% for 7 consecutive days, OR feature PSI > 0.25, OR 80% interval coverage outside [0.70, 0.90].
actual CPI > allowable CPI by > 15% for 3 days on a slice spending > 0.3% of S_daily.
IAP/ad split changes > 10pp for a cohort vs its slice baseline - the total LTV may be unchanged while the payback timing (and therefore the cash decision) changes materially.
top 1% of payers contribute > 55% of a cohort's revenue - the mean LTV is then not a valid basis for scaling and Oracle publishes a median-payer-based allowable CPI instead.

decision_logic.safety_interlock: On confirmed model drift, Oracle immediately publishes MODEL_DEGRADED, which the Warden translates into a fleet-wide demotion of every pLTV-dependent autonomous action to Recommend. This is the most important autonomous action in the system: it is protective, it is triggered by objective statistics, and it prevents the entire fleet from acting on a broken economic model.
decision_logic.prediction_policy: Never publish a point estimate without an interval. Downstream agents must use the interval: scaling decisions use the lower bound, cutting decisions use the upper bound. This asymmetry is enforced in the decision engine, not left to each agent.
decision_logic.allowable_cpi: allowable_CPI(slice) = pLTV_net_at_payback_horizon(slice) * (1 - safety_margin), where safety_margin = 0.10 + 0.5 * (prediction_interval_width / pLTV). Uncertain slices automatically get a bigger margin, which is how model uncertainty becomes a spending constraint rather than a footnote.
decision_logic.maturity_rule: P(target ROAS) is published with a maturity weight: predictions on cohorts younger than D3 blend the model output with the slice prior, weighted by realized-information share.

agent_specific: S_model dominates and is computed directly from the live backtest: calibrated MAPE, interval coverage, and PSI.
Confidence decays with extrapolation distance: a D180 prediction from a D1 cohort is capped at 0.55; from a D30 cohort it can reach 0.85.
-0.20 when attribution certainty for the slice < 0.6 (SKAN-heavy cohorts have systematically noisier revenue attribution).
-0.25 when the cohort is whale-dependent.

root_cause_analysis_process: 1. Decompose the LTV gap: LTV = retention x sessions x (ad_arpdau_component) + payer_conversion x arppu. Attribute the deviation across these factors with contributions.
2. Route each factor to its owner agent (Anchor / Vault / Merchant) and collect their findings before concluding.

3. Distinguish model error from reality: is this cohort deviating from prediction while similar cohorts are on-model (real change), or are all cohorts deviating (model problem)? This test is run automatically before any economic finding is emitted.
4. Check the input data: ULAR reconciliation drift, refund lag, late revenue, attribution restatements - all of which produce fake LTV declines.
5. Feature attribution (SHAP) on the affected cohorts vs a matched healthy set to identify which behavioral inputs shifted.
6. Compare against the 20 nearest historical analogue cohorts and their realized outcomes.
actions_it_can_recommend: Update allowable CPI / target ROAS per slice
Cut or scale spend on economic grounds (executed by Hunter/Ledger)
Change the payback horizon policy (Finance)
Trigger a model retrain or apply a correction factor
Escalate a product/monetization cause instead of an acquisition action
Re-price a slice's bid targets

actions_it_can_execute_automatically.bounds: unlimited - protective, and the highest-priority signal in the system
routine data publication
<= 15% correction to a revenue input when a reconciliation bias is confirmed by Vault/Compass; documented and time-limited to 14 days, after which it must be fixed properly or re-approved
protective; automatically applied when attribution certainty or data quality degrades

actions_requiring_human_approval: Allowable-CPI table changes > 10% (Finance)
Promoting a challenger model to champion (Head of Data)
Payback horizon policy changes (Finance)
Correction factors > 15% or lasting > 14 days
Any change to the revenue definition or rev-share assumptions
safety_guardrails: Never publishes a pLTV used for spending decisions without a current backtest and interval.
Champion/challenger promotion requires: 30-day shadow, better calibrated MAPE on the holdout, no regression in any major slice, and Head of Data sign-off.
Model outputs are versioned and every downstream decision records the model version that produced its inputs, so a bad model's decisions can be identified and reversed en masse.
Correction factors are always time-boxed and visible on the dashboard.
Whale-dependent cohorts are automatically flagged and excluded from mean-LTV-based scaling.

max_allowed_financial_impact.systemic: Oracle's interlock can suspend up to 100% of fleet autonomy - deliberately, because failing closed is the correct behavior when the economic model is untrustworthy.

escalation_rules: Model drift confirmed -> L4 Head of Data + VP Growth immediately, with the fleet demotion already applied.
Payback breach on > 5% of spend -> L4 Finance + VP Growth.
Systematic bias detected in a slice carrying > 15% of spend -> L3 + retrain scheduled.
Interval coverage failure (model overconfident) -> L3, and intervals are widened immediately as a stopgap.

provides_to: Everyone - Oracle's P(target ROAS) and allowable CPI are inputs to Hunter, Ledger, Muse, Prophet and the orchestrator's objective function
The orchestrator's global objective function is evaluated using Oracle's outputs
dependencies_on_other_agents.criticality: Highest fan-out in the fleet; its degradation is a system-wide event.

memory_context_requirements.episodic: every prediction and its realized outcome (the model's own evaluation set), every correction factor and its justification
memory_context_requirements.semantic: slice priors, seasonal LTV patterns, monetization profiles by genre/geo, finance parameters and their effective dates
memory_context_requirements.procedural: playbooks: 'drift triage', 'model vs reality test', 'correction factor application', 'challenger evaluation'

feedback_loop.predictions_registered: Every pLTV prediction is a registered prediction with a natural ground truth at maturity.
feedback_loop.counterfactual_method: Not needed for prediction accuracy (realized values are observed); needed only for the impact of Oracle-triggered actions, measured via the standard synthetic-control approach.

AGT-COH-08.mission: Maintain the cohort substrate the whole system reasons on: build and validate cohorts across the full dimension space, publish the D0 cohort quality index, detect composition shifts that masquerade as performance changes, and find the nearest historical analogues that tell us how a young cohort is likely to end.
data_inputs: fct_installs with the full attribution and device dimension set
fct_cohort_daily (behavior, revenue, retention by cohort age)
kpis_monitored: cohort size and composition by every dimension
cohort maturity and realized-vs-extrapolated value share

monitoring_frequency.cohort_materialization: every 15 minutes for D0, every 6 hours for maturing cohorts

detection_logic.rule: source-level index < 28d mean - 2 sigma with n >= 500 installs/day. Built from D0-only features (session count, session duration, core-loop completions, D0 ad impressions, D0 revenue, tutorial completion), so it is available the same day - the earliest quality signal the system has.

the device/geo/os/placement mix inside a campaign's cohort shifts > 15pp week over week (Jensen-Shannon divergence > 0.08). Network optimizers silently change who they buy; this detects it before the performance consequence appears.
cohort tracking > 25% below the median of its 20 nearest historical analogues at the same age - a model-free check that catches pLTV model failures as well as genuine cohort problems.
top 1% payer revenue share > 55% - blocks mean-LTV-based scaling decisions on that cohort.
any agent request for a decision on a slice below the metric's minimum n - Prism returns a hard refusal that the Warden enforces.
weekly discovery pass finds a dimension combination explaining > 25% of variance in cohort ROAS that is not currently used in targeting or bidding.

decision_logic.service_role: Prism is primarily a service: it answers 'what is this cohort, is it comparable, is it big enough, what did similar cohorts do'. Its autonomous authority is limited to publishing signals and blocking statistically invalid decisions.
decision_logic.blocking_authority: Prism can veto any agent action whose supporting cohort fails the sample-adequacy or whale-dependency test. This veto is enforced at the Action Gateway and cannot be overridden below VP Growth.
decision_logic.mix_adjustment_service: Every other agent requests mix-adjusted metrics from Prism rather than computing them, so mix handling is consistent system-wide.

agent_specific: Quality-index findings are capped at 0.75 (it is a leading indicator built on proxies, not an outcome).

Analogue-based findings scale confidence with analogue similarity (mean cosine similarity of the top-20) and with the analogues' outcome variance - tight, similar analogues can reach 0.85; dispersed ones cap at 0.55.

root_cause_analysis_process: 1. Decompose any cohort metric change into composition and within-composition effects (the canonical mix decomposition used fleet-wide).
2. Identify which dimension values drive the composition shift and trace them to a network-side change, a targeting change, or a budget change (join the action log).
3. For quality-index drops, identify which D0 features moved and route to the owning agent (tutorial completion -> Pulse; D0 ad impressions -> Vault; session depth -> Pulse/Muse).
4. Retrieve nearest analogues and report what happened to them and what actions were taken.
5. Test whether the cohort's dimension distribution is inside the training distribution of the pLTV model; if not, flag extrapolation risk to Oracle.
actions_it_can_recommend: Publish COHORT_QUALITY_CHANGE with a precise slice and quantified delta
Recommend slice-scoped budget actions (executed by Hunter)
Recommend targeting changes to capture or exclude a discovered segment
Feed corrected slice priors to Oracle
Create CRM/re-engagement segments for high-residual-value cohorts
Block a scale decision on statistical grounds

unlimited - protective and mechanical
unlimited (read-only artifacts)

Changing cohort definitions used by finance reporting
Changing the quality index composition or weights

Minimum-n rules are non-negotiable and enforced centrally.
Privacy: user-level drill-downs are pseudonymized, sampled, access-logged, and unavailable for users in jurisdictions or consent states that forbid it.
Cardinality guard: cohort builds exceeding 10k groups are rejected to prevent multiple-comparison fishing; discovery passes apply FDR correction.

Composition shift on a campaign spending > 0.5% of S_daily -> L2 Hunter (the network has changed what it is buying).
Repeated sample-adequacy vetoes against one agent -> L2 to the platform team (indicates that agent is over-slicing).

provides_to: Every agent - Prism is the shared cohort service
Anchor and Oracle depend on it for mix-adjusted inputs

memory_context_requirements.semantic: cohort definitions and versions, dimension hierarchies, minimum-n rules per metric, known composition patterns per network
memory_context_requirements.procedural: playbooks: 'mix decomposition', 'analogue retrieval', 'quality index triage', 'segment discovery with FDR control'
