AGT-ATT-09.default_mode: Mode 2; Mode 3 for fraud blocklisting and for suspending autonomy on measurement failure
AGT-ATT-09.mission: Guarantee the trustworthiness of the acquisition data everything else depends on: reconcile MMP, network, store and internal counts; detect and act on fraud; manage SKAN/AAK modeling quality; maintain incrementality multipliers; and suspend downstream autonomy when measurement itself is broken.
data_inputs: MMP raw installs, in-app events, and re-attributions (AppsFlyer/Adjust)
SKAN/AAK postbacks with conversion values and crowd-anonymity tiers
click and impression logs with timestamps (CTIT computation)
kpis_monitored: MMP vs network discrepancy by network/geo/platform
SKAN postback coverage and null-CV rate

monitoring_frequency.fraud_scan: every 6 hours (and immediately on a volume spike)
monitoring_frequency.multiplier_refresh: weekly or on new test results

detection_logic.rule: |MMP - network|/network > 15% for a network with >= 3% install share, sustained 3 days. Investigation order is fixed and mechanical: attribution window mismatch -> SDK version change -> dedup rule change -> click-time vs impression-time attribution -> timezone misalignment -> fraud rejection -> genuine reporting error.
CTIT distribution mass below 10 seconds > 3x the network's healthy baseline, concentrated in specific sub-publishers with volume >= 200 installs/day.
click volume per install > 5x network median with a flat, long CTIT tail and abnormally low CVR.
new-device ratio > 0.9, low IP entropy, implausible sensor/behavioral profiles, and near-zero D1 retention in the affected sub-publisher's cohort.
coverage down > 20% vs 14d baseline -> iOS measurement failure; triggers an immediate suspension of iOS-dependent autonomous actions.
deterministic share down > 10pp week over week -> widens every downstream confidence interval.
organic installs down > 15% while paid up > 25% in the same geo/title, outside the modeled uplift band -> true incremental CPI is materially higher than reported.
self-attributing-network claims exceed MMP attribution by > 20%.

decision_logic.fraud_rule: Fraud actions are protective and reversible, so they carry a broader autonomous grant than performance actions. Blocklisting a sub-publisher with confidence >= 0.85 is autonomous; the claw-back claim packet is generated automatically but filed by a human.
decision_logic.measurement_interlock: When measurement quality for a channel drops below threshold, Compass publishes MEASUREMENT_DEGRADED for that scope, and the Warden suspends autonomous economic actions on that channel. Acting on unmeasurable channels is how autonomous systems destroy money invisibly.
decision_logic.multiplier_policy: Incrementality multipliers change reported ROAS for every downstream decision, so they are never autonomous - they require Head of Data approval and a version record with an effective date, and all historical decisions retain the multiplier version they used.

agent_specific: Fraud findings gain confidence from independent signal agreement: CTIT anomaly + retention collapse + device-ratio anomaly together can reach 0.92; any single signal alone is capped at 0.60.
Discrepancy findings are capped at 0.70 until the mechanical investigation order has eliminated configuration causes (configuration explains the majority of discrepancies).
SKAN-related findings carry a structural uncertainty penalty of -0.10 because the ground truth is unobservable by design.

root_cause_analysis_process: 1. Run the fixed mechanical checklist for configuration causes before considering fraud or genuine performance causes.
2. Localize the discrepancy by campaign, geo, day, hour, and sub-publisher.
3. Compare the affected cohort's behavioral profile against known-good cohorts (fraudulent installs have distinctive near-zero engagement signatures).
4. Check network changelogs and SDK release notes over the changepoint window (Scout).
5. Cross-validate with store first-open counts, which are the most independent count available.
6. For SKAN issues, examine the conversion-value schema, tier distribution, and postback timing separately - they fail in different ways.
7. Quantify the financial exposure: how much spend was allocated based on the mis-measured installs.
actions_it_can_recommend: Blocklist sub-publishers
File claw-back claims
Change SKAN conversion-value schema
Change attribution windows or dedup rules
Apply or update incrementality multipliers
Suspend autonomy for a channel
Launch an incrementality test
Escalate to the network's account team

actions_it_can_execute_automatically.bounds: confidence >= 0.85 with >= 2 independent fraud signals; affected spend <= 0.5% of S_daily; reversible; notifies immediately
actions_it_can_execute_automatically.rationale: protective; the counterfactual is continuing to pay for fake installs

actions_it_can_execute_automatically.bounds: unlimited - protective interlock
unlimited (document generation, filed by a human)
protective; propagates to Oracle's intervals

actions_requiring_human_approval: Attribution window / dedup / SKAN schema changes (they reset measurement continuity and invalidate historical comparisons)
Incrementality multiplier changes (Head of Data)
Blocklisting an entire network or a sub-publisher above 0.5% of S_daily
Filing claims with networks
Any change to the definition of organic
safety_guardrails: Never changes measurement configuration autonomously - a measurement change is not reversible in its effect on historical comparability.
Fraud blocklists require multi-signal corroboration; single-signal blocklists are Recommend only.
Blocklist actions are capped per day to avoid a cascade that collapses delivery.
Every blocklist carries an automatic 30-day review to prevent permanent blocks on recovered publishers.
SKAN modeled data is always labeled and never silently blended with deterministic data in any decision.

max_allowed_financial_impact.systemic: The measurement interlock can suspend channel-level autonomy entirely - intended behavior.

escalation_rules: SKAN postback collapse -> L4 immediately (iOS decision-making is blind until resolved).
Fraud with exposure > 0.5% of S_daily -> L3 Head of UA + Finance (claw-back has a filing deadline).
Discrepancy > 25% on a major network -> L3 + the network account team.
Organic cannibalization confirmed -> L4 (it changes the profitability of the entire channel).

consumes_from: Anchor (retention of suspect cohorts - fraudulent cohorts have near-zero retention)

memory_context_requirements.episodic: every discrepancy incident and its resolved cause; every blocklist and its outcome
memory_context_requirements.semantic: per-network attribution behavior and known quirks, historical fraud patterns and their signatures, SKAN schema versions and their effective dates, multiplier history
memory_context_requirements.procedural: playbooks: 'discrepancy checklist', 'fraud confirmation', 'SKAN health triage', 'claw-back packet'

feedback_loop.predictions_registered: Expected discrepancy reduction and spend savings after each blocklist.
feedback_loop.counterfactual_method: Post-blocklist cohort quality vs pre-blocklist for the same campaign; network-confirmed claw-back amounts are direct ground truth.
feedback_loop.adaptation: Fraud detector thresholds tune from confirmed cases; the configuration-cause checklist reorders by observed frequency.

success_criteria.detection: Fraud detected within 48h of onset in >= 85% of confirmed cases; discrepancy causes correctly classified in >= 80%.
success_criteria.safety: Zero autonomous economic decisions executed on channels with degraded measurement.

AGT-FCT-10.default_mode: Mode 1/2 (forecasts and scenarios; no direct execution)
AGT-FCT-10.mission: Produce and continuously validate the forward view - spend, installs, revenue, DAU, margin and cash - at portfolio and segment grain, detect when reality is leaving the forecast, and distinguish a model failure from a business change.
data_inputs: all historical fact tables (spend, installs, revenue, DAU, retention)
planned budget envelopes and scheduled campaign changes (Ledger)
cohort retention and revenue curves (Anchor, Oracle)
seasonality calendar (holidays per geo, sales events, LiveOps calendar, release schedule)
known upcoming product launches and experiments (Lab)
kpis_monitored: forecast MAPE by horizon (7/14/30/90d) and by segment

monitoring_frequency.forecast_refresh: hourly for intraday spend/revenue, daily 05:00 UTC for full hierarchical refresh
monitoring_frequency.accuracy_evaluation: daily (every forecast that matured today is scored)

detection_logic.rule: actual outside the 95% prediction interval for 2 consecutive periods.

On a breach, test whether residuals are systematic across segments (a model problem) or isolated to specific segments (a business change). This test decides whether the output is a retrain ticket or a business incident, and getting it wrong wastes days.
rolling 14d MAPE > 1.5x validation MAPE, or interval coverage outside [0.85, 0.99] for the 95% band.

changepoint detected in a series' generating process (level, trend or variance) with posterior > 0.85 -> the pre-break history must be down-weighted or the model will keep predicting a world that no longer exists.
a known seasonal event within 14 days with no corresponding plan adjustment.

decision_logic.hierarchical_reconciliation: Forecasts are produced at campaign, title and portfolio level and reconciled with MinT so the levels are mutually consistent; unreconciled forecasts produce contradictory recommendations at different altitudes.
decision_logic.model_ensemble: Weighted ensemble of: SARIMAX with exogenous regressors (spend, CPM index, seasonality), gradient-boosted trees on engineered calendar/lag features, a structural cohort-accumulation model (DAU and revenue derived from cohort curves rather than extrapolated directly), and a naive seasonal baseline. Weights are set per series by rolling backtest performance. The cohort-accumulation model is the primary one for revenue because it is causally correct - revenue comes from cohorts, not from a time series.
decision_logic.uncertainty_policy: Intervals come from conformal prediction on the rolling backtest residuals, not from model-internal variance, so they are empirically calibrated.
decision_logic.breach_response: A breach is never auto-resolved as 'the model is wrong'. The discrimination test runs first, and a business-change verdict opens an incident routed to the owning agent.

agent_specific: S_model = 1 - normalized rolling MAPE, scaled by interval coverage accuracy.
Confidence decays with horizon: 30-day forecasts cap at 0.75, 90-day at 0.60.
-0.20 when a structural break was detected in the last 30 days (limited post-break history).
-0.15 during periods with known unmodeled events (new title launch, major platform change).

root_cause_analysis_process: 1. Decompose the forecast error by segment and by component (volume vs rate).
2. Run the model-vs-reality discrimination test.
3. For business changes, identify which input assumption broke (spend path, CPM, retention curve, monetization rate) and route to the owning agent.
4. For model problems, diagnose: feature drift, structural break, regime change, or an unmodeled exogenous event.
5. Check whether a known event was missing from the seasonality calendar (the most common and most fixable cause).
6. Backtest the corrected model on the breach window to verify the diagnosis before promoting a fix.
actions_it_can_recommend: Retrain or reweight the ensemble
Add a missing event to the seasonality calendar
Flag a business change to the owning agent
Adjust plan assumptions
Run a scenario analysis for a proposed decision
Widen intervals pending recalibration

actions_it_can_execute_automatically.bounds: routine
protective; automatic when coverage fails
automatic on degradation triggers; the new model still requires champion/challenger evaluation before promotion
only for events confirmed by an external source (holiday calendars, store featuring notifications); anything inferred requires approval

actions_requiring_human_approval: Promoting a challenger forecasting model
Changing plan assumptions used by Finance
Manual overrides of the forecast (allowed, but recorded as an override with an owner and a reason, and scored against the model afterwards)
safety_guardrails: Forecasts used for financial commitments always carry intervals and an accuracy badge; a point forecast never leaves the system naked.
Manual overrides are versioned and scored - a human override that proves worse than the model is visible in the audit.
No forecast is published for a series with < 60 days of history without an explicit low-confidence label.
Structural breaks force interval widening until sufficient post-break history accumulates.

max_allowed_financial_impact.indirect: Forecasts drive Ledger's allocation and Finance's envelopes; a bad forecast is systemically expensive, which is why accuracy monitoring is aggressive and interval calibration is empirical.

escalation_rules: Month-end margin forecast below plan with P > 0.6 -> L4 CMO + Finance.
Forecast accuracy degradation on portfolio-level series -> L3 Head of Data.
Structural break in a core series -> L3 + orchestrator (something material changed in the business).
Repeated breaches in the same segment -> L2 to the owning agent (the business change is real and unaddressed).

consumes_from: Anchor/Oracle (cohort curves - the causal backbone of revenue forecasts)
provides_to: Sentinel (forecast bands are used as anomaly baselines)

memory_context_requirements.episodic: every forecast ever made with its realized outcome (the forecast registry) - this is what makes accuracy claims auditable rather than asserted
memory_context_requirements.semantic: seasonality calendars per geo, known structural breaks and their dates, model configurations and their performance history
memory_context_requirements.procedural: playbooks: 'breach discrimination', 'structural break handling', 'scenario construction'

feedback_loop.predictions_registered: Every forecast at every horizon is a registered prediction, scored automatically at maturity.
feedback_loop.counterfactual_method: Not applicable - forecasts have direct ground truth.
feedback_loop.adaptation: Ensemble weights update weekly from rolling backtests; conformal interval widths recalibrate continuously; the seasonality calendar accumulates learned events.

success_criteria.accuracy: Portfolio revenue MAPE <= 6% at 7d, <= 12% at 30d; spend MAPE <= 4% at 7d; interval coverage within +/-4pp of nominal.
success_criteria.discrimination: Model-vs-business classification correct in >= 85% of breaches.
success_criteria.value: Zero month-end budget surprises > 5%; forecasts trusted enough to drive automated allocation (measured by the share of Ledger packages accepted).

AGT-ANO-11.default_mode: Mode 1 (detect and localize only - Sentinel never acts on the business)
AGT-ANO-11.mission: Watch everything, cry wolf almost never: run the tiered detector ensemble across ~7.2M series, localize each real change in time and dimension space, suppress everything explainable by known events or market conditions, and hand a clean, deduplicated, pre-localized incident to the right domain agent.
data_inputs: every materialized metric series in the semantic layer (the detection substrate)
known-event suppression calendar (releases, experiments, config changes, holidays, network maintenance, LiveOps)
kpis_monitored: all monitored series (it is metric-agnostic by design)
its own operational KPIs: detection latency, precision, alert volume, detector agreement, suppression hit rate, cost per pass

detection_logic.ensemble: See modules_data.anomaly_detection.detector_ensemble for the seven detectors and their parameters.
detection_logic.emission_rule: Emit only when: (>= 2 detectors agree) OR (an invariant is violated) OR (a single detector at |z| > 5); AND the materiality gate passes (estimated impact >= 0.05% of S_daily/day, or the series is portfolio-level); AND the peer-relative check confirms entity-specificity or explicitly labels it market-wide; AND no suppression rule covers it; AND the fingerprint is not in cooldown.
detection_logic.localization: Every emission carries: changepoint timestamp with a credible interval, the minimal dimension set explaining >= 70% of the change with per-value contributions, the peer-relative verdict, and an estimated 7/14/30-day impact if unaddressed.
detection_logic.hierarchy_rule: When a parent metric and its children all fire, emit only the highest node that fully explains the change, attaching children as evidence. This turns what would be 40 alerts into 1.

decision_logic.routing: Each anomaly is routed by metric family to its owning agent, with severity computed from impact x confidence. Clusters of >= 5 correlated anomalies within 30 minutes are escalated to the orchestrator as a single incident rather than routed individually.
decision_logic.no_diagnosis_rule: Sentinel deliberately does not diagnose causes. Detection and diagnosis have different failure modes and different owners; conflating them produces confident wrong stories. Sentinel's job ends at 'what changed, when, where, how much'.

agent_specific: S_stat = normalized detector consensus strength (fraction agreeing, weighted by each detector's historical precision on this metric family).
S_corroboration includes the peer-relative test result as a first-class input.
-0.25 if the affected series had a data-quality event in the window (a partial load looks exactly like a decline).
-0.15 if a suppression rule partially matches (a known event overlaps but the magnitude exceeds expectation).

root_cause_analysis_process: Sentinel performs localization, not causation: (1) changepoint estimation, (2) dimension contribution attribution, (3) peer-relative classification (entity-specific vs market-wide), (4) correlated-series identification (which other metrics moved in the same window - handed over as leads, not conclusions), (5) suppression matching against known events, (6) impact projection. The causal work is done by the owning domain agent or by Sherlock.
actions_it_can_recommend: Route a localized anomaly to a domain agent
Open an incident
Quarantine a data slice (invariant violations)
Apply a suppression rule for a known event
Propose a detector or threshold change with historical simulation

actions_it_can_execute_automatically.bounds: rate-limited by the anti-fatigue budget: max 6 non-Sev-1 per hour per channel, overflow batched
automatic for clusters and Sev-1/2
protective; blocks agent decisions on structurally impossible data
only for pre-registered events with a pre-declared expected direction and magnitude - suppression never hides a change larger than the registered expectation

actions_requiring_human_approval: Permanent threshold changes
Adding a new suppression rule not tied to a registered event
Disabling monitoring for a series (requires a documented reason and an expiry date)
safety_guardrails: Suppression can never hide a Sev-1 or an invariant violation.
Suppression rules expire automatically; permanent suppressions require quarterly review.
Threshold changes must be simulated against 90 days of history and against the known-incident set before proposal - a threshold that would have missed a past real incident is rejected.
Sentinel cannot disable monitoring on portfolio-level KPIs under any circumstance.
Detector changes are shadow-deployed for 14 days alongside the incumbent.

max_allowed_financial_impact.note: Its risk is entirely informational: false negatives cost money silently, false positives cost attention and cause wrong actions downstream. Both are tracked as first-class KPIs.

escalation_rules: Anomaly cluster with combined impact > 1% of S_daily/day -> orchestrator immediately as a Sev-1 incident.
Invariant violation -> L2 data engineering immediately.
Detection blind spot found post-hoc -> L3 platform team with a regression test case attached.
Alert volume exceeding the fatigue budget for 3 consecutive hours -> L2 (the system is being noisy and trust is being burned).

consumes_from: Janitor (data health - critical, because most 'anomalies' in immature systems are data problems)

memory_context_requirements.episodic: every anomaly, its adjudicated verdict (true/false positive), and the eventual cause - the precision measurement substrate
memory_context_requirements.semantic: per-series baselines, volatility profiles, seasonal patterns, peer-group memberships, known event patterns
memory_context_requirements.procedural: detector configurations and their per-metric-family performance

feedback_loop.predictions_registered: Each anomaly registers a projected impact if unaddressed, which is scored against the realized trajectory (for anomalies that were not acted upon, this is a clean natural experiment).
feedback_loop.counterfactual_method: For acted-upon anomalies, the domain agent's measurement provides the counterfactual; for unaddressed ones, the realized series is direct evidence about whether the anomaly mattered.
feedback_loop.adaptation: Detector weights per metric family update from precision outcomes; thresholds adapt per series; suppression rules learn expected magnitudes for recurring events.

success_criteria.latency: p50 detection latency <= 20 minutes for T1 series, <= 90 minutes for T2.
success_criteria.recall: >= 90% of post-hoc-identified material incidents were detected proactively.
success_criteria.hygiene: Alert volume within the fatigue budget >= 95% of hours; duplicate rate < 3%.

AGT-PRD-12.default_mode: Mode 2; Mode 3 only for protective config reverts within an allowlist
AGT-PRD-12.mission: Detect and explain in-app behavioral changes fast enough to protect the cohorts being acquired right now: release regressions, funnel breaks, progression walls, and engagement shifts - and translate each into its retention and LTV consequence.
data_inputs: client and server event streams (sessions, funnel steps, progression, feature usage, errors)
remote config bundles and change history (Lab)
performance telemetry (load times, frame rates, network errors)
kpis_monitored: onboarding step conversion and step timing (p50/p90)

monitoring_frequency.realtime_health: every 5 minutes (crashes, funnel steps, session starts)
monitoring_frequency.release_comparison: every 3 hours during staged rollouts, daily otherwise

detection_logic.rule: any step's conversion down > 5pp vs 14d baseline for the version-adjusted population with n >= 2000. Sev-1 because it damages every cohort acquired from that moment forward, and UA is still spending.
p90 step time up > 50% with conversion flat - a performance regression that will become a conversion regression as it spreads to slower devices.
crash-free session rate < 99.0% or ANR up 3x, at adoption >= 5%.
sessions/DAU down > 8% vs weekday-matched 28d baseline for 2 days.
down > 6% for a specific app_version or config bundle.
a stage whose drop-off exceeds 2.5x the median stage drop-off with volume >= 5000 players/day.
session time up > 5% while ARPDAU down > 5% over 7 days - usually an ad or paywall placement regression masquerading as an engagement win.
a version-comparison scorecard across 20 core metrics at matched days-since-install, with a composite verdict; catches regressions that no single metric would flag.

decision_logic.rollout_gate: During a staged rollout, Pulse computes a release health verdict every 3 hours. A failing verdict recommends halting the rollout - which is the single highest-value product action in the system because it caps the blast radius at the current adoption percentage.
decision_logic.config_revert_rule: If a regression's changepoint aligns with a remote-config change within +/-30 minutes and the affected population matches the config's targeting, Pulse may autonomously revert that parameter if it is on the allowlist and its blast-radius class is low. Config reverts are cheap, instant, and fully reversible - the ideal autonomous action.
decision_logic.ltv_translation: Every finding is translated into a projected retention and LTV delta via Anchor and Oracle, so product regressions are prioritized in dollars against UA and monetization issues rather than in percentage points.

agent_specific: +0.15 when the changepoint aligns within 30 minutes of a known release or config change AND the affected population matches that change's targeting (a near-deterministic causal link).
-0.20 when multiple changes shipped in the same window (confounded).
Device/OS-specific findings require n >= 2000 in the affected segment; below that, cap at 0.6.

root_cause_analysis_process: 1. Localize to the exact funnel step or behavioral event that moved, using step-level conversion and timing.
2. Segment by app_version, config bundle, device_tier, OS version, geo - a regression confined to one segment names its own cause.
3. Align the changepoint against the deployment timeline: app releases, staged rollout percentages, config changes, backend deploys, experiment starts, third-party SDK updates.
4. Separate performance from design: timing distributions distinguish 'slower' from 'harder'.
5. Test the acquisition-mix hypothesis (via Prism): are these different users rather than a changed experience? This must be ruled out before blaming the product.
6. For monetization-adjacent regressions, check ad and paywall exposure changes (Vault, Merchant).
7. Produce a code-owner routing suggestion from the affected event's ownership map.
actions_it_can_recommend: Halt or roll back a staged release
Revert or adjust a remote config parameter
Launch an A/B test on the affected step
Adjust difficulty or economy parameters (design review required)
File an engineering ticket with the evidence bundle and code-owner routing
Notify UA to throttle spend while a regression is live (via COHORT_QUALITY_CHANGE)

actions_it_can_execute_automatically.bounds: parameter on the allowlist with blast-radius class 'low' or 'medium'; changepoint aligned within 30 min; confidence >= 0.85; affected users <= 25% of DAU; auto-notifies the owning PM; reverts to the immediately prior value only
signal only - Hunter decides and executes under its own guardrails
unlimited (ticket creation)

actions_requiring_human_approval: Halting or rolling back an app release (engineering owns deployment)
Any config change that is not a revert to a prior value
Economy or difficulty parameter changes (never autonomous - irreversible player-facing effects)
Any change during a marketing beat or featuring window
safety_guardrails: Config reverts only ever restore a previous known-good value; Pulse cannot invent a new value.
Never autonomously changes anything affecting the game economy, monetization pricing, or player-visible content.
No config action within 15 minutes of another config change (avoids thrashing during an active human deployment).
Release-related findings are always version-segmented; comparing mixed-version populations is prohibited.
During a staged rollout, comparisons must control for the self-selection of early adopters (auto-update users differ systematically).

max_allowed_financial_impact.per_action: Config reverts have no direct spend; modeled revenue exposure per action capped at 0.5% of daily revenue
max_allowed_financial_impact.per_agent_per_day: 2 autonomous config reverts per title per day
max_allowed_financial_impact.note: Pulse's leverage is speed: catching an onboarding regression 6 hours earlier is typically worth more than any budget action available to the fleet.

escalation_rules: Onboarding regression affecting > 50% of installs -> L4 + PagerDuty immediately, and simultaneously notify Hunter to consider spend throttling (do not wait for the fix).
Crash spike -> L2 engineering + halt-rollout recommendation within 5 minutes.
Any regression whose projected 30-day LTV impact > 1% of S_daily x 30 -> L4.
Config drift with no owner -> L3 + governance finding.

consumes_from: Lab (config and experiment context - essential; without it Pulse cannot align causes)

memory_context_requirements.working: current version adoption and release health state
memory_context_requirements.episodic: every release, its health verdict, and its realized retention/LTV effect - builds the release-risk prior
memory_context_requirements.semantic: funnel definitions and their owners, historical regression patterns per platform, device-tier performance profiles, event-to-code-owner mapping
memory_context_requirements.procedural: playbooks: 'release regression triage', 'config alignment test', 'performance vs design discrimination', 'staged rollout gate'

feedback_loop.predictions_registered: Projected retention and LTV impact of each regression; expected recovery after each revert.
feedback_loop.counterfactual_method: Version-holdout comparison (users still on the prior version are a natural control during staged rollouts - the cleanest control group in the whole system); config reverts create clean before/after with the unaffected population as control.
feedback_loop.adaptation: Release-risk priors update per release type; detection thresholds tune per funnel step; the config-alignment heuristic's precision is tracked explicitly.

success_criteria.detection: Release regressions detected at < 15% adoption in >= 80% of cases (capping blast radius).
success_criteria.speed: Median time from regression start to detection <= 90 minutes; to config revert (where applicable) <= 20 minutes.
success_criteria.accuracy: Cause attribution (release / config / mix / external) correct in >= 85% of adjudicated cases.
success_criteria.value: Cohort LTV lost to undetected product regressions reduced >= 70% vs the pre-MART baseline.

AGT-EXP-13.default_mode: Mode 2; Mode 3 for protective guardrail stops and drift reverts
AGT-EXP-13.mission: Keep the experimentation and configuration surface trustworthy and safe: guarantee experiment validity, stop variants that breach guardrails, maintain the config source of truth, and provide every other agent with the change context they need to attribute causes correctly.
data_inputs: experiment definitions, assignments and exposure logs
remote config bundles, versions, targeting rules and change history
metric readouts per variant (from the semantic layer)
guardrail metric definitions and pre-registered thresholds
config service live state (for drift detection)
kpis_monitored: primary metric effect and CI per experiment

monitoring_frequency.readouts: daily, and on reaching pre-registered sample size

detection_logic.rule: chi-square p < 0.001 on assignment ratios -> the experiment is invalid and every conclusion from it must be blocked, not merely caveated.
any pre-registered guardrail metric (crash rate, D1 retention, ARPDAU, session length, checkout success) degrades beyond its threshold with p < 0.05 and a practically significant effect size.
live config value != declared source-of-truth value for > 15 minutes.
a config change with no linked ticket, experiment, or agent action record.
two running experiments modify overlapping parameters on overlapping audiences without orthogonal layer assignment -> both readouts are confounded.
the effect in the first 3 days of exposure differs from later exposure by > 50% -> the readout is premature.
running > 45 days without a decision (occupying traffic and blocking other tests).

decision_logic.stop_rule: Guardrail breaches trigger an automatic variant stop. This is one of the few default-on autonomous actions in the system because it is strictly protective, instantly reversible, and the cost of waiting for a human is measured in damaged users.
decision_logic.readout_rule: No experiment is declared a winner on the primary metric alone; the decision object includes guardrails, segment heterogeneity (with FDR correction), novelty check, and an LTV translation via Oracle. A primary-metric win with a negative net LTV effect is reported as a loss.
decision_logic.traffic_policy: Lab manages the experiment layer allocation and refuses new experiments that would confound running ones.

agent_specific: Experiment findings inherit statistical confidence directly from the test (posterior probability or 1 - p), which makes Lab the best-calibrated agent in the fleet.
-0.30 on any SRM-flagged experiment (invalid).
-0.20 when novelty effects are detected.
Config drift findings are near-deterministic and can reach 0.95.

root_cause_analysis_process: 1. For SRM: check assignment service logs, bucketing hash, targeting rule changes, and client-side filtering (the usual causes, in that order).
2. For guardrail breaches: segment the effect to find whether it is universal or concentrated, and check for interaction with other running experiments.
3. For config drift: diff live vs declared, identify the actor from the config service audit log, and check whether a rollout is stuck mid-propagation.
4. For unexpected metric moves during an experiment: verify the exposure population matches the intended targeting before attributing the effect to the treatment.
actions_it_can_recommend: Ship, kill, or extend an experiment
Ramp exposure
Re-randomize a confounded experiment
Change a config parameter within its declared safe range
Revert to a prior config version
Restructure the experiment layer allocation

actions_it_can_execute_automatically.bounds: pre-registered guardrail with p < 0.05 and practical significance; confidence >= 0.85; notifies the owner immediately
restores the declared source-of-truth value; only when the drift has no linked change record; confidence >= 0.90
SRM or overlap detection; blocks downstream decisions based on it
protective scheduling action

actions_requiring_human_approval: Shipping a variant to 100%
Starting a new experiment
Any config change that is not a revert
Changing guardrail thresholds
Extending an experiment beyond its planned duration
safety_guardrails: Never ships a variant autonomously (shipping is a permanent product decision).
Config changes are limited to the declared allowlist with type and range validation, and every change is a new immutable version.
Blast-radius classification is mandatory before any config action; unclassified parameters are human-only.
Experiment stops are variant-level, never experiment-level, so control is preserved for measurement.
All changes propagate through the same versioned config service with staged rollout (1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100%) unless it is a revert, which propagates immediately.

max_allowed_financial_impact.note: Stopping a harmful variant has negative cost - the risk being managed is stopping a good variant prematurely, which the practical-significance requirement mitigates.

escalation_rules: Guardrail breach with crash or checkout impact -> L2 engineering + L3 product immediately.
SRM on an experiment informing a shipped decision -> L3 (a decision may have been made on invalid data - previous conclusions need review).
Config drift with a material metric impact -> L3 + governance finding (someone is changing production outside the system).
Repeated unattributed changes -> L4 (a governance failure, not a technical one).

provides_to: Every agent - Lab's change log is the alignment substrate for all root-cause analysis. Without it, agents cannot distinguish 'we changed something' from 'the world changed'.

memory_context_requirements.episodic: the full experiment archive with results, decisions and realized post-ship effects (so the same test is not re-run and shipped effects can be verified against test predictions)
memory_context_requirements.semantic: config parameter catalog with types, ranges, blast-radius classes and owners; guardrail definitions; layer topology
memory_context_requirements.procedural: playbooks: 'SRM triage', 'guardrail stop', 'drift revert', 'readout construction'

feedback_loop.predictions_registered: Predicted effect of shipping each winning variant, scored against post-ship reality (a persistent gap between test lift and shipped lift is a critical, commonly-ignored measurement finding).
feedback_loop.counterfactual_method: The experiment's own control arm; post-ship, a holdout population retained for 30 days where feasible.
feedback_loop.adaptation: Post-ship-vs-test discrepancy tracking calibrates future effect-size expectations; guardrail thresholds tune from historical false stops.

success_criteria.validity: Zero decisions made on SRM-invalid experiments; overlap conflicts detected before start in 100% of cases.
success_criteria.safety: Guardrail breaches stopped within 60 minutes of statistical detection in >= 95% of cases.
success_criteria.hygiene: Config drift resolved within 30 minutes; unattributed changes < 1 per month.
success_criteria.velocity: Experiment throughput +40% through automated readouts and conflict prevention.

AGT-DQ-14.agent_name: Janitor - Data Quality & Pipeline Observability Agent
AGT-DQ-14.default_mode: Mode 3 by default for protective gating actions (this agent's autonomy makes the rest of the fleet safe)
AGT-DQ-14.mission: Be the gate between data and decisions: verify freshness, completeness, schema and contract compliance for every dataset, quantify restatement risk, and hard-block agent actions whose lineage is unhealthy.
data_inputs: pipeline orchestration metadata (run status, duration, row counts)
dataset freshness timestamps and partition states
kpis_monitored: freshness lag vs SLO per dataset
pipeline run success rate and duration
restatement magnitude by source and age

monitoring_frequency.restatement_tracking: daily, comparing each partition's current state to its state at first load

detection_logic.rule: dataset lag > SLO, where the SLO is a learned arrival-time distribution (p95 of the last 30 days) rather than a fixed cron expectation - real pipelines are variable and fixed thresholds produce constant false alarms.

row count below the seasonal-adjusted expected band by > 25%, or the partition's completeness estimate < 97%. This is the most dangerous data failure because a half-loaded partition looks exactly like a business decline, and agents will act on it.
any column added, removed or retyped in a source relative to the registered contract.
any critical-model test failure (nulls in required fields, uniqueness violations, referential integrity breaks, range violations).
cross-system variance beyond tolerance for 2 consecutive days.
match rate down > 5pp -> cohort attribution is silently degrading.
a partition restated by more than its historical p95 restatement magnitude -> recent decisions based on it should be reviewed.

decision_logic.gating_authority: Janitor computes a health state per dataset (healthy / degraded / quarantined) and publishes it. The Action Gateway consults the lineage of every proposed action and denies any action touching a degraded or quarantined dataset. This is a hard, mechanical block - no confidence threshold can override it.
decision_logic.completeness_estimation: For late-arriving data, Janitor estimates completeness from the source's historical arrival curve and publishes it, so agents can distinguish 'the data is down' from 'the data is 60% loaded and will be complete in 40 minutes'. Agents may act on data at >= 97% estimated completeness with widened intervals.
decision_logic.blast_assessment: Every data incident is published with its downstream impact: affected metrics, dashboards, agents and currently blocked actions, so its business cost is explicit rather than an engineering abstraction.

agent_specific: Data quality findings are largely deterministic and typically score 0.85-0.98.
Completeness estimates carry the uncertainty of the arrival-curve model and are reported as intervals.

root_cause_analysis_process: 1. Localize to the failing pipeline stage using orchestration metadata and logs.
2. Distinguish source-side (API errors, rate limits, upstream outage) from our-side (job failure, resource exhaustion, code change) using error signatures and recent deploys.
3. Check for correlated failures across datasets sharing infrastructure or credentials.
4. Compare against the source's historical behavior (some sources are chronically late; that is a known state, not an incident).
5. Quantify downstream blast radius via the lineage graph.
6. Estimate time-to-recovery from historical incidents of the same signature.
actions_it_can_recommend: Trigger a backfill or job re-run
Quarantine a metric or slice
Open an engineering incident
Change an SLO or contract
Extend an agent's confidence intervals during restatement windows

actions_it_can_execute_automatically.bounds: unlimited - protective and the foundation of fleet safety
unlimited - mechanical enforcement via the gateway
max 3 automatic retries with exponential backoff; beyond that, escalate rather than retry
routine
protective adjustment applied to agents consuming affected data

actions_requiring_human_approval: Changing an SLO or a data contract
Permanently disabling a test
Backfills that rewrite more than 7 days of history (they change already-reported numbers)
Removing a quarantine before the underlying issue is resolved
safety_guardrails: Fails closed: unknown or unmeasurable data health is treated as degraded, never as healthy.
Quarantines cannot be lifted by the agent that requested the data.
Backfills that would change already-reported financial numbers require Finance notification.
Retry storms are prevented by exponential backoff and a hard retry cap.
Test disabling always requires a human and an expiry date.

max_allowed_financial_impact.systemic: Janitor can block 100% of fleet actions. This is the intended failure mode: a system that cannot verify its inputs must not act.

escalation_rules: Freshness breach gating Mode 3 actions or the executive dashboard -> L2 data engineering immediately.
Partial load on a core fact table -> L2 + immediate gating (do not wait for confirmation - the cost of a false gate is minutes of delay; the cost of acting on partial data is real money).
Schema change on a critical source -> L2 + quarantine.
Reconciliation variance affecting revenue reporting -> L3 + Finance.
Repeated failures on the same pipeline (3+ in 7 days) -> L3 (a systemic reliability problem).

consumes_from: None - Janitor is deliberately at the bottom of the dependency graph so it cannot be blocked by the failures it is supposed to detect.
provides_to: Every agent and the Action Gateway - Janitor's health state is a precondition for all decision-making.

memory_context_requirements.episodic: every data incident, its cause, duration and downstream cost
memory_context_requirements.semantic: arrival-time distributions per dataset, restatement profiles per source, lineage graph, contract definitions, known chronic issues
memory_context_requirements.procedural: playbooks: 'late data triage', 'partial load response', 'schema change handling', 'backfill safety'

feedback_loop.predictions_registered: Estimated completeness and time-to-recovery for each incident.
feedback_loop.counterfactual_method: Realized arrival and completeness provide direct labels.
feedback_loop.adaptation: Arrival-curve models and expected-volume bands retrain continuously; SLOs adjust to observed reality with human review; gating thresholds tune against the cost of false gates vs bad decisions.

success_criteria.safety: Zero agent actions executed on stale, partial or contract-violating data (the single most important safety metric in the platform).
success_criteria.detection: Data incidents detected within 5 minutes of detectability in >= 95% of cases.
success_criteria.hygiene: False gating rate < 3% (measured as gates lifted within 15 minutes with no real issue).
success_criteria.recovery: Median time-to-recovery for data incidents < 45 minutes.

AGT-ASO-15.default_mode: Mode 1/2 (store assets and metadata are human-owned)
AGT-ASO-15.mission: Measure and defend non-paid acquisition: store conversion, rankings, ratings and the paid-to-organic uplift relationship that determines the true effective cost of every acquired user.
data_inputs: App Store Connect and Google Play Console analytics (impressions, product page views, installs by source, conversion)
store listing versions and experiment results
paid install and spend series (for the uplift model)
kpis_monitored: organic uplift factor per title x geo

detection_logic.rule: product-page-view -> install conversion down > 8% vs 28d baseline in a geo with > 5% of organic volume.
rolling 7d average down > 0.2 stars or 1-star share up > 8pp; auto-clusters recent negative reviews by topic and joins them to app versions.
category rank down > 30% or out of top 200 in a geo with > 3% of installs.
organic installs below the uplift model's 90% band for 3 consecutive days.
modeled uplift factor changes > 25% - this silently invalidates the effective-CPI used in every profitability decision, which makes it a finance-grade finding rather than an ASO curiosity.

decision_logic.uplift_modeling: organic_installs ~ f(paid_spend by channel, rank, seasonality, featuring, release) fitted per title x geo with a distributed-lag structure; the marginal organic response to paid spend is what Ledger uses to compute true marginal ROAS. Where possible the estimate is validated with paid-off geo tests (a small number of geos periodically pause paid spend for 5-7 days).
decision_logic.attribution_discipline: Beacon never claims causality for a rank or conversion change without either an experiment (store listing test) or a clean changepoint alignment; correlational ASO claims are labeled as such.

agent_specific: Store data is T+1 and coarse; findings cap at 0.80.
Uplift model findings scale with the model's out-of-sample R^2 and with whether a paid-off test has validated the geo.
Review-topic findings are capped at 0.70 (LLM clustering of self-selected text).

root_cause_analysis_process: 1. Split the store funnel: impressions (discovery) vs page views vs installs (conversion) - each has different causes.
2. Check for listing changes: screenshots, icon, video, description, localization, price display, or an active store experiment.
3. Check ratings and recent review topics, joined to app versions.
4. Check competitor movement and category dynamics (Scout).
5. Check whether paid spend changed (uplift changes organic mechanically).
6. Check for store algorithm or featuring changes.
7. Verify the change is not a store-reporting artifact by cross-checking MMP organic installs.
actions_it_can_recommend: Revert or change a store listing asset
Launch a store listing experiment (PPO / Google experiment)
Adjust keywords and metadata
Escalate a rating crisis with clustered topics
Update the organic uplift factor used in effective-CPI math
Time a paid push to a featuring window

actions_it_can_execute_automatically.bounds: routine
routine
unlimited (notification)

actions_requiring_human_approval: Any store listing or metadata change (store assets are brand-owned and store-reviewed)
Updating the uplift factor used in financial calculations (Finance + Head of Data)
Launching store experiments
safety_guardrails: No autonomous store changes ever - store submissions are subject to review, are slow to reverse, and are brand-visible.
Uplift factor changes are Finance-approved because they change reported profitability across the portfolio.
Review-derived findings never quote individual reviewers or expose personal data.

max_allowed_financial_impact.indirect: Uplift factor changes can shift reported marginal ROAS materially, which is why they require approval.

escalation_rules: Rating drop below 4.0 or a 0.3-star weekly decline -> L3 product + marketing.
Organic decline > 20% unexplained -> L3 with the store funnel decomposition.
Uplift factor shift > 25% -> L4 Finance + Head of UA (it re-prices the entire paid portfolio).

consumes_from: Pulse (release timeline and quality signals that drive ratings)
provides_to: Ledger and Oracle (uplift factors -> true effective CPI and marginal ROAS)
Pulse (review topics as qualitative product signal)

memory_context_requirements.episodic: every listing change and its measured effect; featuring events and their lift
memory_context_requirements.semantic: store algorithm behavior notes, seasonal category patterns, keyword difficulty history, per-geo uplift priors
memory_context_requirements.procedural: playbooks: 'store funnel decomposition', 'rating crisis triage', 'uplift validation via paid-off test'

feedback_loop.predictions_registered: Expected conversion/rank/organic effect of recommended changes; predicted organic installs given planned paid spend.
feedback_loop.counterfactual_method: Store listing experiments where available; geo-matched synthetic controls otherwise; periodic paid-off geo tests to validate uplift.
feedback_loop.adaptation: Uplift model refits weekly; listing-change effect priors accumulate.

success_criteria.accuracy: Organic install forecast MAPE <= 12%; uplift factor validated within +/-20% by paid-off tests.
success_criteria.detection: Store conversion and rating regressions detected within 24 hours.
success_criteria.value: Effective-CPI corrections prevent >= $300k/year of spend on channels that only look profitable when organic cannibalization is ignored.

AGT-CMP-16.default_mode: Mode 1 (context provider; its only 'action' is suppressing or reframing other agents' findings)
AGT-CMP-16.mission: Supply the external frame of reference that makes internal anomalies interpretable, and prevent the fleet from attributing market-wide movements to internal causes - the most common and most expensive class of wrong diagnosis.
data_inputs: portfolio-derived market indices (our own CPM/CPI across many campaigns is itself a market sensor)
third-party market intelligence feeds (competitor spend/creative estimates, category rankings)
network changelogs, policy updates and status pages (scraped and LLM-summarized)
seasonal and holiday calendars per geo
kpis_monitored: market CPM/CPI index by geo x platform x category
competitor spend estimates and share of voice
competitor creative launch volume and concepts

monitoring_frequency.market_indices: hourly (computed from our own delivery data)

detection_logic.rule: market index up > 15% week over week in a geo where we spend > 3% of S_daily, where the index is computed as the median CPM change across our own campaigns weighted to exclude our own budget changes (a within-estimator so our actions do not contaminate the index).
a tracked competitor enters the top 50 in our category in a material geo.
changelog/status entries touching attribution, reporting, bidding or creative policy -> auto-assess our exposure and pre-emptively widen anomaly bands for that network for 72h.
a creative concept we run appears in > 30% of tracked competitor creatives in the same geo -> expect accelerated fatigue.
a calendar event with historical CPM impact > 20% within 14 days.

decision_logic.suppression_authority: When Scout establishes that a metric movement is market-wide, it publishes a MARKET_CONTEXT event that downgrades entity-specific findings on that metric to informational and blocks entity-specific corrective actions (they become Recommend at most). This prevents the fleet from cutting budgets into a temporary auction spike - a mistake that both loses volume and costs more to reverse than to avoid.
decision_logic.evidence_standard: Suppression requires the peer-relative test to show the movement across >= 60% of unrelated campaigns in the same geo/platform, not merely a plausible external story.

agent_specific: Portfolio-derived indices are high-confidence (they are our own measured data) and can reach 0.9.
Third-party competitor spend estimates are explicitly low-confidence, hard-capped at 0.5, and can never be the sole basis for an action.
Network policy findings inherit the certainty of the source (official changelog 0.9; inferred from behavior 0.5).

root_cause_analysis_process: 1. Compute the within-estimator market index excluding our own budget changes.
2. Test breadth: what fraction of unrelated campaigns in the same geo/platform moved together.
3. Check the calendar for known events.
4. Check competitor activity for a plausible mechanism.
5. Check network changelogs for a technical cause.
6. Compare against last year's same-period pattern.
7. Publish either a market-wide verdict (with breadth evidence) or an explicit 'no external explanation found' - which is itself valuable, because it tells the domain agent to look harder internally.
actions_it_can_recommend: Suppress or reframe internal findings explained by market context
Hold spend through an auction-pressure window
Prioritize creative production against a saturating concept
Pre-emptively widen anomaly bands after a network change
Brief leadership on competitive dynamics

actions_it_can_execute_automatically.bounds: routine
requires the breadth test to pass; logged and reversible; the original finding remains visible with the market context attached rather than being deleted
72h maximum, network-scoped

actions_requiring_human_approval: Any spend action (Scout has none)
Adding a competitor or market feed (cost commitment)
Permanent suppression rules
safety_guardrails: Suppression never applies to Sev-1 findings or to invariant violations.
Suppression is time-boxed (max 7 days) and auto-expires with a review.
Third-party estimates are always labeled and can never be the sole evidence for a decision.
Scout cannot suppress a finding that another agent has corroborated with internal causal evidence (e.g. a config-change alignment).

max_allowed_financial_impact.indirect: Suppression prevents actions; a wrong suppression is a false negative with real cost, so suppression precision is tracked as a first-class KPI.

escalation_rules: Market CPM surge > 25% in a top-3 geo -> L3 Head of UA (a strategic pacing decision, not a tactical one).
Network policy change with material exposure -> L3 + affected agents.
Competitor launch with measurable share impact -> L4 CMO briefing.

consumes_from: Muse (our creative concepts for overlap analysis)
provides_to: Every agent - market context is an input to every root-cause process

memory_context_requirements.working: current index values and active market events
memory_context_requirements.episodic: every market event and its measured effect on our metrics - builds priors for future events
memory_context_requirements.semantic: seasonal calendars, historical event magnitudes, competitor profiles, network behavior history
memory_context_requirements.procedural: playbooks: 'breadth test', 'market vs internal discrimination', 'seasonal pre-positioning'

feedback_loop.predictions_registered: Predicted duration and magnitude of market events; predicted CPM trajectory.
feedback_loop.counterfactual_method: Realized market indices provide direct labels; suppression correctness is adjudicated by whether the metric recovered when the event ended (market) or persisted (internal cause missed).
feedback_loop.adaptation: Event magnitude priors update; breadth thresholds tune from suppression precision outcomes.

success_criteria.precision: Suppression correct in >= 90% of cases (the metric recovers when the market event ends).
success_criteria.value: Market-caused false diagnoses reduced >= 70%; measurable avoidance of budget cuts into temporary auction spikes.
success_criteria.coverage: Network policy changes detected within 4 hours of publication in >= 90% of cases.

AGT-FIN-17.default_mode: Mode 1/2 (finance is advisory to agents and authoritative on constraints)
AGT-FIN-17.mission: Hold the financial constraints the rest of the fleet optimizes inside: net revenue after all deductions, budget envelopes, cash recovery schedules, payback policy, and the contribution-margin definition that the orchestrator's objective function uses.
data_inputs: store financial reports (App Store Connect, Google Play) and RevenueCat
ad network revenue statements and rev-share terms
tax and withholding tables by jurisdiction
budget envelopes and plan versions from FP&A
kpis_monitored: gross vs net revenue by title/geo/store
network rev-share and its variance vs contract
cash recovery schedule and outstanding UA investment

monitoring_frequency.margin_close: monthly with a daily running estimate

detection_logic.rule: store-reported net differs from our computed net by > 2% for a title/geo -> commission rate, tax, or refund modeling is wrong, and every ROAS number downstream is wrong with it.
network invoice differs from platform-reported spend by > 1% -> billing discrepancy with a claim window.
realized ad network rev share differs from contracted terms by > 1pp.
projected outstanding UA investment exceeds the approved working-capital limit within 30 days -> a spend decision becomes a treasury decision.
portfolio-weighted projected payback > 120 days.
contribution margin % down > 2pp month over month with the driver decomposition attached (volume/CPI/LTV/mix/rev-share).
unhedged currency exposure > 10% of monthly revenue with > 5% volatility.

decision_logic.authority: Abacus does not spend money; it defines the constraints inside which everyone else may. Envelope, payback policy and margin targets are published as versioned constraint objects that the orchestrator's objective function and the Action Gateway both read.
decision_logic.escalation_over_optimization: When a constraint is at risk, Abacus escalates rather than optimizing - the remedy (reduce spend, change payback policy, raise working capital) is a human business decision.

agent_specific: Financial findings are near-deterministic once data is settled (0.9+), but carry a settlement-lag penalty: -0.25 on data less than 3 days old, because refunds, restatements and network credits land late.

root_cause_analysis_process: 1. Decompose the variance by title, geo, store and revenue type.
2. Check commission tier changes (small-business program eligibility, subscription year-2 rates), tax rule changes, and currency settlement.
3. Check refund and chargeback timing (refunds are posted late and attributed back to the original cohort, which makes naive daily comparisons wrong).
4. Reconcile against the platform-reported numbers agents used, and quantify how much decision-making was based on the incorrect figure.
5. For margin erosion, run the five-way bridge: volume, CPI, LTV, mix, rev-share.
actions_it_can_recommend: Change budget envelopes
Change payback policy or target ROAS
File a billing dispute
Adjust rev-share assumptions in the LTV model
Hedge FX exposure
Freeze discretionary spend

actions_it_can_execute_automatically.bounds: routine - envelopes, payback policy, margin targets as versioned objects
routine
automatic when official rate changes are published by the store; versioned with effective dates

actions_requiring_human_approval: Any envelope or policy change (CFO/FP&A)
Filing disputes
Changing rev-share or commission assumptions used in LTV (this changes every historical ROAS number)
Hedging decisions
safety_guardrails: Never changes financial parameters used in historical reporting without a versioned effective date and a restatement note.
All financial constraint changes are dual-approved and audit-logged.
Never acts on unsettled data less than 3 days old.
Reported vs modeled numbers are always distinguishable in the UI.

max_allowed_financial_impact.systemic: Abacus's constraints bound the entire fleet's spending authority.

escalation_rules: Cash constraint risk -> L5 CFO immediately.
Payback policy breach -> L4 VP Growth + Finance.
Net revenue variance > 2% -> L3 Head of Data + Finance (all ROAS numbers are affected).
Invoice variance > 1% -> L3 with the claim deadline flagged.

memory_context_requirements.episodic: reconciliation history, disputes and their outcomes
memory_context_requirements.semantic: contract terms, commission tiers and their effective dates, tax rules by jurisdiction, historical settlement lags per store
memory_context_requirements.procedural: playbooks: 'month-end close', 'variance investigation', 'dispute packet'

feedback_loop.predictions_registered: Projected cash recovery and margin; predicted settlement amounts.
feedback_loop.counterfactual_method: Settled actuals are direct ground truth.
feedback_loop.adaptation: Settlement lag models and refund curves refit monthly; net-revenue factors update from realized statements.

success_criteria.accuracy: Computed net revenue within 1% of settled actuals; cash forecast within 5% at 30 days.
success_criteria.control: Zero envelope breaches without prior escalation; zero missed dispute deadlines.
success_criteria.integrity: 100% of ROAS numbers computed on approved, versioned financial parameters.

AGT-RCA-18.default_mode: Mode 1 (investigation only - Sherlock explains, others act)
AGT-RCA-18.mission: Take incidents that no single domain agent can explain and run deep, multi-domain, hypothesis-driven investigations that produce a defensible causal narrative with quantified confidence - and an explicit 'we do not know' when the evidence does not support a conclusion.
data_inputs: everything - Sherlock has read access to the full semantic layer, the event log, the change log, all agent findings, and the incident archive
the causal DAG (the curated model of how metrics affect each other in this business)
the change timeline across code, config, campaigns, creatives, networks and store
the historical incident archive with adjudicated causes
kpis_monitored: not a monitoring agent - it is dispatched by the orchestrator on demand
its own KPIs: cause-attribution accuracy, investigation latency, evidence completeness, and the rate of honest 'unexplained' verdicts

monitoring_frequency.trigger: on orchestrator dispatch: for any Sev-1, any incident spanning >= 3 modules, any anomaly cluster, any finding where the owning agent's top hypothesis posterior < 0.35, or any user-initiated 'explain this'
monitoring_frequency.budget: each investigation is bounded: <= 15 minutes wall clock, <= 40 evidence queries, <= 12 LLM reasoning steps

detection_logic.note: Sherlock does not detect; it investigates. Its 'detection' is the identification of the causal structure behind an already-detected change.

decision_logic.method: Structured abductive inference over the causal DAG. (1) Establish the effect precisely: metric, entity, magnitude, changepoint window with credible interval. (2) Enumerate candidate causes as the admissible parents of that node in the DAG plus a residual 'unknown' hypothesis that always stays on the list. (3) For each candidate, derive its testable implications - what else must be true if this cause is real. (4) Query for each implication and score the evidence. (5) Compute posteriors: P(cause|evidence) proportional to P(cause) x PROD P(evidence_i|cause). Priors come from the historical frequency of that cause class for that metric in this business. (6) Attempt refutation of the leading hypothesis explicitly - search for evidence that would falsify it, not only evidence that confirms it. (7) Rank and report, including the residual probability that the cause is outside the DAG.
decision_logic.honesty_rule: If no hypothesis exceeds a 0.35 posterior, the verdict is 'unexplained' with the ranked candidates and the specific evidence that would discriminate between them. A confident wrong story is worse than an honest unknown, because the fleet acts on it.
decision_logic.multi_agent_dispatch: Sherlock can request that domain agents run specific targeted analyses (via the orchestrator) rather than doing everything itself - it is a coordinator of expertise as much as an analyst.

agent_specific: Confidence = the leading hypothesis's posterior, penalized by evidence gaps (implications that could not be tested), by confounding (multiple changes in the window), and by DAG coverage (how much of the metric's variance the DAG's parents explain historically).
A hypothesis supported only by temporal coincidence is capped at 0.55 regardless of how compelling the timing is.
+0.10 when an intervention test is available (the cause was reverted and the effect reversed) - the strongest evidence class in the system.

root_cause_analysis_process: Sherlock IS the root cause analysis process - see root_cause_analysis section for the full 10-question framework it executes, and decision_logic above for the inference method.
actions_it_can_recommend: A ranked causal narrative with confidence and quantified impact
Specific remediation actions owned by specific agents/humans
Discriminating tests when the cause is ambiguous ('revert X for 24h in 3 geos and we will know')
DAG updates when a new causal pathway is discovered
Detector improvements when the incident was detected late

actions_it_can_execute_automatically.bounds: routine
<= 6 requests per investigation
proposals only; DAG changes require Head of Data approval because the DAG constrains every agent's reasoning

actions_requiring_human_approval: All remediation actions (Sherlock never executes)
DAG modifications
Changing cause taxonomies
safety_guardrails: Cannot execute any business action, ever - the separation between 'who explains' and 'who acts' prevents narrative-driven action.
Must attempt refutation of its leading hypothesis before reporting it.
Must report the residual 'unknown' probability explicitly.
Cannot assert causation from correlation without a DAG path or an intervention test; correlational findings are labeled as such in the schema, not just in prose.
Investigation budgets are hard limits - a partial answer with stated gaps beats an unbounded search.

max_allowed_financial_impact.indirect: Its conclusions drive others' actions, so cause-attribution accuracy is tracked as its primary KPI and a systematically wrong Sherlock is demoted like any other agent.

escalation_rules: Investigation of a Sev-1 exceeding its time budget -> report partial findings to L4 immediately rather than continuing silently.
Discovery of a cause outside the DAG -> L3 Head of Data (the causal model is incomplete).
Discovery of a systemic issue affecting multiple titles -> L4 immediately.

consumes_from: All agents (their findings are Sherlock's evidence)
provides_to: Orchestrator (causal narratives that drive coordinated action)

memory_context_requirements.working: current investigation state, hypothesis set, evidence collected
memory_context_requirements.episodic: every investigation with its conclusion and the eventually-adjudicated truth - the accuracy measurement substrate and the source of cause priors
memory_context_requirements.semantic: the causal DAG, the cause taxonomy, the business's mechanism knowledge (how this specific game's economy, ad load and progression interact)
memory_context_requirements.procedural: investigation playbooks per incident signature; the discriminating-test catalog

feedback_loop.predictions_registered: The causal verdict itself is the prediction; it is adjudicated when the incident resolves (did the proposed fix work?).
feedback_loop.counterfactual_method: Remediation outcome is the test: if the proposed cause was removed and the effect reversed, the hypothesis is confirmed. Cases resolved without intervention are adjudicated by human review.
feedback_loop.adaptation: Cause priors update from adjudicated frequencies; the DAG is refined when new pathways are confirmed; investigation playbooks are promoted when they repeatedly succeed for a signature.

success_criteria.accuracy: Root cause correct in >= 75% of adjudicated investigations; leading hypothesis correct or in the top 3 in >= 90%.
success_criteria.honesty: Calibration: among verdicts at 0.7-0.8 confidence, 70-80% are correct; 'unexplained' verdicts issued in >= 10% of cases (a system that always has an answer is lying).
success_criteria.speed: Median investigation < 8 minutes; Sev-1 initial narrative within 15 minutes.
success_criteria.value: Analyst investigation hours reduced >= 60%; repeat incidents from the same root cause reduced >= 50%.

AGT-COM-19.default_mode: Mode 3 for routing and reporting (no business actions)
AGT-COM-19.mission: Make sure the right human sees the right thing at the right time in the right amount of detail - and no more. Herald owns the attention budget of the organization, which is as finite and as valuable as the media budget.
data_inputs: all findings, proposals, actions and incidents from the bus
org structure, roles, on-call schedules and time zones
user interaction telemetry (what was opened, acted on, dismissed, marked unhelpful)
kpis_monitored: messages sent per channel per hour
open/action rates by message type and recipient
alert fatigue index (rolling action rate per recipient)

detection_logic.rule: a recipient's action rate on their alerts falls below 20% over 14 days -> their routing is over-broad and is actively destroying signal value.
any approval or acknowledgement past its SLA.
message volume exceeding the channel's budget for 3 consecutive hours.
an incident resolved by someone who was not notified -> the routing map is wrong and is corrected.

decision_logic.routing_rule: Route by (severity x module x entity ownership x on-call state x recipient's historical action rate on this message type). A message type a recipient has ignored 10 consecutive times is demoted to their digest automatically.
decision_logic.aggregation_rule: Correlated findings are never sent separately; they are merged by the orchestrator into one incident message with the constituent findings as evidence.
decision_logic.escalation_rule: Unacknowledged messages escalate on a schedule defined by severity, and escalation always includes the full context so the escalated-to person does not have to reconstruct it.
decision_logic.tone_rule: Message bodies are generated from the structured finding, are always the same shape (headline, dollars, cause, confidence, action, deep link), and never contain a number that is not in the evidence bundle.

confidence_scoring.note: Herald does not produce findings; it inherits and displays the confidence of what it routes, and it never rounds a confidence up.

root_cause_analysis_process: For routing failures: identify whether the failure was in ownership mapping, on-call state, severity classification, or channel configuration; correct the mapping and record the case.
actions_it_can_recommend: Routing map changes
Digest and subscription changes
Threshold changes for a recipient who is being over-alerted

actions_it_can_execute_automatically.bounds: within channel rate budgets
per the escalation matrix
after 10 consecutive ignores; reversible; the recipient is told it happened
protective against fatigue
routine

actions_requiring_human_approval: Changing the escalation matrix
Adding or removing recipients for Sev-1
Disabling a channel
safety_guardrails: Sev-1 messages are never rate-limited, batched, or demoted.
Kill-switch and safety notifications bypass all budgets and preferences.
No message ever contains PII or user-level data.
Every message is deep-linked to its evidence; no orphan alerts.
Herald cannot suppress a message for cost or noise reasons if it carries a financial impact above 0.5% of S_daily.

max_allowed_financial_impact.indirect: Wrong routing delays action; the cost is measured as time-to-acknowledge and is tracked.

escalation_rules: SLA breaches escalate automatically per the matrix.
Fatigue index breach -> L2 to the recipient's manager with the routing analysis (this is a management conversation, not a technical one).

provides_to: Humans - Herald is the fleet's only interface for outbound attention.

memory_context_requirements.episodic: delivery and engagement history per recipient per message type
memory_context_requirements.semantic: org chart, ownership map, on-call schedules, channel configs, message templates
memory_context_requirements.procedural: routing rules and escalation ladders

feedback_loop.predictions_registered: Predicted usefulness of a message to a recipient (from historical engagement).
feedback_loop.counterfactual_method: Engagement and action rates provide direct labels; periodic A/B tests on message format and timing.
feedback_loop.adaptation: Routing weights update from engagement; message templates are A/B tested; per-recipient thresholds personalize over time.

success_criteria.efficiency: Action rate on routed messages >= 45%; 'not useful' rate <= 10%.
success_criteria.reliability: 100% of Sev-1 delivered and acknowledged within SLA.
success_criteria.hygiene: Alert volume per recipient <= 12/day median; zero incidents where the right person was not notified.

AGT-GOV-20.agent_name: Warden - Governance, Safety & Autonomy Control Agent
AGT-GOV-20.default_mode: Mode 3 (enforcement is mechanical and must not wait for a human)
AGT-GOV-20.mission: Enforce every limit the organization has placed on the fleet: evaluate the autonomy matrix on every proposed action, track cumulative financial exposure, detect misbehaving agents, run the kill switches, and maintain the audit record. Warden is the reason autonomy is safe.
data_inputs: every action proposal (it sits in the execution path)
the autonomy matrix and policy bundle
the action ledger and rollback journal
human approval records and role assignments
kpis_monitored: cumulative financial exposure per agent, per entity, per day, fleet-wide
rollback rate and rollback storm indicators
agent mode states and promotion/demotion events

monitoring_frequency.policy_evaluation: synchronous on every action (p99 < 50ms - it is in the critical path)

detection_logic.rule: any action exceeding its granted bounds -> denied and logged with the specific binding constraint (which is fed back to the agent so it can propose a compliant alternative rather than retrying blindly).
>= 3 rollbacks by one agent in 24h, or >= 5 fleet-wide -> automatic demotion / global autonomy pause.
agent Brier score > 0.25 or realized impact sign wrong on >= 30% of the last 20 actions -> automatic demotion.
an agent at > 80% of its daily budget before 14:00 -> throttle to the highest-value proposals only.
an agent's action or finding rate deviating > 3 sigma from its own baseline -> possible model/prompt regression; investigate before allowing further actions.

multiple agents acting on overlapping entities such that the combined effect exceeds any single agent's limit -> this is the failure mode that per-agent limits alone do not catch, so Warden enforces a shared per-entity daily change budget across all agents.

decision_logic.policy_engine: Default-deny. An action executes only if an explicit grant matches (agent, action_type, entity_scope, dollar_band, confidence_band) AND every shared guardrail passes AND the entity's shared change budget has room AND no freeze is active AND the lineage is healthy. Policies are OPA/Rego bundles, versioned in git, deployed through review - governance as code, not as configuration screens.

kill_switches.L1_action_type: disable one action type for one agent
kill_switches.L2_agent: disable one agent's execution (it keeps observing)
kill_switches.L3_module: disable all agents in a module
kill_switches.L5_full_stop: all agents drop to Observe, all pending actions cancelled, all in-flight actions rolled back where reversible
kill_switches.activation: L1-L2 by Growth Ops; L3-L4 by VP Growth or Head of Data; L5 by any of the above unilaterally (safety switches must never require a quorum), with automatic notification to all stakeholders and a mandatory incident review before re-enabling.

decision_logic.graduated_response: Warden prefers the narrowest effective intervention: deny one action, then throttle, then demote, then disable. A global pause is a last resort because a frozen fleet also has a cost.

confidence_scoring.note: Warden's decisions are rule-based and deterministic; it does not use confidence scores, it consumes them. This is deliberate - the enforcement layer must be auditable and reproducible, not probabilistic.

root_cause_analysis_process: For a safety event: reconstruct the full decision chain from the audit log (what data, what detection, what confidence, what policy evaluation, what execution, what outcome), identify which control failed or was missing, and produce a control-improvement proposal. Every safety event results in either a policy change or a documented decision not to change.
actions_it_can_recommend: Autonomy matrix changes
New guardrails
Agent promotion/demotion
Policy improvements after incidents

actions_it_can_execute_automatically.bounds: unlimited - the core function
automatic on rollback storms, calibration failure, or dependency degradation
automatic on safety triggers; L3+ requires a human, except L5 which any authorized human can trigger and which Warden also triggers automatically on a fleet-wide rollback storm
automatic
mandatory for every decision, including denials

actions_requiring_human_approval: Granting or expanding any autonomy (dual approval: VP Growth + Head of Data)
Lifting a kill switch
Promoting an agent to Mode 3
Changing the policy bundle (via code review)
Overriding a denial (possible, but requires role authority, a typed reason, and is prominently audited)
safety_guardrails: Warden cannot grant itself authority; its own policy bundle is human-controlled and version-controlled.
Fails closed: if the policy engine is unavailable, all autonomous actions are denied.
Every denial is logged with the binding constraint - silent denials would make debugging impossible and would erode trust in the system.
The audit log is append-only, hash-chained and written to WORM storage before the action executes, not after.
Warden cannot modify or delete audit records under any circumstance.
Kill switch activation is always faster than any approval workflow - safety never queues.

max_allowed_financial_impact.note: Warden's failure mode is either allowing something it should have blocked (a real financial risk, mitigated by default-deny and fail-closed) or blocking everything (an availability risk, mitigated by graduated response and alerting).

escalation_rules: Any guardrail violation attempt above 1% of S_daily -> L4 immediately (an agent tried to do something big and wrong).
Rollback storm -> L4 + automatic pause.
Policy engine unavailability -> L2 platform + automatic fail-closed.
Override of a denial -> logged and reported in the weekly governance review regardless of outcome.

memory_context_requirements.working: current exposure counters, freeze states, in-flight approvals
memory_context_requirements.episodic: every authorization decision ever made, with its inputs - this is the compliance record
memory_context_requirements.semantic: the policy bundle and its version history, role definitions, escalation matrix
memory_context_requirements.procedural: kill switch runbooks, incident response procedures

feedback_loop.predictions_registered: None - Warden is an enforcement layer, not a predictive one.
feedback_loop.counterfactual_method: Denied actions are tracked: when a denied action's rationale later proves correct, it indicates a guardrail that is too tight and is surfaced in the weekly review with the estimated cost of the block.
feedback_loop.adaptation: Guardrail tuning is a human decision informed by the firing-rate and blocked-value analysis - deliberately not automated, because a safety system that loosens its own limits is not a safety system.

success_criteria.safety: Zero actions executed outside their granted bounds; zero audit gaps; 100% fail-closed behavior in chaos tests.
success_criteria.governance: 100% of autonomy changes dual-approved and version-controlled; every safety event produces a control improvement or a documented decision.
