AGT-LRN-21.default_mode: Mode 1/2 (proposes model, threshold and playbook changes; humans approve promotions)
AGT-LRN-21.mission: Close the loop: measure what every agent predicted against what actually happened, recalibrate confidence, promote and demote playbooks, and continuously answer the question 'is this system actually making better decisions than it was last month'.
data_inputs: the prediction registry (every prediction from every agent)
the action ledger with prior states and rollback records
measurement job outputs (realized values and counterfactuals)
human approval/rejection decisions with reason codes
incident adjudications (what the cause really was)
agent operational telemetry (latency, cost, error rates)
kpis_monitored: per-agent precision, calibration (Brier score, reliability curves), realized-vs-predicted MAPE and bias
human approval rates and rejection reason distributions
cost per finding and per dollar of realized impact
system-level: incremental margin attributable to MART

monitoring_frequency.outcome_measurement: continuous, as measurement jobs complete at +24h/+72h/+7d/+30d
monitoring_frequency.fleet_review: weekly, with a monthly deep review

detection_logic.rule: Brier score > 0.25, or reliability curve deviating > 0.15 from the diagonal in any confidence decile with n >= 20.
realized impact consistently below predicted by > 25% over the last 20 actions of a type (the classic over-optimism failure mode of automated systems).
a playbook's hit rate falls below 0.5 over its last 10 applications, or below its historical rate by > 20pp.
a specific rejection reason code exceeding 30% of rejections for one agent -> the agent has a systematic blind spot, and the reason code names it.
agent-managed entities underperform the human-managed holdout on contribution margin over a full quarter -> a fundamental finding that must be escalated loudly, not buried.
detection latency or precision degrading > 20% month over month.

decision_logic.calibration: Fit isotonic regression per (agent, finding type) mapping raw confidence to empirical correctness; apply as a post-hoc transform. Agents whose calibration cannot be fit (insufficient samples) are capped at Mode 2.
decision_logic.playbook_management: Playbooks are promoted (wider applicability, higher default confidence) when their hit rate exceeds 0.75 over >= 20 applications; demoted or retired when they decay. New playbooks are proposed from clusters of successful ad-hoc actions that share a situation fingerprint.
decision_logic.threshold_optimization: For each detector, compute the cost-weighted optimal threshold from the historical distribution: cost(false positive) = wasted attention + wrong-action risk; cost(false negative) = realized impact of the missed incident. This turns threshold setting into an explicit economic decision rather than a taste judgment.
decision_logic.attribution_of_value: Maintain the running estimate of MART's incremental contribution using the persistent 10% manual-managed holdout plus switchback tests, and report it honestly including negative results.

agent_specific: Scholar's own claims are statistical and carry standard CIs; it never reports a performance improvement without a confidence interval and the sample size behind it.

root_cause_analysis_process: For a performance regression in an agent: check for (1) model/prompt version changes, (2) data distribution shift in its inputs, (3) business regime change making its historical priors invalid, (4) threshold drift, (5) a dependency degradation, (6) a genuine capability limit. Each has a different remedy and confusing them wastes months.
actions_it_can_recommend: Recalibration (applied automatically), retraining, threshold changes
Agent promotion or demotion
Playbook promotion, modification or retirement
New detector proposals
Autonomy expansion or contraction with the historical simulation attached
Killing an agent that does not earn its cost

actions_it_can_execute_automatically.bounds: weekly, bounded to +/-0.2 confidence adjustment per refit so no single refit can radically change fleet behavior
routine
routine
automatic, via Warden

actions_requiring_human_approval: Promoting an agent's mode or expanding autonomy
Promoting a new playbook to autonomous use
Retraining and promoting production models
Retiring an agent
Changing detection thresholds on Sev-1-capable detectors
safety_guardrails: Calibration adjustments are bounded per refit and are always in the conservative direction when the sample is small.
Scholar can demote but cannot promote autonomously - the asymmetry is deliberate: automatic loosening of safety is never acceptable, automatic tightening always is.
All performance claims are computed on held-out data with explicit CIs; in-sample improvements are never reported as results.
Negative results (an agent making things worse) are surfaced with the same prominence as positive ones, in the same weekly report.

max_allowed_financial_impact.systemic: Scholar's calibration outputs modulate every agent's confidence, and therefore every mode decision - which is why its adjustments are bounded and auditable.

escalation_rules: Holdout underperformance over a quarter -> L5 CMO + VP Growth (the platform's core value proposition is in question and must be discussed openly).
Systematic over-optimism in an agent with Mode 3 grants -> L4 + immediate demotion.
Any agent whose cost exceeds its measured value -> L3 with a recommendation to retire or rescope.

memory_context_requirements.episodic: the complete prediction-outcome archive - the training data for the entire learning loop
memory_context_requirements.semantic: evaluation methodology, holdout definitions, cost parameters for threshold optimization
memory_context_requirements.procedural: evaluation playbooks, counterfactual construction methods

feedback_loop.note: Scholar IS the feedback loop. Its own meta-feedback: are its calibrations improving downstream decision quality? Measured by whether post-calibration confidence better predicts realized correctness than pre-calibration confidence, on held-out periods.

success_criteria.calibration: Fleet-wide Brier score <= 0.15; reliability curves within 0.10 of the diagonal in all populated deciles.
success_criteria.learning: Demonstrable improvement in agent precision quarter over quarter until plateau; playbook hit rates trending up.
success_criteria.honesty: Value attribution published monthly with CIs; negative results reported within 7 days of detection.
success_criteria.value: MART's incremental contribution measured and defensible via the holdout, with the estimate's CI narrowing over time.

chief_orchestrator.position: Sits above all 21 specialized agents and below human governance. Every agent proposal that is financially material passes through Atlas; every incident spanning more than one module is owned by Atlas; every conflict between agents is resolved by Atlas.
chief_orchestrator.mission: Hold the single global picture of the business, convert a stream of local, partial, sometimes contradictory agent findings into a ranked, causally coherent set of decisions, and ensure that no local optimization is allowed to damage portfolio contribution margin.
chief_orchestrator.why_it_exists: Each specialized agent is deliberately myopic - that is what makes it good at its job. Hunter maximizes campaign efficiency, Vault maximizes ad revenue, Pulse maximizes engagement, Merchant maximizes IAP. Left alone, these four agents will fight: Vault raises ad load (helping ARPDAU, hurting retention), Anchor sees the retention drop and tells Hunter to cut traffic, Hunter cuts a campaign that was fine, and the portfolio loses on all three fronts while every agent's local KPI looks defensible. Atlas exists to make that impossible.

global_objective_function.primary: maximize E[ contribution_margin_180 ] = SUM_over_cohorts( pLTV_180_net(c) * installs(c) ) - SUM( spend(c) ) - variable_costs
hard_constraints: no title's D1 retention may fall below its floor as a consequence of a MART-initiated action
no action may be taken on data that is stale, partial or contract-violating
cumulative fleet financial exposure per day <= 6% of S_daily

soft_objectives_with_weights.objective: Portfolio resilience (network/geo/creative diversification, avoiding single points of failure)
Learning value (information gained for future decisions - explicitly valued so the system does not become purely exploitative)

global_objective_function.evaluation: Every candidate action set is scored against this function using Oracle's pLTV posteriors and Ledger's response curves, with the portfolio-level effect computed - not the sum of local effects. Interaction terms (a budget increase raising CPM for our own other campaigns in the same auction; an ad-load increase reducing retention which reduces future ad impressions) are modeled explicitly in the cross-effect matrix.

core_responsibilities.mechanism: Subscribes to every event on the bus. Maintains a live incident graph: findings are nodes, and edges are created when findings share an entity, a dimension slice, a time window, or a causal-DAG relationship. Findings that connect become one incident with one owner and one narrative, rather than N alerts to N people.
core_responsibilities.dedup_rule: Two findings merge when: same entity subtree AND overlapping changepoint windows (Jaccard > 0.5) AND a DAG path exists between their metrics. Merged incidents inherit the maximum severity and the union of evidence.

core_responsibilities.mechanism: All open incidents and proposals are ranked by the decision engine's priority score, recomputed every 5 minutes as evidence and impact estimates evolve. The ranking is global across modules, so a $180k monetization issue outranks a $12k campaign issue even though they arrive in different channels and have different owners.

Maintains the causal DAG (curated, versioned, human-approved) and the cross-effect matrix. When two findings in different modules are DAG-connected, Atlas proposes the causal ordering and dispatches Sherlock to confirm or refute it. This is how 'ad revenue is down in BR' and 'a UA source scaled 3 days ago' become one story instead of two tickets.

core_responsibilities.responsibility: Decide when additional agents should investigate
core_responsibilities.mechanism: Dispatch policy: dispatch an agent when the expected information gain (reduction in the entropy of the cause posterior) times the incident's dollar impact exceeds the agent's compute cost times 20. Concretely: for a $200k incident, dispatch liberally (up to 6 agents in parallel); for a $2k incident, dispatch nobody and let the owning agent finish alone. Dispatch decisions and their cost are logged.
See portfolio_guard below - this is Atlas's most important function.

conflict_types.example: Hunter proposes +20% budget on campaign X (low CPI, high marginal ROAS); Anchor has an open finding that X's cohorts have declining D7 retention.
conflict_types.resolution: The proposal is evaluated on the global objective using Oracle's P(target ROAS) which already incorporates the retention signal. If P < 0.5, the scale is denied and a throttle is considered instead. Acquisition-side evidence never overrides cohort-economics evidence - this precedence is hard-coded, not negotiated.

conflict_types.example: Ledger wants to move $40k/day from T2 to T1; Hunter wants to scale a T2 campaign; both cannot happen.
conflict_types.resolution: Compute the joint portfolio effect of each combination (including the do-nothing baseline) and select the maximum. Partial combinations are allowed: often the correct answer is the reallocation at 60% size plus the scale at 50% size.

conflict_types.example: Vault wants to raise ad floors to recover ARPDAU; Pulse has found that a config change reduced impressions/DAU.
conflict_types.resolution: Fix the cause before compensating for the symptom. Atlas orders the actions: revert the config (addresses the cause), then re-measure, then only if the gap persists consider floor changes. Compensating actions taken before the cause is fixed create a double-correction when the cause is later resolved - a classic and expensive oscillation.

conflict_types.example: Muse wants to rotate creatives on a campaign that Hunter is mid-way through a staged scale-up on.
conflict_types.resolution: Sequence, do not parallelize: changing two variables on one entity destroys the measurement of both. Atlas enforces a one-change-at-a-time rule per entity, ordering by expected value and urgency, with the second change scheduled after the first's measurement window.

conflict_types.example: Sentinel flags an anomaly; Scout says it is market-wide; Hunter's own peer check says it is entity-specific.
conflict_types.resolution: Weight by evidence quality: internal causal evidence (a config alignment, an intervention test) > breadth evidence (peer movement) > temporal coincidence. If unresolved, dispatch Sherlock and hold all actions in the meantime.

conflict_types.example: Two titles bidding on the same audience in the same auction, raising each other's CPMs.
conflict_types.resolution: Atlas holds the only view where this is visible. It detects internal auction cannibalization (correlated CPM increases across our own campaigns targeting overlapping audiences) and proposes deconfliction - a decision no single-title agent can make.

precedence_hierarchy: 1. Safety and data integrity (Janitor, Warden) - always wins, no exceptions
4. Cause over symptom (fix the driver before compensating)
5. Reversibility (prefer the more reversible action when expected values are within 20%)
conflict_resolution.unresolvable_rule: If a conflict cannot be resolved by the hierarchy within 30 minutes, Atlas escalates to the human owner with both positions stated fairly, the portfolio-level numbers for each, and its own recommendation. It does not silently pick one.

portfolio_guard.purpose: Block or resize any action whose local benefit is outweighed by its portfolio cost.

cross_effect_matrix.action_class: Scale UA spend on a campaign
modeled_side_effects: own-auction CPM inflation for our other campaigns targeting overlapping audiences (measured elasticity per network/geo)
cohort mix dilution (marginal users are systematically worse than average users - the marginal-vs-average distinction is enforced everywhere)
IAP conversion decline (ad-watchers convert to payers at different rates)
future ad impressions lost through the retention channel - so the naive revenue gain is systematically overstated
network learning-phase reset (recovery cost when re-enabled)
measurement contamination for any concurrent test
cross-metric effects (a cooldown change moves ad revenue, session length, and retention simultaneously)

portfolio_guard.guard_procedure: For every material proposal: (1) compute the local expected value; (2) compute each modeled side effect's expected value with its own uncertainty; (3) sum into a portfolio expected value; (4) if portfolio EV < 0, deny with an explanation; if portfolio EV > 0 but < 50% of local EV, resize the action to the point where marginal portfolio value is zero; (5) record both numbers in the audit so the difference between local and portfolio thinking is visible and auditable.

worked_example_from_requirements.scenario: A UA agent wants to scale a campaign because CPI is low.
worked_example_from_requirements.naive_local_decision: Hunter's acquisition-side rule set sees CPI 24% below baseline and budget utilization at 97%, and proposes +20% budget.
atlas_evaluation: P(cohort D180 ROAS >= target) from Oracle = 0.19, well below the 0.65 scaling gate.
Payback constraint is violated (168 > 120), which is a hard constraint, not a tradeoff.

Cross-effects: scaling adds marginal users worse than the current average, so realized quality would degrade further; organic cannibalization in this geo is 0.28, so true effective CPI is $2.33, not $1.82.
Portfolio EV of the proposed scale: -$34k over 30 days (local EV was computed as +$11k on acquisition metrics alone).
The low CPI is itself diagnostic: cheap installs plus poor retention plus declining ad ARPDAU is the signature of a traffic-quality problem, not a bargain.
worked_example_from_requirements.atlas_decision: DENY the scale. Instead: (a) dispatch Prism and Anchor to localize the quality problem to specific sub-publishers/placements/geos; (b) instruct Hunter to prepare a targeted exclusion rather than a blanket action; (c) if localization succeeds with explanatory power >= 0.70, apply the exclusion (surgical, preserves the good part of the campaign); (d) if it fails, throttle 30% and re-evaluate in 72h; (e) register the prediction that CPI will rise toward $2.20 after the exclusion, which is the expected and desirable outcome - and pre-communicate that to the UA manager so a rising CPI is not read as a failure.
worked_example_from_requirements.governance: The denial, both EV numbers, the evidence and the alternative plan are written to the audit log and surfaced in the UA cockpit, so the human sees exactly why the system refused to scale a 'good' campaign. Unexplained denials destroy trust faster than wrong actions.

investigation_choreography.trigger: Sev-1/Sev-2 incidents, anomaly clusters, findings whose owning agent has a top-hypothesis posterior < 0.35, cross-module DAG-connected findings, or a human 'investigate deeper' request.

actions: Merge related findings into one incident
Establish the precise effect: metric, entity, magnitude, changepoint window
Select the investigation tier from impact: Tier A (>1% S_daily/day, up to 6 agents, frontier reasoning tier), Tier B (0.2-1%, up to 3 agents), Tier C (<0.2%, owning agent only)

Dispatch agents in parallel with specific questions, not vague requests: 'Prism: did the cohort composition of campaign X change between Aug 20-26, and by how much on which dimensions?' rather than 'Prism: investigate campaign X'
Each dispatched agent returns a structured evidence packet with its own confidence
Scout is always dispatched for external context on Tier A/B (ruling out the market explanation early prevents a whole class of wrong conclusions)
Janitor is always consulted first to rule out a data artifact - the single most common cause of dramatic-looking incidents
Sherlock builds the causal hypothesis set constrained by the DAG, scores posteriors, and attempts refutation of the leader
Atlas checks the synthesis against the global context (known events, ongoing changes, prior similar incidents)
Produce the causal narrative with confidence and an explicit unknown residual
Generate candidate action sets (including do-nothing, which is always scored)
Score each against the global objective with cross-effects
Apply the precedence hierarchy and guardrails

phases.phase: 5. Execute and measure (13-15 min, then ongoing)
actions: Route actions to their owning agents for execution under their own guardrails (Atlas never touches an API directly - separation of decision and execution)
Publish the incident narrative to the humans who need it

investigation_choreography.cost_control: Tier A investigations cost roughly $8-20 in model spend and are worth it for a $200k incident. Tier C investigations must stay under $0.20. The tier is chosen from impact before any expensive reasoning begins, and the budget is enforced.
investigation_choreography.parallelism_rule: Agents are dispatched in parallel wherever their questions are independent, and sequentially only where one answer determines the next question. Most investigations are 80% parallel, which is what keeps Tier A under 15 minutes.

contents: Business calendar: releases, LiveOps events, marketing beats, featuring windows, seasonal events per geo, competitor launches, planned experiments
Strategic context: current portfolio priorities (e.g. 'T2 is in a growth push; accept payback up to 150 days through Q4'), title lifecycle stages, market entry plans, partnership commitments
Constraint state: current envelopes, payback policy, cash limits, change freezes, contractual minimums
System state: which agents are in which mode, which datasets are degraded, which models are drifting, what is currently being changed by humans
Recent action memory: every action taken by anyone (human or agent) in the last 30 days, so nothing is diagnosed in ignorance of a change that caused it
Historical case archive: past incidents with their causes and resolutions, retrievable by similarity
global_context_store.maintenance: Calendar and strategic context are human-maintained through the console (with an ingestion path from Jira/Notion/Slack for release and LiveOps schedules); constraint and system state are agent-maintained; action memory is automatic from the audit log.
global_context_store.usage: Injected into every Tier A/B investigation prompt and consulted by the portfolio guard on every material proposal. A finding that contradicts known context (e.g. 'installs dropped' during a planned budget pause) is auto-suppressed with an explanation.

decision_cadence.continuous: Event-driven: every finding is triaged within 30 seconds of arrival; incident graph updated continuously.
decision_cadence.every_5_min: Re-rank all open incidents and proposals by priority score.
decision_cadence.every_15_min: Portfolio state refresh: spend pace, revenue run-rate, exposure counters, agent states.
decision_cadence.hourly: Coherence check - scan for contradictory open directives, oscillating entities, and stalled incidents.
decision_cadence.daily_07_00_utc: Portfolio review: evaluate the full action set for the day, approve or resize agent proposals in batch, publish the executive narrative, set the day's priorities.
decision_cadence.daily_18_00_local: End-of-day reconciliation: what was predicted vs what happened today, which actions need checkpoint evaluation tomorrow.
decision_cadence.weekly: Strategic review: portfolio allocation, agent performance (with Scholar), guardrail effectiveness, incident retrospectives.
decision_cadence.monthly: Objective function review with leadership - are the weights still right, is the payback policy still right, what did the holdout show.

orchestrator_own_guardrails: Atlas never executes an action directly - it authorizes and sequences; owning agents execute under their own guardrails, and Warden independently re-validates every action. Three independent checks (agent, orchestrator, Warden) must agree before money moves.
Atlas cannot grant autonomy, expand a limit, or lift a kill switch - those are human-only powers.
Atlas cannot suppress a Sev-1 finding or hide an agent's dissent; conflicting positions are preserved in the incident record even when it decides against one.
Atlas's own decisions are subject to the same prediction registry and measurement as any agent's, and Scholar scores its conflict-resolution accuracy separately.

Fleet-wide exposure cap: the sum of all authorized actions in a rolling 24h window cannot exceed 6% of S_daily; approaching the cap, Atlas authorizes strictly in priority order and tells the humans what it is deferring and why.

If Atlas is unavailable, agents fall back to Mode 2 (Recommend) automatically - they never execute autonomously without orchestrator authorization, so a dead orchestrator degrades the system to human-in-the-loop rather than to uncontrolled autonomy.

memory_and_reasoning.reasoning_tier: Frontier reasoning model tier for synthesis, conflict resolution and Tier A investigations; balanced tier for routine triage; the deterministic scoring, ranking and constraint checks are code, not model calls.
memory_and_reasoning.context_construction: Atlas never receives raw data. It receives: the incident graph, structured findings with their evidence summaries, the global context store, the constraint set, and the candidate action sets with their computed EVs. Its job is judgment over structured inputs, not analysis of raw tables.

memory.working: the live incident graph and portfolio state
memory.episodic: every orchestration decision, conflict resolution and its outcome
memory.semantic: the causal DAG, cross-effect matrix, precedence hierarchy, strategic context
memory.procedural: investigation choreographies and resolution patterns that have worked

escalation_rules: Any incident with projected 30-day impact > 2% of S_daily x 30 -> L5 (CMO) within 15 minutes with the narrative as it stands, even if incomplete.
Any unresolvable conflict after 30 minutes -> the human owner of both agents' modules.
Any hard-constraint violation (payback, envelope, cash) -> L4 Finance + VP Growth immediately.
Fleet exposure cap reached -> L3 with the deferred-action list.
Three or more Sev-2 incidents open simultaneously in one module -> L3 (something systemic is happening in that domain).
Contradiction between two agents that both have high confidence and internal causal evidence -> L4 Head of Data (this usually means a data or definitional problem, not a business one).

success_criteria.coherence: Zero instances of agents taking contradictory actions on the same entity; zero oscillation events (an entity changed in opposite directions within 48h).
success_criteria.portfolio_protection: >= 95% of local-optimization traps caught (measured against a labeled set of historical cases plus injected synthetic cases in chaos testing).
success_criteria.prioritization: The top-5 ranked incidents each day account for >= 70% of the day's total identified business impact.
success_criteria.investigation: Tier A investigations complete in < 15 minutes with a causal narrative in >= 90% of cases; conflict resolutions later judged correct in >= 80%.
success_criteria.trust: Human override rate of Atlas decisions < 15%, and overrides that later prove correct < 40% of those (if humans override often and are usually right, Atlas is wrong; if they override often and are usually wrong, the explanations are failing).

cohort_intelligence.design_statement: The cohort model is the spine of the platform. Every economic claim, every agent decision and every dollar of autonomous spend authority traces back to a row in the cohort fact tables. It is therefore designed for correctness first (immutable install-date grain, explicit maturity, versioned definitions) and for query speed second (pre-aggregated projections, materialized rollups).

grain_definition.cohort_key: surrogate hash of the full acquisition dimension tuple: (title_id, install_date_utc, media_source, campaign_id, adset_id, ad_id, creative_id, geo_country, geo_region, platform, os_version_major, app_version_at_install, device_tier, device_model_group, is_organic, user_type, acquisition_objective, attribution_type, attribution_certainty_band, experiment_assignment_hash, monetization_segment_at_d0)
grain_definition.why_a_hash: Storing the tuple as a hash makes cohort identity stable across dimension additions and lets the fact table stay narrow; the tuple itself lives in dim_cohort with a surrogate key and full history.
grain_definition.user_level_backing: fct_user_daily exists at (user_pseudo_id, date) grain for behavioral modeling and for building arbitrary cohorts on demand; it is the source from which cohort aggregates are built, is access-controlled, and is subject to retention and deletion policy.
grain_definition.immutability_rule: The acquisition dimensions of a cohort are fixed at install and never change. A user who later moves country, upgrades OS, or joins an experiment does NOT change cohort. Post-install attributes are behavioral dimensions on the daily fact, never on the cohort key. Violating this rule silently destroys the comparability of every historical cohort.

acquisition_dimensions.notes: the cohort anchor; also stored as install_week, install_month for rollups
used for hour-of-day cohorting and CTIT analysis
normalized across MMPs; a mapping table reconciles network naming ('googleadwords_int' -> 'google_ads')
concept id comes from the creative clustering model and enables learning across creatives
organic is a first-class cohort, not an absence of data; it is the primary quality benchmark
propagates into every confidence calculation downstream
critical for fraud analysis; high cardinality, stored on the user fact and rolled up on demand rather than in the cohort key

geographic_dimensions.notes: state/province where available; used for geo-holdout design
derived, used for benchmarking and peer grouping
US only; the unit of geo-lift experiments

device_and_platform_dimensions.notes: distinct from current app_version, which lives on the daily fact

device_and_platform_dimensions.derivation: RAM x CPU benchmark x GPU class, refreshed quarterly; one of the most predictive quality dimensions and routinely missing from network-side reporting

user_and_behavioral_dimensions.notes: computed at D0 (predicted) and updated continuously (actual); the cohort key stores the D0 predicted segment, the daily fact stores the current actual
daily fact; the frontier analysis dimension
affects both measurement and monetization; a major and frequently ignored confounder in geo comparisons

experiment_and_config_dimensions.notes: hashed into the cohort key so experiment cohorts are separable
daily fact; enables config-change impact analysis

temporal_dimensions.notes: the cohort age axis - the single most important column in the warehouse
the calendar date of the activity, so both cohort-age and calendar views are possible from one table

dimension_model.cardinality_management: The full cross-product is astronomically large; the physical cohort table is materialized at a governed set of ~15 dimension combinations covering >99% of query patterns, with an on-demand path that builds arbitrary cohorts from fct_user_daily for the long tail. Cohort builds exceeding 10k groups are rejected to prevent multiple-comparison fishing.

fct_cohort_daily.partitioning: PARTITION BY install_date_utc, CLUSTER BY (title_id, media_source, geo_country, days_since_install)
measures: installs (denominator, constant across all rows of a cohort)
active_users_d (returning users on this day - the retention numerator)
cumulative_revenue_per_install (= LTV actual at this day)
spend_allocated (the cohort's share of campaign spend, allocated at click/install time - constant across rows)
maturity_flag (which metrics are valid at this age), completeness_estimate
restatement_generation (increments when the row is restated by late data)
fct_cohort_daily.sql_sketch: CREATE TABLE fct_cohort_daily ( cohort_key BYTES NOT NULL, days_since_install INT64 NOT NULL, install_date_utc DATE NOT NULL, activity_date DATE NOT NULL, title_id STRING, media_source STRING, campaign_id STRING, geo_country STRING, platform STRING, installs INT64, active_users_d INT64, sessions INT64, session_seconds INT64, ad_impressions INT64, ad_revenue_estimate NUMERIC, ad_revenue_reconciled NUMERIC, iap_revenue_net NUMERIC, total_revenue_net NUMERIC, cumulative_revenue_net NUMERIC, spend_allocated NUMERIC, cumulative_roas NUMERIC, predicted_ltv_180 NUMERIC, predicted_ltv_180_lower NUMERIC, predicted_ltv_180_upper NUMERIC, p_target_roas NUMERIC, pltv_model_version STRING, maturity_flag STRING, completeness_estimate NUMERIC, restatement_generation INT64, updated_at TIMESTAMP ) PARTITION BY install_date_utc CLUSTER BY title_id, media_source, geo_country, days_since_install;
fct_cohort_daily.refresh: incremental every 15 minutes for days_since_install <= 2; every 6 hours for <= 30; daily beyond that. Late-arriving revenue triggers targeted re-materialization of the affected cohort rows with an incremented restatement_generation.

fct_user_daily.purpose: behavioral modeling, feature engineering, ad-hoc cohort construction, churn scoring
fct_user_daily.measures: sessions, session_seconds, events by category, ad impressions by format, ad revenue, iap revenue, progression state, current app version, current config bundle, current experiment assignments, churn score, predicted segment
fct_user_daily.privacy: pseudonymous ids only; joins to identity are permission-gated; row-level deletion supported for GDPR/CCPA requests with a documented 30-day SLA; the table is excluded from any export.

dim_cohort.content: the full dimension tuple plus derived attributes (geo_tier, device_tier, concept_id), plus cohort-level constants (installs, spend_allocated, first_seen_at)
dim_cohort.type: SCD Type 2 on any dimension that could be restated (e.g. attribution reassignment), so historical analyses remain reproducible

fct_cohort_curve_fits.content: fitted parameters for retention (sBG alpha/beta), revenue accrual, and ROAS maturation, with goodness of fit and CIs - used for early-signal detection of curve-shape changes and for extrapolation

fct_cohort_predictions.content: every pLTV/retention prediction ever made, with intervals and the feature snapshot id - this is the prediction registry that makes model accuracy auditable rather than asserted

retention: D0 (same-day return), D1, D3, D7, D14, D30, D60, D90 classic
rolling retention at the same checkpoints
fitted curve parameters and implied long-run retention
engagement: sessions per user per day and cumulative
monetization: ad impressions per user per day
payer conversion rate at each day
risk_and_quality: mean churn probability and expected churn count

maturity_and_validity_rules.principle: An immature metric is NULL, never zero, and never silently averaged. This one rule prevents the most common catastrophic error in cohort reporting - a fresh cohort appearing to have 0% retention and 0 ROAS and triggering a panic cut.
rules: retention_dN is valid only when now() >= install_ts + (N+1) days AND the day's data is >= 97% complete.
cumulative_roas at day N is valid only when all revenue through day N has settled (ad revenue reconciled T+3, IAP refunds T+3).
Any metric computed on a cohort with installs < the metric's minimum n is returned with an inadequate_sample flag that the Action Gateway treats as blocking.

Predictions are always available (that is their purpose) but carry maturity_days_at_prediction, and downstream confidence is capped by maturity: <D1 -> 0.55, D1-D3 -> 0.65, D3-D7 -> 0.75, D7-D30 -> 0.85, >D30 -> 0.95.
Comparisons are only permitted at equal cohort age. The semantic layer physically rejects a query comparing a D3 cohort's cumulative ROAS to a D30 cohort's.
maturity_and_validity_rules.derivation: n_min is derived per metric from the variance needed to detect the smallest business-relevant effect at 80% power and alpha 0.05, recomputed quarterly from observed variance rather than fixed by intuition.

primary_keys.role: the spine of all internal behavioral data
joins attribution and MMP-delivered ad revenue to the user
reinstall detection and cross-app (same publisher) linking where permitted
deterministic attribution when available; increasingly absent on iOS
cross-device identity for logged-in users; also the join to RevenueCat
the authoritative purchase key; the only reliable way to deduplicate revenue
join to cost data - note that MMP and network id formats differ per network and require a normalization mapping table
the weakest link in the join graph; several networks do not expose a stable creative id in cost reporting, requiring name-pattern matching plus a maintained mapping table

identity_and_join_keys.resolution_strategy: Deterministic first (customer_user_id > idfv/android_id > appsflyer_id), never probabilistic across users. Match rate is monitored by Janitor; a drop is treated as a data incident because it silently degrades every cohort.
identity_and_join_keys.skan_handling: SKAN/AAK installs cannot join to a user. They are stored in a parallel fct_skan_cohort table at (campaign, geo, conversion_value, postback_day) grain, modeled into estimated cohort metrics using a mapping learned from the consented population, and always labeled attribution_type='skan_modeled'. They are never silently merged into the deterministic cohort table.

pltv_model.architecture: Two-stage ensemble per (title, platform, monetization_profile): (1) a payer classifier (gradient boosted trees) producing P(user becomes a payer by D180); (2) a conditional revenue regressor (GBT on log revenue) for predicted payer spend; (3) an ad-revenue model based on predicted retention x predicted impressions/DAU x geo eCPM; (4) a survival model (Weibull/sBG) for the retention curve that drives both; (5) hierarchical Bayesian shrinkage that pulls small-slice estimates toward their parent slice, which is what makes campaign-level and creative-level pLTV usable at all.
features: D0-D2 behavioral: session count, total session seconds, core-loop completions, progression depth, tutorial completion, time-to-first-key-action, day-1 return
D0 monetization: ad impressions, ad revenue, any early purchase
cohort dimensions: geo, platform, device_tier, media_source, campaign, creative concept, os version
slice priors: the historical LTV curve of this slice with shrinkage
seasonality: install month, day of week, proximity to LiveOps events
creative attributes of the acquiring creative
pltv_model.training: Rolling 18 months with recency weighting (half-life 90 days); trained on matured cohorts (D180 realized); evaluated on a held-out time period, never a random split (random splits leak future information through calendar effects and produce dishonestly good metrics).
pltv_model.outputs: point estimate + 80% prediction interval + P(target ROAS) + SHAP attributions, refreshed every 6 hours as behavioral evidence accumulates and the prediction sharpens.
pltv_model.governance: Champion/challenger with a 30-day shadow; promotion requires better calibrated MAPE on the holdout, no regression in any slice carrying >5% of spend, and Head of Data approval. Every downstream decision records the model version used.

how_cohort_data_feeds_autonomous_decisio.principle: A cohort row is the unit of economic truth. No autonomous action is permitted unless it can name the cohort slice it is acting on, that slice passes the maturity and sample gates, and its P(target ROAS) supports the direction of the action.

concrete_pathways.flow: fct_cohort_daily -> Oracle computes P(target ROAS) per campaign slice -> Hunter's scaling rule requires P >= 0.65 with the 80% interval lower bound above target -> Warden verifies the cohort passed sample and maturity gates -> action executes.
concrete_pathways.effect: Makes it structurally impossible to scale on CPI alone. The cohort table is the veto.

concrete_pathways.flow: D0-D2 behavioral features -> Prism's quality index and Anchor's early-signal model -> predicted D7 below corridor -> COHORT_QUALITY_CHANGE event -> Hunter throttles the specific slice 20-35% -> measurement at +72h against matched controls.
concrete_pathways.effect: Cuts bad spend 4-6 days before the cohort's ROAS would have revealed the problem. This pathway alone is the largest single source of the platform's projected savings.

concrete_pathways.pathway: Surgical exclusion instead of blunt cut
concrete_pathways.flow: Cohort dimension contribution analysis localizes the damage (e.g. 78% of the loss is device_tier=low x placement=audience_network) -> Hunter applies a placement/device exclusion rather than a budget cut -> the profitable 80% of the campaign keeps running.
concrete_pathways.effect: Preserves volume while removing loss. Only possible because the cohort model retains dimensions the network's own reporting does not.

concrete_pathways.flow: Cohort pLTV by slice -> Abacus's payback policy -> allowable CPI with an uncertainty-scaled safety margin -> Hunter's bid targets and Ledger's allocation constraints.
concrete_pathways.effect: Bids are derived from measured cohort value rather than from a static target set months ago.

concrete_pathways.flow: Cohort revenue decomposition (retention x ad ARPDAU x payer conversion) identifies which component moved -> the finding is routed to Anchor, Vault or Merchant instead of triggering a UA action.
concrete_pathways.effect: Prevents cutting good traffic to compensate for a product or monetization regression - the single most expensive misdiagnosis in mobile UA.

concrete_pathways.flow: A young cohort is matched to its 20 nearest historical analogues -> their realized outcomes provide a model-free prior -> a large divergence between the pLTV model and the analogue distribution blocks autonomous action and triggers an investigation.
concrete_pathways.effect: Catches model failures that internal model diagnostics miss.

concrete_pathways.flow: Every action registers the affected cohort_keys -> at +7/+30 days the realized cohort outcome is compared against the prediction and against matched control cohorts -> the delta updates the agent's calibration and playbook hit rates.
concrete_pathways.effect: The cohort table is simultaneously the decision input and the evaluation ground truth, which is what makes the learning loop closed rather than aspirational.

gates_enforced_at_the_cohort_layer: attribution certainty (low certainty widens intervals and can block)
composition stability (a cohort whose mix shifted > 15pp is not comparable to its own history and cannot serve as a baseline)

supported_segmentations: any behavioral segment defined on fct_user_daily (e.g. 'completed tutorial in session 1')
cohort_segmentation_capabilities.composite_segments: Any boolean combination, saved as a versioned cohort object with an owner, usable by dashboards, alerts and agents alike - so a human and an agent are always talking about exactly the same population.
cohort_segmentation_capabilities.comparison_engine: Any two cohort objects can be compared with automatic significance testing, effect sizes, multiple-comparison correction across the compared metrics, and automatic highlighting of the largest standardized differences; the engine refuses comparisons at unequal cohort age or with inadequate samples.

integration_principles: Land raw, immutable, timestamped payloads first (bronze); never transform before persisting. Every downstream bug is debuggable only if the original payload survives.
Every source has a declared data contract (schema, expected volume band, expected arrival window, uniqueness keys, allowed null rates) enforced on every load by Janitor.

Restatement is normal, not exceptional. Every fact carries a restatement_generation and a loaded_at; consumers must be able to ask 'what did we believe at time T', which is what makes historical agent decisions auditable.

Rate limits are treated as a first-class design constraint: every connector implements token-bucket throttling, exponential backoff with jitter, request coalescing, and a priority queue so a backfill never starves the realtime path.

Normalization happens once, in the staging layer, into a canonical schema (canonical network names, canonical geo codes ISO-3166-alpha2, canonical currency USD with the rate stamped at ingest, canonical event names). No agent or dashboard ever sees a network's raw naming.
Cost data and event data are never joined on date without an explicit grain declaration - the single most common source of wrong ROAS in the industry.
data_integration.verification_note: API rate limits, endpoint names and field availability change frequently and differ by account tier and API version. Every limit below is a starting configuration to be verified against the provider's current documentation during connector implementation, and is stored in connector config rather than hardcoded. The connector framework treats an unexpected 429/403 as a signal to re-read the provider's published limits, not as a fatal error.

appsflyer.role: Primary MMP - system of record for attribution
data_collected: raw installs (Pull API / Data Locker): install time, click time, attribution touch, campaign hierarchy, geo, device, IDs
ad revenue (ULAR) events forwarded from mediation
cost aggregation (Cost ETL) where the network integration exists
appsflyer.granularity: user-level rows for consented/Android traffic; aggregate + modeled for SKAN; campaign/adset/ad/site_id dimensions on every row
appsflyer.update_frequency: Raw data pulls every 15 minutes (rolling window with lookback); Data Locker delivers hourly partitions to cloud storage; aggregate reports hourly; SKAN postbacks arrive 24-72h after install with additional postback windows
api_limitations: Pull API has per-account daily request budgets and row limits per report; large accounts must use Data Locker (S3/GCS delivery) rather than API pulls
Raw-data retention window is limited (typically ~90 days) - historical data must be persisted by us on arrival or it is lost
Cost ETL coverage varies by network and is not available for all self-attributing networks
Rate limiting is per-account, not per-app, so backfills must be scheduled against the same budget as realtime pulls
attribution_considerations: Attribution windows (click 7d default, view 1d, but per-network configurable) directly determine install counts - any window change breaks historical comparability and must be recorded as a versioned config event

Self-attributing networks (Meta, Google, TikTok, Apple) report their own installs and are reconciled, not attributed, by the MMP - discrepancies are expected and are a monitored metric, not necessarily an error
Re-attribution and re-engagement windows can silently move installs between organic and paid
SKAN data is modeled and has crowd-anonymity thresholds that suppress fine-grained conversion values at low volume
appsflyer.freshness_expectation: raw installs <= 30 min p95; in-app events <= 30 min; ad revenue events <= 60 min; cost <= 3h; SKAN 24-72h
appsflyer.ingestion_pattern: Data Locker -> object storage -> incremental load to bronze -> dedupe on (event_uuid) -> staging normalization; Pull API used only for gap-filling and reconciliation
failure_modes_to_monitor: silent partial partitions in Data Locker
attribution window config changed by a human in the AppsFlyer UI without notice
cost ETL gaps for a network appearing as a spend drop

adjust.role: Secondary MMP (parallel measurement on a subset of titles) - used for cross-validation and as a migration hedge
data_collected: installs, sessions, in-app events via callbacks (real-time server-to-server) and CSV uploads
cost data via Adjust's cost integration
cohort and deliverables reports via the Report Service API
adjust.granularity: user-level via callbacks; aggregate via Report Service (KPI-level with dimension breakdowns)
adjust.update_frequency: callbacks in real time (seconds); Report Service near-real-time with a short delay; cost daily with intraday refreshes
api_limitations: Report Service API applies per-token rate limits and has a maximum dimension cardinality per request; wide breakdowns must be split into multiple requests and stitched
Historical data access depends on the plan; raw export requires callback capture at the time of the event - you cannot retroactively retrieve raw callbacks you failed to capture
attribution_considerations: Adjust and AppsFlyer will disagree by 2-8% on the same traffic due to differing dedup, window and fingerprinting rules - the difference is a measurement finding, not a bug, and Compass tracks it as a monitored variance
Running two MMPs requires both SDKs and careful event-name mapping; a canonical event dictionary is mandatory
adjust.ingestion_pattern: S2S callbacks -> API gateway -> Kafka topic -> bronze; Report Service pulls for reconciliation

meta_ads.role: Cost, delivery, creative and audience data for Meta campaigns; write target for budget/bid/status changes
data_collected: Insights: spend, impressions, clicks, reach, frequency, CPM, CTR, conversions, app installs, purchase events, video metrics, by campaign/adset/ad
entity configuration: budgets, bid strategies, targets, targeting, status, learning phase state
meta_ads.granularity: campaign/adset/ad x day x (optional breakdowns: country, placement, device, age/gender, publisher_platform). Note that breakdown combinations are restricted and some cannot be combined in a single request.
meta_ads.update_frequency: every 30-60 minutes for active entities; hourly for full account sync; entity config sync every 15 minutes for entities under agent control
api_limitations: Business Use Case (BUC) rate limiting with per-app and per-account scoring; heavy insight queries consume budget quickly and trigger throttling that can last hours
Async report jobs are required for large queries (submit, poll, download) - synchronous requests fail at scale
Attribution setting on the account determines the conversion numbers returned; changing it changes history
Data can be restated for up to 28 days (billing adjustments, invalid traffic)
Some breakdowns are unavailable at ad level or in combination
Write operations are subject to separate, tighter limits, and entity changes can take minutes to propagate
identity_join_keys: MMP campaign id mapping (Meta ids appear directly in MMP data for SAN traffic)
attribution_considerations: Meta is self-attributing: its reported installs will not match MMP-attributed installs, typically by 5-15%, driven by different attribution windows, view-through handling and SKAN modeling
SKAN/AAK campaigns report modeled conversions with delays and aggregation floors
Advantage+ / AAA campaigns collapse targeting dimensions, reducing the granularity available for cohort analysis - cohorts must fall back to placement/geo/device dimensions from the MMP side
meta_ads.freshness_expectation: spend within 90 minutes of the Meta UI; final within 28 days
write_capabilities: bid amount / cost cap / ROAS goal
meta_ads.write_safety: All writes are preceded by a read of current state and followed by a read-back verification 60 seconds later; idempotency is enforced by our own key since the API does not provide one for most edits.

google_ads.role: Cost, delivery and asset data for App campaigns (UAC/AC); write target for budgets and targets
data_collected: campaign, ad group, asset group and asset-level metrics: cost, impressions, clicks, installs, in-app conversions, conversion value
bid strategy configuration and target CPA/ROAS
google_ads.granularity: campaign / ad group / asset x day x segments (geo, device, network). Asset-level metrics are limited and asset performance is reported as coarse labels rather than full metrics.
google_ads.update_frequency: hourly via GAQL queries (Google Ads API); full daily reconciliation
api_limitations: Operations-per-day quotas depend on access level (basic vs standard); reporting queries and mutate operations draw on different quotas
GAQL requires explicit field selection and does not allow arbitrary metric/segment combinations - some breakdowns are simply unavailable
Conversion data is restated for several days as conversions are attributed back to click dates
App campaigns expose very limited sub-campaign structure - there are no traditional adsets, which limits targeting-level actions
Changing target CPA/ROAS resets the learning period; the API will accept rapid changes that will damage delivery, so rate limiting must be enforced on our side
identity_join_keys: MMP mapping via campaign id embedded in the tracking link
attribution_considerations: Google is self-attributing with its own modeled conversions, including modeled iOS conversions; discrepancy with MMP of 5-20% is normal
Conversion lag means today's reported installs will grow for several days - never treat T-0 as final
AC campaigns optimize toward the chosen conversion event; changing that event effectively creates a new campaign behaviorally
google_ads.freshness_expectation: cost within 3 hours; conversions settle over 3-7 days

tiktok_ads.role: Cost, delivery and creative data; write target for budget/bid/status
data_collected: spend, impressions, clicks, installs, conversions, video views and completion metrics, by campaign/adgroup/ad
tiktok_ads.granularity: campaign/adgroup/ad x day x (country, placement, device) breakdowns
tiktok_ads.update_frequency: hourly reporting sync; entity config every 15 minutes for controlled entities
api_limitations: Per-app QPS limits and daily quotas; large reports must be requested asynchronously
Reporting dimensions are restricted in combination; some metrics are unavailable at ad level
Data restatement for up to 72 hours
Creative-level reporting granularity varies by campaign type (Smart Performance campaigns hide much of the structure)
identity_join_keys: advertiser_id, campaign_id, adgroup_id, ad_id, creative/video id
MMP mapping via tracking link parameters
attribution_considerations: TikTok is self-attributing; view-through attribution contributes materially and inflates TikTok's own numbers relative to MMP click-based attribution
Creative ids in cost reporting may not match the asset ids in our creative system - a maintained mapping table is required

unity_ads.role: UA cost/delivery (Unity Ads network) and, separately, monetization revenue if used as a demand source
data_collected: acquisition: spend, impressions, clicks, installs, CPI by campaign/target/geo/source app
monetization: revenue, impressions, eCPM, fill by placement/geo
source-app (publisher) level performance - unusually granular and valuable for blocklisting
unity_ads.granularity: campaign x target x geo x source app x day (acquisition); placement x geo x day (monetization)
unity_ads.update_frequency: acquisition stats hourly; monetization daily with intraday estimates
api_limitations: Reporting API has request rate limits and a maximum date range per request
Source-app level data can be very high cardinality and requires pagination
Revenue figures are restated at month close
identity_join_keys: campaign id, target id, source app id
attribution_considerations: Source-app (sub-publisher) data is essential for fraud detection and blocklisting; it is one of the few networks exposing it cleanly
Unity's install counts are click-based and reconcile reasonably well with MMP data
unity_ads.freshness_expectation: acquisition <= 2h; monetization revenue estimates same-day, reconciled T+2
write_capabilities: campaign budget and bid (via the campaign management API)
source app blocklist/allowlist - a high-value automated action

applovin.role: Dual: MAX mediation (monetization system of record for many titles) and AppDiscovery (UA demand)
data_collected: MAX: user-level ad revenue (ULAR) via S3/API export, impression-level data with network, placement, country, ad unit, waterfall instance, eCPM
MAX: aggregate revenue, impressions, fill by network/geo/format
AppDiscovery: spend, installs, campaign performance, creative performance
applovin.granularity: impression-level for ULAR (the richest monetization data available anywhere); aggregate reports at ad_unit x network x country x day
applovin.update_frequency: ULAR files delivered hourly to S3; aggregate reporting API refreshed hourly; revenue reconciled T+1 to T+3
api_limitations: Reporting API rate limits per key; ULAR volume is very large (billions of rows/month at scale) and must be loaded incrementally into columnar storage, never queried row-by-row
Estimated revenue in ULAR is revised at reconciliation; the variance is material for low-volume slices
Waterfall configuration changes via API require care - a malformed waterfall can zero out fill
identity_join_keys: idfa/gaid/idfv (ULAR carries device ids for joining to users)
custom user id if passed to the SDK (strongly recommended - it is the only reliable join to our user table)
ad unit id, network name, country
attribution_considerations: ULAR is the foundation of user-level ad LTV; without it, ad revenue can only be allocated by impression share, which destroys cohort-level ad revenue accuracy
The MAX-reported network name is the demand source, not the mediation - do not confuse the two in eCPM analysis

mintegral.role: UA demand source and ad network
data_collected: spend, impressions, clicks, installs, conversions by campaign/offer/geo/sub-publisher
monetization revenue if used as demand in mediation
mintegral.granularity: campaign x offer x geo x sub_publisher x day
api_limitations: Reporting API rate limits and date-range caps; sub-publisher reports may be delayed or capped in row count
Data restatement common for up to 72h, especially after fraud filtering
identity_join_keys: campaign id, offer id, sub-publisher id
MMP site_id maps to sub-publisher id - the key join for fraud analysis
attribution_considerations: Sub-publisher level fraud analysis is essential on this class of network; blocklisting is the primary control
Discrepancy with MMP is typically higher than on SANs and requires an explicit tolerance band

pangle.role: UA demand source and ad network (ByteDance)
data_collected: spend, impressions, clicks, installs by campaign/geo/app
monetization revenue and eCPM if used as demand
pangle.granularity: campaign x geo x day; publisher app level where exposed
api_limitations: Rate limits and regional API endpoints (accounts may be region-partitioned); documentation and field availability differ between the global and CN platforms
Restatement up to 72h
attribution_considerations: Both a demand source for our UA and a demand partner in our mediation - the same partner name appears on both sides of the business and must be kept separate in reporting to avoid double-counting relationships

ironsource_levelplay.role: Mediation platform (monetization SoR for some titles) and UA demand (ironSource Ads)
data_collected: mediation: revenue, impressions, eCPM, fill rate, requests by network/instance/placement/country/ad unit
UA: spend, installs, campaign performance, publisher-level data
ironsource_levelplay.granularity: network x instance x placement x country x day; ULAR at impression level where enabled
ironsource_levelplay.update_frequency: mediation reporting hourly with a delay; ULAR near-real-time where enabled; revenue reconciled T+1 to T+3
api_limitations: Reporting API rate limits; some metrics available only at daily grain
Historical data windows limited on some endpoints
Instance-level configuration changes via API need careful validation
identity_join_keys: app key, instance id, placement, country
attribution_considerations: Running two mediation platforms across a portfolio (MAX on some titles, LevelPlay on others) requires a canonical monetization schema so eCPM and fill are comparable across titles - naming and definitions differ

cas_ai.role: Alternative mediation/monetization SDK used on selected titles
data_collected: revenue, impressions, eCPM, fill by network/format/geo
cas_ai.granularity: network x format x geo x day; user-level where supported
cas_ai.update_frequency: daily reporting with intraday estimates where available
api_limitations: Smaller platform: reporting API surface is narrower and rate limits are conservative; some data may require CSV export rather than API
Verify user-level ad revenue availability per account - the cohort ad-LTV pipeline depends on it and a fallback allocation method must exist where it is absent
identity_join_keys: app id, network, country; device ids where ULAR is available
attribution_considerations: Where user-level ad revenue is unavailable, cohort ad revenue must be allocated by impression share within the geo x day, which introduces bias for cohorts with unusual ad engagement - this bias must be labeled on any cohort using allocated rather than measured ad revenue
cas_ai.freshness_expectation: T+1 for reconciled; same-day estimates where offered
write_capabilities: mediation configuration where API-supported (treat as Recommend-only until write reliability is proven)

firebase.role: App analytics, crash reporting, and Remote Config - the product-side backbone
data_collected: Analytics events streamed to BigQuery (the export is the integration; the Firebase UI is not)
Remote Config parameter values, conditions, and version history
firebase.granularity: event-level with full parameter payloads and user properties; Remote Config at parameter x condition x version
firebase.update_frequency: BigQuery streaming export near-real-time (minutes) plus a daily batch table; Crashlytics near-real-time; Remote Config on publish
api_limitations: The daily BigQuery export table is finalized once per day and can differ from the streaming table - use streaming for realtime and the daily table for the record of truth, and never mix them in one query
Remote Config Admin API has quota limits on publish operations; template versions are the unit of change and rollback
GA4/Firebase event parameter cardinality limits can silently drop high-cardinality parameters
identity_join_keys: user_pseudo_id (Firebase instance id) - joins to our internal user id only if we explicitly set user_id
attribution_considerations: Firebase's own attribution is not used; the MMP is authoritative. Firebase data is behavioral, joined to cohorts via user_pseudo_id -> our user id -> MMP id.
Setting user_id in Firebase is mandatory for the join to work at all - a common integration gap that silently breaks cohort behavioral analysis
firebase.freshness_expectation: events <= 5 min (streaming); crash data <= 15 min; config changes immediate
write_capabilities: Remote Config parameter values via the Admin API with template versioning and one-call rollback to a prior version - the safest write surface in the entire platform

google_analytics_4.role: Secondary web/app analytics, primarily for web-to-app funnels and marketing site attribution
data_collected: events, sessions, user properties, traffic sources, conversion events
web funnel steps preceding app install
google_analytics_4.granularity: event-level via BigQuery export; aggregate via Data API
google_analytics_4.update_frequency: BigQuery export daily (streaming available); Data API near-real-time with sampling caveats
api_limitations: Data API has token-based quotas per property per day/hour and applies sampling and thresholding on large or high-cardinality queries
Cardinality limits cause 'other' bucketing that silently hides long-tail dimensions
Consent mode and modeled conversions mean some data is estimated rather than observed
identity_join_keys: UTM parameters carried into the app install via deferred deep links
attribution_considerations: Web-to-app attribution requires deep-link parameter passing; without it the funnel breaks at the store
GA4 attribution models differ from MMP models and must never be blended
google_analytics_4.freshness_expectation: T+1 for the record of truth; near-real-time for directional monitoring

mixpanel.role: Product analytics for behavioral cohorts, funnels and experiment readouts on selected titles
data_collected: events with properties, user profiles, cohorts, funnel and retention reports
mixpanel.update_frequency: ingestion near-real-time; Export API for raw events (day-partitioned); Query API for aggregates
api_limitations: Query API rate limits and concurrency caps; the raw Export API is heavily rate limited and intended for batch use, not for repeated large pulls
Historical exports are throttled and should be run as scheduled batch jobs
Cohort sync back into Mixpanel has size limits
identity_join_keys: distinct_id (must be set to our user id at identify time)
attribution_considerations: Mixpanel is behavioral, never attributional. Its cohorts are useful for product analysis; UA decisions always use the warehouse cohort model to avoid two competing definitions of the same cohort.
mixpanel.freshness_expectation: <= 15 min for queries; T+1 for raw export completeness

supabase.role: Application backend (Postgres) for LiveOps configuration, player accounts, and internal tooling state
data_collected: LiveOps event schedules and offer configuration
any game-server-side state relevant to marketing (progression snapshots, entitlements)
supabase.update_frequency: CDC (logical replication via Debezium) with sub-minute latency; nightly full-table snapshots as a reconciliation baseline
api_limitations: Direct Postgres access requires connection pooling discipline; the REST/PostgREST layer has row limits and is unsuitable for bulk export
Read replicas should be used for analytical extraction to avoid impacting the live application
Row Level Security policies can silently filter rows for the extraction role - the service role and its policy exposure must be explicitly verified
identity_join_keys: customer_user_id (the canonical join to the analytics user)
attribution_considerations: LiveOps schedule data is essential context for every revenue anomaly - a revenue spike during an unrecorded LiveOps event will be misdiagnosed by every agent that lacks it

internal_backend_databases.role: Game servers and services: authoritative economy, progression, entitlement and telemetry data
data_collected: matchmaking/social data where relevant to retention
internal_backend_databases.update_frequency: CDC streams for state tables; Kafka event streams for telemetry; hourly aggregate rollups
api_limitations: Analytical load must never touch production primaries - read replicas or CDC only
Schema changes are made by game teams on their own cadence; the data contract and schema registry are the only protection against silent breakage
Event volume is the largest in the platform (billions/day) and requires sampling policies for expensive analyses
attribution_considerations: Server-validated data is the truth for economy and purchases; client-reported values are used only for latency-sensitive realtime tiles and are always reconciled
Server-side data is the only reliable source for economy balance analysis

revenuecat.role: Subscription and IAP management with server-side receipt validation - the system of record for validated purchase state
data_collected: validated transactions, renewals, trials, cancellations, refunds, billing issues
revenue net of store commission where configured
revenuecat.update_frequency: webhooks in real time; REST API for state; scheduled data exports (S3/BigQuery) daily
api_limitations: REST API rate limits per project; the API is designed for per-subscriber lookups, not bulk analytics - use the scheduled export for analytics
Webhook delivery requires idempotent handling and a replay mechanism for missed events
Historical restatement occurs for refunds and billing retries
identity_join_keys: app_user_id (must be set to our customer_user_id)
attribution_considerations: Subscription revenue recognition differs from IAP: trials, grace periods and billing retries mean 'revenue' at a point in time is an estimate until settled
Refunds arrive late and must be attributed back to the original cohort, never to the refund date, or cohort LTV is systematically overstated then wrong
revenuecat.freshness_expectation: webhooks < 1 min; exports T+1; refunds settle over up to 30 days

app_store_connect.role: iOS store analytics, sales/finance reports, and SKAN reporting
data_collected: App Analytics: impressions, product page views, conversion rate, installs by source (search/browse/referral), retention, sessions
Sales and Trends reports: units and proceeds
Financial reports: settled revenue by region and currency
ratings, reviews, and app version metadata
app_store_connect.granularity: app x day x territory x source; finance at monthly settlement grain
app_store_connect.update_frequency: App Analytics T+1 (sometimes T+2); Sales reports daily; Financial reports monthly at settlement
api_limitations: The Analytics API surface is limited compared to the UI, and some UI metrics are not available programmatically; report-request-then-download workflows are required for the newer analytics reports
Sales reports are files, not queries, and must be downloaded and parsed daily - missing a day is not always recoverable
Rate limits per key; JWT tokens expire (typically 20 minutes) and must be refreshed
Data is not available before it is generated - there is no intraday store data
attribution_considerations: Store 'installs' (first opens / units) differ from MMP installs and from our SDK first-sessions - all three are tracked and reconciled; the store number is the most independent and is used as the reconciliation anchor
Product page conversion rate is the ASO metric; it cannot be joined to campaigns except through Custom Product Pages
app_store_connect.freshness_expectation: T+1 by 10:00 UTC for analytics; finance monthly

google_play_console.role: Android store analytics, financial reports, and ratings
data_collected: store listing performance: impressions, store listing visitors, conversion rate by traffic source
install/uninstall statistics by country, device, OS version, app version
google_play_console.granularity: app x day x country x dimension (device, OS, source)
google_play_console.update_frequency: reports delivered daily to a Cloud Storage bucket (the supported programmatic path); Play Developer API for release management
api_limitations: Most reporting is via GCS bucket CSV exports rather than a query API - the pipeline is a file-ingestion pipeline, with all the partial-file and late-file failure modes that implies
Reporting Data API coverage is narrower than the console UI
Publishing/release APIs have separate quotas and require careful handling during staged rollouts
attribution_considerations: Play install statistics count differently from MMP (device vs user, install vs first-open) and lag by 1-2 days
Uninstall data is available here and nowhere else - it is a valuable and underused retention signal
google_play_console.freshness_expectation: T+1 to T+2; Android vitals near-real-time for crashes

remote_config_systems.role: The primary safe write surface for product-side agent actions (Firebase Remote Config plus any in-house config service)
data_collected: parameter definitions, types, allowed ranges, default and conditional values
template version history with author, timestamp and diff
live-value telemetry from clients (what values are actually being served and received)
remote_config_systems.granularity: parameter x condition x version; client-received values sampled at session start
remote_config_systems.update_frequency: on publish (immediate); live-value telemetry every 15 minutes; drift check every 15 minutes
api_limitations: Publish quotas limit how frequently templates can be updated - agent config actions must be batched and rate-limited

Propagation to clients is not instantaneous: clients fetch on their own cadence (typically session start with a minimum fetch interval), so the measured effect of a config change ramps over hours and must never be evaluated in the first 30-60 minutes
Conditions are evaluated client-side, so targeting errors are only visible in the live-value telemetry, not in the template
identity_join_keys: app instance id for live-value telemetry
attribution_considerations: Config changes are the most common unrecorded cause of metric movements. Every publish is captured as a first-class change event on the timeline with its diff, blast radius estimate and author - without this, root cause analysis across the whole platform degrades severely.
remote_config_systems.freshness_expectation: publish immediate; effective rollout 1-6 hours depending on client fetch cadence; drift detection <= 15 min
write_capabilities: set parameter value within declared type/range
revert to a prior template version (single call, the preferred agent action)

competitive_intelligence_feeds.role: External market context (Sensor Tower / data.ai / Apptopia class providers plus network changelogs)
data_collected: network policy changelogs and status pages (scraped and summarized)
competitive_intelligence_feeds.granularity: app x country x day (estimates); creative-level for ad libraries
competitive_intelligence_feeds.update_frequency: daily for estimates; every 4 hours for changelog scraping
api_limitations: Provider APIs are seat/quota limited and expensive per call - caching and selective refresh are mandatory
Estimates carry substantial error, especially for smaller apps and non-US markets
attribution_considerations: These are estimates, not measurements, and are hard-capped at 0.5 confidence in every agent decision; they inform context, never action

install_count_reconciliation.method: daily four-way comparison per title x geo x platform with tolerance bands per pair; the internal SDK first-session count is the anchor for total volume, the MMP is the anchor for attribution, and the store is the independent check

revenue_reconciliation.method: daily comparison with the store financial report as the ultimate authority at monthly settlement; intermediate sources are estimates and are labeled as such

ad_revenue_reconciliation.method: daily variance tracking per network with a correction factor applied to pLTV inputs when drift exceeds 8%

spend_reconciliation.method: daily API-vs-ETL comparison, monthly invoice reconciliation; invoices are authoritative for finance, API cost is authoritative for operational decisions

patterns.technology: Kafka/Redpanda -> Flink for enrichment and windowed aggregation -> ClickHouse (realtime serving) + object storage (bronze)
object storage event notification -> loader -> bronze with file-level idempotency and completeness checks

Dagster/Airflow-scheduled connectors with token-bucket rate limiting, checkpointed incremental windows, and automatic re-pull of the trailing restatement window (7 days for cost, 30 days for conversions)
API gateway -> queue -> idempotent consumer with replay capability

ingestion_architecture_summary.restatement_handling: Every API-pull connector re-pulls a trailing window on every run (cost: 7 days, conversions: 30 days, revenue: 3 days). Restatements write new rows with an incremented restatement_generation rather than updating in place, so 'what we believed at time T' is always reconstructible - which is what makes an agent's historical decision defensible.
ingestion_architecture_summary.backfill_policy: Backfills run on a separate rate-limit budget and a lower-priority queue, are chunked by partition, and are gated by Janitor to avoid competing with realtime ingestion during business hours.

cross_module_interactions.name: Ad revenue decline traced to acquisition source quality
cross_module_interactions.trigger: Vault detects T1 ad_arpdau in BR below forecast p05 for 2 consecutive hours; daily projection -9.2% vs weekday-matched baseline.

chain.action: Changepoint localized to 2026-08-24 06:00-07:00 UTC (BOCPD posterior 0.91). Contribution attribution: geo=BR carries 84% of the aggregate move; format=rewarded carries 71% within BR. Emits KPI_ANOMALY.

Runs the ARPDAU decomposition: eCPM -1.2% (within noise), fill 99.1% (unchanged), show rate unchanged, impressions_per_dau -11.4% (dominant). Cause class = SUPPLY or MIX, not DEMAND. Emits AD_REVENUE_CHANGE with cause_class candidates.
Queried for config/version changes in the window for BR: none. Rules out the SUPPLY/config hypothesis (posterior drops from 0.45 to 0.08).

DAU acquisition-mix analysis: the share of BR DAU acquired from media_source=X rose from 11% to 29% over 9 days. Those users' impressions_per_dau is 4.1 vs the BR average of 7.9 - they simply consume fewer ads. Emits COHORT_QUALITY_CHANGE. The aggregate decline is a mix effect, not a monetization failure.

Identifies the 4 campaigns responsible for 91% of the source-X BR volume; combined spend $14.2k/day. Their cohort ad-LTV is $0.31 vs the BR portfolio average $0.74, while their CPI is only 18% lower - so they are economically worse despite looking cheaper.
Recomputes: these cohorts' P(target ROAS) = 0.22. Allowable CPI for the slice is $0.94 against an actual CPI of $1.46.

Merges all findings into one incident. Rejects the naive monetization response (raising BR floors would not help - eCPM was never the problem and raising floors would cut fill). Authorizes a 40% budget reduction on the 4 campaigns, staged 20% + 20% over 48h, plus a bid-target reduction to the allowable CPI. Explicitly instructs Vault to take no monetization action.
Executes step 1 (-20%, within the autonomous band); step 2 queued pending the 24h checkpoint.

Registers predictions: BR ad_arpdau recovers to within 3% of baseline by +7d as the DAU mix normalizes; portfolio margin +$41k/30d. Measurement scheduled at +24h/+72h/+7d against matched BR cohorts from other sources.

cross_module_interactions.prevented_failure: Without Prism's mix analysis, Vault would have concluded 'monetization degradation in BR' and tuned floors - a change that would have reduced fill, made revenue worse, and left the real cause (a bad traffic source scaling) untouched for weeks.
cross_module_interactions.elapsed_time: 11 minutes from anomaly to first executed action

cross_module_interactions.name: Excellent CPI blocked by cohort economics (the canonical scaling trap)
cross_module_interactions.trigger: Hunter's scaling evaluation flags campaign 23851 (Meta, T2, US iOS): CPI $1.82 vs $2.40 baseline, budget utilization 97%, marginal ROAS from the fitted curve above target.

chain.action: Generates a +20% budget proposal ($3.1k/day increase) and, as required, requests the cohort-economics gate from Oracle before submitting.
P(D180 ROAS >= target) = 0.19 [interval 0.11-0.29]. Predicted D180 ROAS 0.63 vs 1.25 target. Payback projected at 168 days vs the 120-day hard constraint.

D7 retention for the campaign's last 3 cohorts is 9.1% vs the 14.8% corridor floor; the decline is within-slice (mix-adjusted) and confined to this campaign, not the title. Classification: ACQUISITION cause.
Ad ARPDAU of these cohorts is declining 6% w/w - they are both retaining worse and monetizing worse, which rules out 'cheap but fine' users.
Organic uplift factor for T2 US is 0.28, so the true effective CPI is $2.33, not $1.82 - most of the apparent CPI advantage is organic cannibalization.
Portfolio EV of the proposed scale = -$34k/30d against a local EV of +$11k. Hard constraint (payback) violated. DENIES the scale with a full explanation posted to the UA cockpit.
Dispatched to localize: 78% of the retention deficit is carried by placement=audience_network x device_tier=low, which represents 31% of the campaign's spend but 64% of its installs.

Authorizes a surgical placement + device-tier exclusion rather than a budget cut. Pre-registers the expectation that CPI will RISE to approximately $2.20 and volume will fall about 30% - and Herald communicates this to the UA manager in advance so a rising CPI is not misread as a failure.
Executes the exclusion (autonomous: affected spend 31% <= 25%? No - 31% exceeds the 25% autonomous bound, so it is routed as a Mode 2 proposal and approved by the UA lead in 40 minutes).
At +7d: CPI $2.18 (predicted $2.20), D7 retention 15.6% (above corridor floor), P(target ROAS) 0.71. The campaign becomes a legitimate scaling candidate two weeks later.

cross_module_interactions.prevented_failure: Scaling would have added roughly $93k of spend over 30 days at a projected 0.63 ROAS - approximately $34k of destroyed margin - while making the campaign's headline CPI look even better.
cross_module_interactions.elapsed_time: 6 minutes to denial; 52 minutes to the corrective action

cross_module_interactions.name: Creative fatigue caught before CPI deteriorates
cross_module_interactions.trigger: Muse's 6-hourly fatigue pass: creative cr_88431 CFI 0.58 (critical) on Meta US iOS at 2.1M cumulative impressions.

chain.action: IPM fell 14.2 -> 8.9 over 11 days. Peer check: concurrent creatives in the same (network x geo x placement) cells fell only 6%, so this is creative-specific, not auction-wide. CTR decomposition shows the decline is hook-side (CTR down 38%) not store-side (CVR flat). Emits CREATIVE_FATIGUE.
