Confirms no market-wide CPM event in these cells; also notes that this creative's concept now appears in 34% of tracked competitor creatives in US casual - concept saturation is accelerating fatigue portfolio-wide, not just for this asset.
Identifies that cr_88431 carries 31% of campaign 41229's delivery and 12% of the title's US iOS spend. CPI has risen only 4% so far - the damage has not yet surfaced in the metric UA managers watch.

Finds 2 qualified replacements from the same concept cluster (tested IPM 13.8 and 12.9, cohort quality above peer P25). Projects that doing nothing costs about $8.9k over 14 days in CPI inflation and volume loss.

Authorizes a staged rotation: 40% of the fatigued creative's budget share to replacements now, remainder over 48h contingent on IPM recovery. Also raises a Sev-3 to the Creative Lead about concept saturation, with a production brief request for a differentiated concept.
Executes step 1 autonomously (affected spend within bounds, confidence 0.84, replacements available, creative below the 40% delivery ceiling).

Measures at +72h against matched adsets that were not rotated: IPM recovered to 12.6, CPI held flat instead of rising, volume maintained. Playbook 'staged rotation' hit rate updated to 0.81 over 27 applications.

cross_module_interactions.prevented_failure: The conventional workflow catches fatigue when CPI has already risen 15-25%, which is typically 5-9 days and $20-40k later on a campaign this size.

cross_module_interactions.name: Product regression triggers UA throttle before cohorts are poisoned
cross_module_interactions.trigger: Pulse detects tutorial step 4 conversion falling 92% -> 78% on Android device_tier=low, app_version 3.8.0 at 41% adoption.

chain.action: p90 step time rose 4.1s -> 11.6s: a performance regression (asset loading), not a design change. Changepoint aligns with the 3.8.0 staged rollout. Confidence 0.88. Emits KPI_ANOMALY + RELEASE_HEALTH_DEGRADED.

Early-signal model predicts D7 retention for cohorts installing since the rollout at 11.2% vs 14.9% baseline for the affected segment. Emits RETENTION_DECLINE (predicted). Universality test: confined to Android low-tier, so it is a PRODUCT cause and no UA source is at fault.
Translates to pLTV: -18% for affected installs, which are 38% of daily Android volume. Portfolio LTV impact approximately -$21k per day of continued acquisition at current spend.

Two parallel tracks, because the fix and the mitigation have different owners and different speeds: (a) Sev-1 to engineering with the halt-rollout recommendation and the asset-loading diagnosis; (b) instruct Hunter to reduce Android low-tier-heavy campaign spend by 25% until the fix ships - not to cut good campaigns permanently, but to stop buying users into a broken experience.

Applies device-tier bid modifiers where supported and budget reductions where not, on 7 campaigns. Registers that this is a temporary, product-caused throttle with an automatic restoration trigger, so the throttle does not silently become permanent.
Halts the rollout at 41%, ships a hotfix in 14 hours.
Confirms step-4 conversion recovered to 91% on 3.8.1. Emits RELEASE_HEALTH_RESTORED.
Automatically restores the throttled budgets (the restoration trigger fires), staged over 24h.

Cohorts acquired during the incident window are tagged so they are excluded from campaign quality baselines - otherwise the product bug would permanently and wrongly damage those campaigns' historical quality scores and future bid targets.

cross_module_interactions.prevented_failure: Two failures at once: 2-3 days of acquiring users into a broken onboarding, and the subsequent misattribution of that damage to the UA campaigns that happened to be running.
cross_module_interactions.elapsed_time: 22 minutes from detection to both tracks in motion

cross_module_interactions.name: Attribution fraud detected and priced into budget
cross_module_interactions.trigger: Compass's 6-hourly fraud scan: Mintegral T3 Android CTIT distribution develops 34% mass below 8 seconds (baseline 4%).

chain.action: Localizes to 3 sub-publishers (61% of that campaign's spend). Corroborating signals: new-device ratio 0.94, D1 retention 2.1% vs 31% for the campaign's other sub-publishers. Three independent signals -> confidence 0.91. Classification: click injection. Emits ATTRIBUTION_DISCREPANCY + FRAUD_DETECTED.
Confirms these installs' cohort quality index is 4.2 sigma below the source baseline and that they carry essentially zero downstream revenue.
Blocklists the 3 sub-publishers autonomously (within the fraud grant), and generates a claw-back packet estimating $22.4k of fraudulent spend over 18 days.

Critically, reduces the campaign's budget by the corresponding share. Without this, the network's optimizer will simply reallocate the same budget to other sub-publishers, and the campaign will 'recover' its install volume with different, possibly equally bad, traffic - the classic blocklist-whack-a-mole failure.

Recomputes the campaign's historical cohort quality excluding fraudulent installs: the genuine traffic's P(target ROAS) is 0.58, materially better than the contaminated 0.31. The campaign is worth keeping, at a lower budget - a conclusion impossible without separating the fraud.

Authorizes the blocklist plus the budget reduction, routes the claw-back packet to the Head of UA for filing (deadline flagged), and schedules a 14-day re-scan for displacement fraud on the same campaign.

Measures: post-blocklist campaign D1 retention 29.4% (from 19.1%), CPI rose 41% (expected and correct - we are now paying for real installs only), P(target ROAS) 0.61. Fraud detector thresholds retuned from the confirmed case.

cross_module_interactions.prevented_failure: Blocklisting alone leaves the budget in place and lets the network refill it. Cutting the campaign entirely would have discarded genuinely profitable traffic. Only the joint action is correct.

cross_module_interactions.name: Monetization change blocked by the retention frontier
cross_module_interactions.trigger: Vault identifies that reducing the interstitial cooldown from 45s to 30s would raise ad ARPDAU by an estimated 6.2% on T1.

chain.action: Proposes the change; the ad-load frontier check is mandatory for any exposure-increasing proposal.
Frontier model: T1 users above 9.4 impressions/DAU show a D7 retention decline; the proposed change moves the median from 8.1 to 10.3, crossing the frontier for approximately 44% of DAU.
Net LTV computation: +$0.041/user ad revenue, -$0.072/user from the retention-driven loss of future sessions and future ad impressions. Net -$0.031/user (-2.4%), with the interval excluding zero.

Denies the blanket change. Instead authorizes an experiment: Lab runs a 3-arm test (45s control / 38s / 30s) at 10% traffic with D7 retention as a pre-registered guardrail, so the frontier is measured rather than modeled.

Runs 14 days. Result: 38s yields ad ARPDAU +3.1% [+1.9,+4.3] with D7 retention -0.4pp [-0.9,+0.1] (not significant, inside the guardrail). 30s yields ARPDAU +6.0% but D7 -1.9pp, breaching the guardrail - the variant is auto-stopped at day 9.
Net LTV for the 38s variant: +$0.019/user, positive with the interval above zero.
Recommends shipping 38s (human approval required - config ships are never autonomous). Estimated portfolio value +$310k/year.

Records that the frontier model's prediction for the 30s arm was directionally correct but underestimated the magnitude by 35%; the frontier is refit with the experimental data - the highest-quality evidence available.

cross_module_interactions.prevented_failure: A revenue-positive, LTV-negative change that would have looked like a monetization win for a full quarter before the retention cost surfaced in cohort data.
cross_module_interactions.elapsed_time: 18 minutes to the experiment decision; 14 days to the answer

cross_module_interactions.name: Budget pacing risk resolved by economics-aware reallocation
cross_module_interactions.trigger: Ledger projects month-end spend at $7.14M vs a $7.50M envelope (-4.8%) with 9 days remaining.

chain.action: Decomposes the gap: 78% is Meta T1, where delivery is bid-limited (budget utilization 71% at a $1.90 target CPA), not budget-limited. Emits BUDGET_PACING_RISK.

Prices the two remedies. (a) Raising Meta's target CPA to $2.15 would unlock roughly $210k of spend at a marginal D180 ROAS of 1.19 - below the 1.25 target, so margin-dilutive. (b) Moving $180k to Google AC iOS, which still has headroom at marginal ROAS 1.34.
Confirms the Google AC campaigns are budget-limited (utilization 96%), have no open quality findings, and their creatives are below fatigue thresholds - all scaling preconditions hold.
Forecasts that option (b) closes 84% of the pacing gap; the residual underspend of ~$58k is acceptable and preferable to dilutive spending.

Selects (b) plus a partial (a): a smaller CPA increase to $2.02 on the 2 Meta adsets whose marginal ROAS is above target, rather than all of them. Rejects the reflexive 'spend the envelope' framing explicitly in the explanation.
Builds a 4-step staged package; steps execute autonomously with 24h checkpoints after the Head of UA approves the package.

Step 2's measured install lift fell outside its prediction interval (the Google campaigns saturated faster than the curve predicted). The package auto-halts, Ledger re-optimizes, and the spend-response curve for those campaigns is refit with the new evidence - which is exactly what staging is for.

cross_module_interactions.prevented_failure: The reflex response - raise budgets everywhere to hit the number - would have added ~$210k at 1.19 marginal ROAS, spending the envelope while reducing margin.
cross_module_interactions.elapsed_time: 9 minutes to proposal; 3 days of staged execution

cross_module_interactions.name: LTV model drift triggers a fleet-wide safety interlock
cross_module_interactions.trigger: Oracle's hourly model-health check: rolling 14d D30 pLTV MAPE reaches 0.34 (threshold 0.30) with a systematic +19% bias on Mintegral Android T3 cohorts.

chain.action: Runs the model-vs-reality discrimination test: are all cohorts deviating (model problem) or only some (reality problem)? Deviation is concentrated in one source x platform x geo-tier cell, so it is partly real - but feature PSI on ad_impressions_d0 is 0.31, indicating an input distribution shift as well. Both are true: the input changed and the model has not adapted.
Confirms the input cause: ULAR-vs-reconciled variance for that network has been 11% for 6 days (above the 8% threshold), so the model has been fed inflated D0 ad revenue.
Emits MODEL_DEGRADED scoped to Mintegral Android T3. Applies a bounded -11% correction factor to the ad revenue input, time-boxed to 14 days, and widens prediction intervals for the affected scope.

Demotes every pLTV-dependent autonomous action within that scope to Recommend. Actions outside the scope continue - the interlock is surgical, not global, because a blunt global freeze has its own cost.

Reviews the last 30 days of decisions made using the biased inputs: 14 actions identified, of which 3 (scaling decisions) may have been wrong. Those 3 campaigns are re-evaluated with corrected inputs; 1 is rolled back.
Opens a reconciliation incident with the network; the root cause turns out to be a mediation SDK update changing revenue estimation.
Retrains with corrected data; the challenger beats the champion on the holdout; Head of Data approves promotion. Autonomy is restored to the scope after 5 days of clean calibration.

cross_module_interactions.prevented_failure: Nineteen percent over-prediction of LTV would have caused systematic over-scaling of a bad source. The retrospective review of decisions made on bad inputs is as important as stopping new ones - a step most automated systems omit entirely.
cross_module_interactions.elapsed_time: 4 minutes to the interlock; 5 days to full restoration

cross_module_interactions.name: Market-wide CPM spike prevents 34 wrong internal actions
cross_module_interactions.trigger: Sentinel fires CPI-spike anomalies on 34 campaigns across 3 networks within 40 minutes.

chain.action: Recognizes the cluster (>= 5 correlated anomalies sharing a dimension) and escalates it as ONE incident rather than routing 34 alerts.

Market CPM index for casual-puzzle US iOS is up 21% w/w; the breadth test shows 79% of unrelated campaigns in the same cells moved together; two tracked competitors launched major campaigns on 2026-08-24. Emits MARKET_CONTEXT with a market-wide verdict.

Downgrades all 34 entity-specific findings to informational and blocks entity-specific corrective actions on them. Cutting budgets into a temporary auction spike surrenders share and costs more to re-enter than to ride out.
Recomputes the economics at the elevated CPM: 26 campaigns remain above target ROAS even at the higher CPI; 8 fall below. Only the 8 need any action, and only if the spike persists.

Authorizes a hold with a defined checkpoint: re-evaluate at the end of the competitor flight window (estimated 2026-09-02 from Scout's history of similar events). For the 8 below-target campaigns, authorizes a modest 15% throttle rather than a cut, preserving learning-phase state.

Sends ONE message to the Head of UA explaining the market event, the decision to hold, the 8 exceptions, and the checkpoint date - instead of 34 alerts that would have burned the channel's credibility.
At the checkpoint, CPMs normalized to +4% vs baseline. Suppression judged correct. Scout's suppression precision updated to 0.92 over 24 events.

cross_module_interactions.prevented_failure: Thirty-four reflexive budget cuts, roughly $47k/day of volume surrendered into a 9-day auction event, followed by an expensive re-entry into a market where competitors had gained share.

cross_module_interactions.name: IAP offer lapse detected through an LTV anomaly
cross_module_interactions.trigger: Oracle: T2 cohorts from 2026-08-17 onward are tracking 22% below their own D7 pLTV predictions.

chain.action: Decomposes the gap: ad revenue per install is on-model; IAP revenue per install is 46% below. Retention is on-model. So this is a monetization problem, not a traffic-quality problem - which means the correct action is NOT a UA action.

First-purchase rate for D0-D3 fell 2.1% -> 1.2%. Purchase funnel: paywall impressions and opens flat, checkout-initiated -> success down only 1pp. So exposure and technical execution are fine; demand collapsed.

Checks the offer calendar: the starter-pack SKU (t2_starter_499) ended 2026-08-16 23:59 UTC with no successor scheduled. It had contributed 31% of D0-D3 IAP revenue. Emits IAP_ANOMALY with a near-deterministic cause.
Confirms no config or experiment change in the window that would explain it; the offer's absence is the only change.

Because the identical offer configuration ran within the last 45 days and was previously approved, this qualifies as a restoration rather than a new commercial decision. Authorizes Merchant's autonomous restore, with immediate notification to the monetization PM.
Restores the offer. Estimated recovery $47k over 30 days.

Also raises a process finding: no automated successor-scheduling exists for revenue-material offers. Recommends a calendar-integrity check as a permanent detector - fixing the class of failure, not just the instance.

At +7d, cohort pLTV returns to within 4% of prediction. The affected cohorts (Aug 17-26) are tagged so their depressed LTV does not permanently damage the quality scores of the campaigns that acquired them.

cross_module_interactions.prevented_failure: This class of failure typically surfaces 3-6 weeks later during a monthly review, by which time 4-6 weeks of cohorts carry permanently depressed LTV and several campaigns have been wrongly throttled for 'poor traffic quality'.

cross_module_interactions.name: Store listing regression surfaces as an organic install decline
cross_module_interactions.trigger: Beacon: T1 organic installs in DE are 19% below the uplift model's 90% band for 4 consecutive days despite paid spend being up 8%.

chain.action: Store funnel decomposition: impressions flat, product-page-view -> install conversion fell 31% -> 24%. This is a conversion problem, not a discovery problem.
Store listing version history: the German localized screenshots reverted to English on 2026-08-23 (listing version 14) - a regression introduced during an unrelated metadata update.

Flags the second-order effect: paid campaigns in DE also route through the same store page, so paid CVR fell too - the reported paid CPI rose 14% in DE and would otherwise have been diagnosed as a campaign or creative problem.
Retroactively links 6 open DE campaign anomalies to this single root cause and merges them into the incident, closing them as explained.

Routes the store fix to the ASO owner (store changes are never autonomous), and instructs Hunter to hold DE budgets rather than cut them, since the CPI increase is caused by a fixable store issue and the traffic itself is fine.
Estimates loss at 1,900 organic installs/day (~$6.5k/day of equivalent paid value) plus the paid CVR drag.

After the fix, conversion recovers to 30.4% within 48 hours. A new detector is proposed: alert on any store listing version change that is not linked to a planned ASO ticket - closing the loop on the process gap.

cross_module_interactions.prevented_failure: Six campaign-level CPI investigations, probable budget cuts in a healthy market, and weeks of unexplained organic decline.

cross_module_interactions.name: Internal auction cannibalization between two titles
cross_module_interactions.trigger: Ledger observes correlated CPM increases across T1 and T3 US iOS campaigns with no corresponding market index movement.

chain.action: Market index for the relevant cells is flat (+2%), so this is internal, not external. The breadth test fails, which is itself informative.

Audience overlap analysis: T1 and T3 US iOS campaigns share an estimated 47% audience overlap (both target casual-game lookalikes from the same seed characteristics). T3's spend rose 60% over 8 days following a scale-up, exactly when T1's CPM began rising.

This is a conflict only visible at portfolio level - no single-title agent can see it. Computes the joint effect: T3's incremental spend generated $19k of incremental margin but raised T1's CPMs enough to cost $23k. Net portfolio effect is negative despite T3's own metrics looking excellent.
Confirms T3's marginal ROAS on the incremental spend is 1.31 in isolation, but 0.88 once T1's CPM externality is included - the difference between a local and a portfolio view.

Authorizes deconfliction: narrow T3's audience definition to reduce overlap to under 25%, and cap T3's US iOS spend at the point where the joint marginal effect is zero. Proposes a longer-term structural fix (portfolio-level audience deconfliction rules) as a Recommend item.

Registers the prediction that T1 CPMs fall approximately 9% within 5 days. Measured at +7d: -7.4%, within interval. The cannibalization elasticity is added to the cross-effect matrix so future scale proposals price this externality automatically.

cross_module_interactions.prevented_failure: Both titles' agents would have kept optimizing locally forever - T3 scaling profitably by its own numbers while quietly taxing T1. Nothing in either title's dashboard would ever reveal it.
cross_module_interactions.elapsed_time: 3 days to detect (slow-building signal); 12 minutes to resolve once detected

cross_module_interactions.name: Data pipeline failure prevents a cascade of wrong actions
cross_module_interactions.trigger: AppsFlyer Data Locker partition for 2026-08-26 lands 94 minutes late and 12% short on row count.

chain.action: Detects both the freshness breach and the volume anomaly. Estimates completeness at 88% from the source's historical arrival curve. Marks fct_installs degraded for that partition.

The Action Gateway begins denying any action whose lineage includes fct_installs for that date. Seven pending autonomous actions are held; 3 agents (Hunter, Prism, Oracle) are gated on the affected scope.

Would otherwise have fired 40+ 'install volume collapse' anomalies. The data-degraded state suppresses them at source - a partial load looks exactly like a business catastrophe, and this is precisely the scenario that destroys trust in automated systems.

Historical restatement for this source at T+94min is 8-14%, so the shortfall is consistent with normal lateness rather than data loss. Publishes the completeness estimate with its interval and a projected full-arrival time.
One informational message to Growth Ops: what is late, what is blocked, when it is expected. No panic, no alerts to UA managers.

At +40 minutes, completeness reaches 99.2%; the degraded flag is lifted; the held actions are re-evaluated against the now-complete data. Two of the seven are no longer justified and are dropped - direct evidence that acting on the partial data would have been wrong.

Records the near-miss: 2 of 7 actions would have been incorrect, with an estimated avoided cost of $6.8k. This is the ongoing justification for the data gate's existence, quantified rather than assumed.

cross_module_interactions.prevented_failure: A 40-alert storm and up to 7 automated actions taken on 88%-complete data - the most common way autonomous marketing systems destroy value and trust simultaneously.
cross_module_interactions.elapsed_time: Detection in 3 minutes; resolution in 137 minutes

cross_module_interactions.name: Creative concept insight rewrites the production brief and the bid targets
cross_module_interactions.trigger: Muse's weekly attribute-learning refit across 412 creatives over 90 days.

chain.action: Finds that creatives whose first frame shows real gameplay have 28% lower IPM but 41% higher D7 retention and 0.14 higher D30 ROAS than stylized-render hooks, controlling for network, geo and campaign via a mixed-effects model.

Confirms with cohort data: the cohorts acquired by authentic-gameplay creatives have a materially different composition - fewer immediate churners, higher payer conversion - and the effect holds within every geo tier.

Computes net margin per dollar: authentic creatives are 19% better despite worse acquisition metrics. This inverts the ranking that every network optimizer and every conventional creative scorecard produces.

Three coordinated outputs: (a) a production brief recommending a shift in the concept mix, with expected value; (b) a change to Muse's creative quality score weighting to increase the downstream-ROAS component; (c) a note to Hunter that campaigns running authentic-gameplay creatives should have their allowable CPI raised, because their users are genuinely worth more.
Approves the brief; 12 new creatives are produced against the attribute target over 3 weeks.
Tracks the new cohort of creatives: 8 of 12 outperform their attribute-based prior; the prior is updated with the new evidence.
At +90 days, measures the portfolio effect via the concept-mix shift: D30 ROAS +0.06 portfolio-wide on affected titles, attributable via the manual-managed holdout which did not receive the brief.

cross_module_interactions.prevented_failure: Optimizing creative on IPM alone - which is what every network's optimizer does by default - systematically selects for misleading creatives and slowly poisons cohort quality across the whole portfolio.
cross_module_interactions.elapsed_time: Weekly cycle; 90 days to measured portfolio effect

transport.technology: Kafka (or Redpanda) with a Schema Registry (Avro/Protobuf) and a compacted topic for entity state; Flink for stream joins and windowed correlation; Postgres outbox pattern for transactional event emission from agents so an event is never emitted for an action that did not commit.

topics.retention: 7 years (also mirrored to WORM object storage)
topics.purpose: proposals, approvals, executions, rollbacks - the audit spine
market context, data health, model health, freeze state - latest value wins
outcome measurements feeding the learning loop
dead letters with the original payload and failure reason

transport.ordering_guarantee: Per-key ordering (entity_id), which is what matters: all events about one campaign are ordered. Global ordering is neither needed nor attempted.
transport.delivery_semantics: At-least-once delivery with idempotent consumers. Every event carries an event_id (UUIDv7, time-sortable) and consumers maintain a processed-id set with a 24h window.
transport.backpressure: Consumers report lag; when an agent's lag exceeds 5 minutes on a realtime topic, it sheds low-priority work (T3 series screening) before high-priority work, and Warden downgrades it to Observe if lag exceeds 30 minutes - a lagging agent is acting on stale reality.

fields.event_type: one of the registered types below
fields.occurred_at: when the underlying change happened (the changepoint), not when it was detected

entity.path: hierarchical path for rollup, e.g. portfolio/T1/meta/23851/adset_991

scope.dimensions: the dimension slice this event applies to

fields.correlation_id: shared by all events in one investigation or causal chain
fields.causation_id: the event_id that directly caused this one
fields.incident_id: set once the orchestrator merges it into an incident

data_snapshot.datasets: list with their as-of timestamps and completeness

fields.evidence_ref: pointer to the immutable evidence bundle in object storage
fields.ttl: when this event's conclusion expires and must be re-derived

envelope_schema.validation: Schema Registry enforces compatibility (backward-compatible evolution only). An event failing validation goes to the DLQ and raises a platform alert - it is never silently dropped, because a dropped finding is an invisible failure.

event_types.description: A monitored series deviated materially from expectation, with the change localized in time and dimension space.
publishers: any agent detecting within its own scope
subscribers: the owning domain agent (routed by metric family)
event_types.typical_volume: 80-200/day after suppression and merging (from ~15k raw detector fires)

event_types.description: A campaign's delivery or efficiency changed materially, with the CPI decomposition attached.
A within-slice, mix-adjusted retention decline, actual or predicted, with its product-vs-acquisition classification.
event_types.criticality: This is the highest-weight early signal in the system; Hunter treats it as a scaling veto.

event_types.description: A material change in predicted LTV, P(target ROAS), or allowable CPI for a slice.
payload: previous and new pLTV with intervals
whether this is a real change or a model change

event_types.description: A material ad revenue or ad ARPDAU change with its cause class.
payload: ARPDAU decomposition (imp-per-DAU / eCPM / fill / show / DAU-mix contributions)

event_types.description: A change in IAP revenue, payer conversion, offer performance, or checkout health.
A creative's efficiency is decaying beyond its peer-adjusted expectation, or a creative is acquiring poor-quality cohorts.
payload: qualified replacements with their tested metrics

event_types.description: Measurement systems disagree beyond tolerance, or measurement quality has degraded.
payload: mechanical checklist results (which configuration causes were eliminated)

event_types.description: Projected spend will breach the envelope, or allocation is materially inefficient.
payload: MTD actual, plan, projection with interval
delivery constraint classification per contributing campaign
remedy options with their marginal ROAS

event_types.description: A cohort slice's quality index or composition changed materially.
payload: composition shift (JS divergence and the shifted dimensions)

event_types.description: External conditions that explain or contextualize internal movements.
payload: breadth test result (fraction of unrelated entities moving together)

event_types.description: Dataset health transitions: healthy, degraded, quarantined, restored.
event_types.criticality: Consumed as a hard gate, not as advice.

event_types.description: A model's accuracy, calibration or drift state changed materially.
An app version or config bundle is harming core metrics, or has recovered.
payload: affected metrics with deltas and significance

subscribers: all agents (as change context - this is what makes root-cause alignment possible)

event_types.description: A fully specified, executable action awaiting authorization.

payload: reason with the binding constraint if denied
event_types.criticality: Denials are as important as approvals - they are the record of the system's judgment and the primary training signal for calibration.

event_types.description: An action was committed against an external system.

payload: measured values vs the trigger thresholds
event_types.criticality: Rollback rate is a core safety KPI and drives automatic demotion.

event_types.description: The realized outcome of a prediction or action, with its counterfactual.

event_types.criticality: Bypasses all rate limits and reaches every agent within seconds.

highest_fan_out_publishers: Janitor (DATA_HEALTH_STATE - every agent gates on it)
Oracle (LTV_FORECAST_CHANGE - every economic decision depends on it)
Lab (CONFIG_CHANGED - the alignment substrate for all root-cause work)
Scout (MARKET_CONTEXT - the external frame for every diagnosis)
publisher_subscriber_matrix_summary.design_note: Agents never call each other synchronously. All coordination is through events plus orchestrator-mediated dispatch, so an agent failure degrades the system gracefully instead of cascading. The only synchronous call in the system is the Action Gateway's policy evaluation, which is deliberately fast (p99 < 50ms) and fails closed.

replay_and_recovery.replay: Any agent can replay a topic from a timestamp to rebuild its state; consumers are idempotent so replay is safe. This is used after a bug fix to re-derive findings from historical evidence.
replay_and_recovery.evidence_immutability: Evidence bundles are written to object storage with content-addressed keys before the event is emitted, so an event's evidence can never drift from what the agent actually saw - which is what makes retrospective audits meaningful.
replay_and_recovery.dead_letter_handling: DLQ entries are reviewed daily; a DLQ entry on mart.actions.v1 is a Sev-2 because an action event that failed to publish means the audit record is incomplete.

decision_engine.purpose: A single, deterministic, auditable scoring layer that every agent and the orchestrator share. It converts heterogeneous findings into comparable numbers so that a monetization issue, a creative issue and a budget issue can be ranked against each other on one scale - and so that the same input always produces the same decision, which is what makes the system debuggable.
design_rules: All scores are computed in deterministic code, never by the LLM.
Every score is decomposable: the UI and the audit record show each component's contribution, so a human can see exactly why something scored 82 and not 60.
Scores are calibrated against outcomes weekly, so the numbers mean something empirically rather than being an arbitrary index.
No score is ever displayed without its inputs' sample sizes and data freshness.

confidence_model.then: confidence = calibrate(confidence_raw | agent, finding_type) using the isotonic transform fitted weekly by Scholar on realized outcomes. Only calibrated confidence may gate an action.

components.computation: For threshold detections: min(1, |z| / 5). For model-based: 1 - p_value, or the posterior probability of the changepoint. For experiments: the posterior probability the effect exceeds the practical significance threshold.
PRODUCT over lineage datasets of (freshness_factor x completeness x (1 - expected_restatement)). freshness_factor = 1 if within SLO, else max(0, 1 - lag_excess/SLO).
components.example: one dataset at 98% complete with 5% expected restatement and fresh -> 0.98 * 0.95 = 0.93

components.computation: min(1, sqrt(n / n_required)) where n_required is the metric's minimum for detecting the observed effect size at 80% power. The square root is deliberate: it rewards exceeding the minimum with diminishing returns rather than treating 10x the minimum as 10x the confidence.

(number of independent confirming signals) / (number checked), where 'independent' means the signals do not share a common data source or derivation. Zero checked signals scores 0.3 (neutral-low), not 0.
components.example: retention decline confirmed by session-depth decline and by the early-signal model, contradicted by none: 2/2 = 1.0

components.computation: Beta posterior mean of this agent's historical correctness on this finding type in this entity class: (successes + 2) / (attempts + 4). A new agent starts at 0.5, not 1.0, so unproven agents cannot bootstrap themselves into high confidence.
For findings using a model: (1 - normalized_MAPE) x coverage_accuracy x (1 - min(1, PSI/0.5)). For findings not using a model: 0.7 (neutral).

Sum of: 0.15 (any lineage dataset degraded), 0.10 (a known confounding event overlaps the window), 0.10 (the entity had another change within 48h), 0.20 (effect inside the metric's historical noise band), 0.10 (attribution certainty < 0.6), 0.15 (cohort maturity below the metric's minimum), 0.10 (single-cell effect with no cross-cell replication).

worked_example.calibrated: 0.71 after the isotonic transform for Hunter/cohort-quality findings
worked_example.consequence: 0.71 exceeds the 0.70 threshold for autonomous budget_decrease but is below the 0.80 threshold for budget_increase - so a throttle may execute autonomously while a scale on the same evidence could not. The asymmetry is intentional.

business_impact_model.formula: impact_usd_30d = daily_effect_usd x persistence_days x probability_of_persistence, where daily_effect_usd is computed per finding type from the metric delta and the affected volume

computation_by_type.formula: delta_CPI x installs_per_day x 30, or equivalently the extra spend required for the same volume
(pLTV_baseline - pLTV_current) x installs_per_day x 30 (the value destroyed on future acquisition) + the already-acquired cohort's realized loss
delta_ARPDAU x DAU x 30, or delta_revenue_per_day x 30

translated through the pLTV model: delta_retention -> delta_pLTV -> x installs_per_day x 30. Retention is never reported as an impact in percentage points alone, because a 2pp D7 decline means completely different money on different titles.
marginal_ROAS_above_target x available_headroom_spend x 30, discounted by the probability of realizing it

business_impact_model.persistence_estimation: From the historical duration distribution of this finding type: creative fatigue persists and worsens (persistence 1.0, and the estimate is conservative because it worsens); market CPM spikes decay (median 7 days, persistence 0.23 over a 30-day horizon); product regressions persist until fixed (estimated from the historical fix-time distribution for that severity).
business_impact_model.uncertainty: Impact is always reported as a point estimate plus an 80% interval derived from the underlying metric's uncertainty and the persistence distribution. The interval is what the orchestrator uses when comparing options, not the point estimate.
business_impact_model.double_counting_control: The orchestrator deduplicates impact across merged findings: if three findings describe one causal chain, the incident's impact is the impact of the root, not the sum of all three. Without this, incident impact inflates by 2-4x and prioritization becomes meaningless.

components.computation: log-scaled normalization: min(1, log10(1 + impact_usd_30d) / log10(1 + 0.02 * S_daily * 30)). The reference point is 2% of monthly portfolio spend - an issue of that size scores 1.0. Log scaling prevents one huge issue from making everything else invisible.
the calibrated confidence directly

1 / (1 + hours_until_impact_is_irreversible / 24). A creative fatiguing over weeks scores low; an onboarding regression damaging every install right now scores near 1. Urgency is about the cost of waiting, not about how alarming it looks.
1 - recoverable_fraction. Spend on a bad cohort is unrecoverable (R near 1). Missed scaling upside is partly recoverable later (R near 0.4).
From the global context store: 1.0 if the affected entity is in a current strategic priority (a growth-push title, a market entry), 0.5 default, 0.2 for deprioritized areas.

priority_score.usage: Sorts the Command Center 'what needs you now' list, the approvals queue, the orchestrator's authorization order under the exposure cap, and Herald's routing urgency. Recomputed every 5 minutes.

worked_example.finding: T1 ad ARPDAU decline, impact $186k/30d, confidence 0.81, becomes irreversible over ~6 hours per day of delay, unrecoverable, strategic title

expected_value_model.formula: EV = P_success x Upside - (1 - P_success) x Downside - ExecutionCost - OptionValueLost

components.computation: The calibrated confidence times the playbook's historical hit rate for this action type in this situation class. Two independent factors: being right about the cause, and the action working given the cause.
The modeled 30-day margin gain if the action works as predicted, from the same models that produced the impact estimate.

The modeled 30-day margin loss if the causal hypothesis is wrong and the action is taken anyway. For a budget cut on a healthy campaign: lost volume x margin per install. For a scale on a bad cohort: added spend x (1 - realized ROAS). Downside is computed against the specific failure mode, not as a generic risk factor.
Learning-phase reset cost, delivery disruption, measurement contamination, human approval time. Small but non-zero, and it is what makes 'do nothing' the right answer for marginal findings.

The value of information forgone by acting now instead of waiting for more evidence. High when the cohort is immature and one more day would materially sharpen the estimate; near zero when waiting only accumulates loss. This term is what stops the system from acting prematurely on thin data.

expected_value_model.do_nothing_baseline: Every decision scores the do-nothing option explicitly, with its own EV (usually negative for a real problem, positive for a marginal one). An action is taken only if its EV exceeds do-nothing by a margin exceeding the EV estimate's own uncertainty.

worked_example.P_success: 0.71 (confidence) x 0.83 (playbook 'quality-decline throttle' hit rate over 34 applications) = 0.59
worked_example.Upside: $18,400 (avoided loss over 30 days at the current spend rate and predicted ROAS gap)
worked_example.Downside: $6,200 (lost volume and margin if the cohort quality decline is spurious and the campaign was actually fine)
worked_example.OptionValueLost: $900 (waiting 48h more would raise confidence to about 0.85, but costs $1,200/day of continued exposure - so waiting is net negative)
worked_example.decision: Act. EV advantage $20,078, far exceeding the estimate's uncertainty.

components.computation: action's 30-day exposure / (1% of S_daily x 30)

0 for instantly reversible with no side effects (a config revert, a floor change); 0.3 for reversible with a delay (a budget change - the money spent meanwhile is gone); 0.7 for reversible with a cost (a campaign pause resetting learning phase); 1.0 for effectively irreversible (a store change, an economy change, a shipped variant)
affected daily spend or affected DAU, normalized against the portfolio
the width of the EV's 80% interval relative to its point estimate
1 - (number of similar prior executions / 30), capped at 1. A novel action type is riskier than one performed 50 times, regardless of how confident the model is.

risk_score.usage: Risk determines the mode gate (high-risk actions require human approval regardless of EV), the approval role required, and the tightness of the rollback triggers.

recommendation_strength.formula: strength = (EV / max(1, Downside)) x confidence x (1 - risk) x maturity_factor

bands.meaning: Act now; delay is expensive and the evidence is strong.
bands.presentation: Top of queue, red, push notification if above the impact threshold.

bands.meaning: Clear recommendation; execute autonomously if the grant allows, otherwise approve within SLA.
Reasonable action, but waiting for more evidence is defensible. Never autonomous.
Informational. Presented as a watch item, not a recommendation.
Not surfaced as a recommendation at all; logged for the learning loop only. Surfacing weak recommendations is how a system trains its users to ignore it.

recommendation_strength.maturity_factor: Scales with cohort/data maturity: 0.6 below D1, 0.75 at D1-D3, 0.9 at D3-D7, 1.0 beyond D7. This is why the same evidence produces a stronger recommendation a few days later, and why the system says so explicitly rather than silently changing its mind.

mode_gating_matrix.description: The deterministic mapping from (confidence, risk, exposure, action_type) to execution mode. Evaluated by the agent, re-evaluated by the orchestrator, and independently enforced by Warden at the gateway.

rules.note: absolute rule, no confidence can override

rules.condition: action_type not on the autonomy matrix for this agent+scope
any hard gate failed (data, sample, maturity, freeze, cooldown, rate, human right-of-way)
all gates pass AND confidence >= threshold AND exposure within band AND action on the matrix

mode_gating_matrix.action_sizing_rule: Autonomous action magnitude scales with confidence: magnitude = base_magnitude x ((confidence - threshold) / (1 - threshold)) ^ 0.5, floored at 40% of base. A barely-confident action is a small action; a highly confident one approaches the full bound but never exceeds it.

calibration_and_audit.weekly_calibration: Scholar fits isotonic regression per (agent, finding type) on the last 180 days of outcomes and publishes reliability curves. Uncalibrated (insufficient sample) combinations are capped at Mode 2.
calibration_and_audit.score_audit: Every score's components are persisted with the finding. When a decision is questioned - by a human, an auditor, or a post-mortem - the exact arithmetic is reproducible from the stored components and the stored evidence bundle.
calibration_and_audit.drift_detection: If the realized distribution of outcomes diverges from what the scores predicted (Brier score degradation), the affected agent is demoted automatically and the scoring weights are reviewed.

framework.core_rule: Autonomy is granted per tuple (agent, action_type, entity_scope, dollar_band, confidence_band), never globally. Default is deny. Every autonomous action carries, without exception: a confidence threshold, a financial limit, a rollback condition, a cooldown, an immutable audit record, and a human-readable explanation of why it was taken.
action_lifecycle: 1. PROPOSE: the agent constructs a fully specified action object (target, exact deltas, prior state, EV, downside, rollback plan, evidence ref).
2. SELF-GATE: the agent evaluates the mode gating matrix; if not autonomous, it becomes a Mode 2 proposal.
3. ORCHESTRATE: Atlas evaluates portfolio effects and either authorizes, resizes, defers, or denies, issuing a signed execution token with a short TTL (5 minutes).
4. POLICY: Warden independently re-evaluates every guardrail against the live state. Default deny; a stale token is rejected.

5. DRY RUN: the gateway computes the exact external API calls and their diff, validates them against the entity's current state read fresh from the network, and aborts if the current state does not match the prior_state the decision was based on (optimistic concurrency - someone else changed it).
6. AUDIT PRE-WRITE: the full action record, prior state and rollback plan are written to the append-only, hash-chained audit log BEFORE execution. An action that cannot be audited cannot execute.
7. EXECUTE: idempotent call with the idempotency key; retries on transient failure with backoff, capped at 3.
8. VERIFY: read back the entity state after 60 seconds; on mismatch, retry once, then roll back, then alert.
9. REGISTER: schedule rollback-trigger evaluation and measurement jobs at +1h/+24h/+72h/+7d.
10. EXPLAIN: publish the explanation artifact to the dashboard action feed and, above the notification threshold, to Slack.
framework.sizing_rule: magnitude = base_magnitude x ((confidence - threshold)/(1 - threshold))^0.5, floored at 40% of base and capped at the grant's bound. Confidence buys size, never permission.
framework.shared_change_budget: All agents share a single per-entity daily change budget (default: 35% cumulative parameter change per campaign per day, 50% per 7 days). This prevents the failure where three agents each make an individually-compliant 20% change to the same campaign.
framework.human_right_of_way: Any entity touched by a human in the last 4 hours is off-limits to autonomous action. Humans are never overwritten by an agent without an explicit approval.
framework.kill_switch_precedence: Kill switches take effect within 5 seconds fleet-wide and cancel in-flight actions that have not yet reached step 7.

action_catalogue.description: Reduce a campaign's or adset's daily budget.
action_catalogue.financial_limit: <= 35% of current daily budget per action; entity daily spend <= 0.50% of S_daily; <= 0.20% of S_daily in daily-budget delta per action
preconditions: cohort economics support the direction (P(target ROAS) < 0.5) or a confirmed quality/fraud finding exists
cohort n >= 300
no market-wide explanation active for this entity
not in learning phase with > 20% change
shared change budget has room
action_catalogue.rollback_condition: If at +72h the campaign's cohort P(target ROAS) has risen above 0.65 AND CPI has not deteriorated, restore 50% of the reduction. Immediate rollback if the finding that justified it is retracted (e.g. the data proved partial).
action_catalogue.cooldown: 12 hours per entity; max 2 decreases per campaign per day; max 50% cumulative per 7 days
action_catalogue.explanation_template: Reduced {entity} daily budget from ${prior} to ${new} (-{pct}%) because {cause_summary}. Evidence: {top_3_evidence_points}. Expected effect: {predicted_effect} over 30 days. If wrong, the cost is approximately ${downside}. Confidence {confidence}. This will be re-evaluated at {checkpoint}.
action_catalogue.measurement: +24h spend and delivery; +72h cohort quality; +7d ROAS vs matched control campaigns

action_catalogue.description: Increase a campaign's or adset's daily budget to capture profitable headroom.
action_catalogue.financial_limit: <= 20% of current daily budget per action; resulting daily spend <= 0.40% of S_daily; <= 0.20% of S_daily delta per action
preconditions: ALL six scaling conditions (marginal ROAS above target with the CI lower bound also above target; cohort ROAS inside corridor at every checkpoint; budget utilization > 92%; top-3 creatives CFI < 0.35; no open quality finding; no scale within 72h)
P(target ROAS) >= 0.65
portfolio headroom exists and the envelope permits
pLTV model not degraded for this scope
action_catalogue.rollback_condition: Automatic revert to the prior budget if at +72h ANY of: CPI > pre-change baseline x 1.25, D1 retention < baseline - 3pp, cohort P(target ROAS) < 0.45, or spend materialized > 115% of the new budget (runaway delivery).
action_catalogue.cooldown: 48 hours per entity; max 1 increase per campaign per day; cumulative <= 50% per 7 days
action_catalogue.audit_fields: as above plus the spend-response curve snapshot and the saturation-knee estimate used
action_catalogue.explanation_template: Increased {entity} daily budget from ${prior} to ${new} (+{pct}%) because marginal D180 ROAS is {marginal_roas} vs target {target} with the 80% interval lower bound at {lower_bound}, and delivery is budget-limited at {utilization}% utilization. Cohort quality is inside corridor at D1/D3/D7. Expected: +{installs} installs/day at ${cpi} CPI, +${margin} margin over 30 days. Auto-reverts at +72h if CPI exceeds ${cpi_trigger} or D1 retention falls below {ret_trigger}%.
action_catalogue.measurement: +24h delivery and CPI; +72h retention and early ROAS; +7d cohort economics; synthetic control from matched non-scaled campaigns
action_catalogue.note: Deliberately asymmetric with decrease: higher confidence bar, smaller step, longer cooldown. Scaling a bad cohort costs far more than failing to scale a good one, and the system's incentives are set accordingly.

action_catalogue.description: Pause an adset or individual ad (never a campaign autonomously).
preconditions: not the last active adset in its campaign
P(target ROAS) < 0.25 with n >= 500, or a confirmed fraud/policy finding
cohort maturity >= D3 for economics-based pauses
action_catalogue.rollback_condition: Resume if the underlying finding is retracted within 24h, or if the campaign's total delivery falls > 40% below its pre-pause level (the paused entity was load-bearing).
action_catalogue.cooldown: 24 hours; max 3 pauses per campaign per week
action_catalogue.audit_fields: standard plus the delivery share of the paused entity and the campaign's projected delivery after pause
action_catalogue.explanation_template: Paused {entity} because {cause}. It carried {share}% of campaign delivery at a projected D180 ROAS of {roas} (target {target}). Remaining active entities: {count}. Estimated saved spend ${saved}/day.
action_catalogue.measurement: +24h campaign delivery integrity; +7d campaign-level economics vs control

action_catalogue.description: Apply a placement, device-tier, OS-version or geo exclusion to an adset - the surgical alternative to a budget cut.
action_catalogue.financial_limit: affected spend share <= 25% of the campaign; <= 0.20% of S_daily
preconditions: dimension localization explanatory power >= 0.70
the excluded segment's P(target ROAS) < 0.30 while the campaign's remainder is >= 0.55
the network supports the exclusion type without resetting the campaign
action_catalogue.rollback_condition: Remove the exclusion if at +72h campaign volume fell > 40% (the segment was carrying more value than modeled) or the campaign's blended economics did not improve.
action_catalogue.cooldown: 72 hours per entity per exclusion type
action_catalogue.audit_fields: standard plus the localization analysis and the excluded segment's full metric profile
action_catalogue.explanation_template: Excluded {dimension}={value} from {entity}. This segment is {spend_share}% of spend and {install_share}% of installs but has D7 retention {ret} vs {ret_rest} for the rest of the campaign, and projected D180 ROAS {roas_seg} vs {roas_rest}. Expected effect: CPI rises to approximately ${new_cpi} (this is expected and correct - we stop buying the cheap bad users), volume falls about {vol}%, margin improves ${margin}/30d.
action_catalogue.measurement: +24h delivery; +72h blended cohort quality; +7d margin vs control

action_catalogue.description: Adjust bid, target CPA or target ROAS.
action_catalogue.financial_limit: <= 12% change per action; resulting implied CPI must remain <= 0.90 x allowable CPI
preconditions: allowable CPI is current (Oracle not degraded)
adset not in learning phase
no target change in the last 24h from any actor
action_catalogue.rollback_condition: Revert if at +72h the achieved cost exceeds the new target by > 20%, or delivery collapsed > 50%, or the learning phase reset unexpectedly.
action_catalogue.cooldown: 24 hours per entity; networks need 3-5 days to stabilize after a target change, so a second change inside 72h requires human approval regardless
action_catalogue.audit_fields: standard plus allowable CPI at decision time and the implied CPI after the change
action_catalogue.explanation_template: Changed {entity} target from ${prior} to ${new} ({direction} {pct}%). Allowable CPI for this slice is ${allowable} based on pLTV ${pltv} and a {payback}-day payback target. Delivery was {constraint}-limited. Expected: {effect}.
action_catalogue.measurement: +72h achieved cost vs target, delivery volume, learning phase state

action_catalogue.description: Execute one step of a human-approved staged budget reallocation package.
action_catalogue.financial_limit: <= 15% of the affected campaign's budget per step; package total <= 5% of S_daily; net portfolio spend change <= 2%/day
preconditions: the package was approved by a human
the previous step's measured effect fell inside its prediction interval
all receiving campaigns still pass their scaling preconditions at execution time (a package approved yesterday does not authorize a step into a campaign that developed a quality problem overnight)
action_catalogue.rollback_condition: Halt the remaining package and restore the last step if the measured install or revenue effect falls outside the 80% prediction interval, or if any receiving campaign develops an open quality finding.
action_catalogue.audit_fields: package id, step number, per-campaign deltas, curve snapshots, checkpoint measurement results
action_catalogue.explanation_template: Reallocation package {id}, step {n} of {total}: moved ${amount}/day from {donors} to {recipients}. Marginal ROAS before: donors {d_roas}, recipients {r_roas}. Expected margin gain ${gain} over 30 days. Next checkpoint {time}.
action_catalogue.measurement: +24h per-campaign delivery; +72h cohort quality on recipients; +7d portfolio margin

action_catalogue.description: Pause a fatigued or misleading creative and shift its budget to qualified replacements.
preconditions: CFI >= 0.55 (fatigue) or the misleading-creative criteria (top IPM quartile, bottom retention quartile, n >= 500)
a qualified replacement exists (fatigue only)
the creative carries <= 40% of the adset's delivery
adset retains >= 2 active creatives
no market-wide CPM event active
cumulative impressions >= 150k and days live >= 7
action_catalogue.rollback_condition: Reactivate if adset delivery falls > 35% within 24h or the replacement's IPM underperforms the paused creative's trailing 7-day IPM by > 25%.
action_catalogue.cooldown: 72 hours per adset; max 3 rotations per campaign per week
action_catalogue.audit_fields: standard plus the CFI decomposition, peer comparison, and replacement candidates with their test metrics
action_catalogue.explanation_template: Paused creative {id} ({name}) on {entities}. Fatigue index {cfi}: IPM fell {ipm_from} -> {ipm_to} over {days} days at {impressions} cumulative impressions, while peer creatives in the same cells fell only {peer_decline}% - so this is creative-specific, not market-wide. Budget shifted to {replacements}. Cost of inaction was estimated at ${cost} over 14 days.
action_catalogue.measurement: +24h delivery integrity; +72h IPM and CPI recovery vs matched non-rotated adsets; +7d cohort quality of the replacements

action_catalogue.description: Promote a test-winning creative to its first scaling stage (up to 15% budget share).
preconditions: P(IPM > incumbent) > 0.90 with >= 30k impressions
early cohort quality not below peer P25
no open quality finding on the campaign
action_catalogue.rollback_condition: Revert the share if at +72h the promoted creative's IPM falls below the incumbent's or its cohort quality index falls below peer P25.
action_catalogue.cooldown: 72 hours; stages beyond 15% require human approval
action_catalogue.audit_fields: test results, cohort quality at promotion time, share before/after
action_catalogue.explanation_template: Promoted creative {id} to {share}% budget share. Test result: IPM {new} vs incumbent {old}, P(better) {prob} on {impressions} impressions. Early cohort quality {quality} (peer median {peer}). Next stage requires human approval.

action_catalogue.description: Adjust a mediation instance's floor price.
action_catalogue.financial_limit: <= 15% change per action; projected revenue impact <= 0.25% of daily ad revenue per action; cumulative <= 3% of a title's ad revenue per 7 days
preconditions: a measured price-response curve exists for this instance
no mediation SDK update in the last 48h
reporting is fresh and ULAR-vs-reconciled variance < 8%
no active partner dispute on this instance
staged by geo tier (T3 first)
action_catalogue.rollback_condition: Revert if at +24h fill rate falls > 5pp or total placement revenue falls > 3% vs the matched-geo control.
action_catalogue.audit_fields: prior floor, new floor, price-response curve snapshot, win rate before, projected and realized revenue effect
action_catalogue.explanation_template: Raised the floor for instance {id} ({network}, {geo}, {format}) from ${prior} to ${new}. Win rate was {wr}% with realized eCPM {ecpm} exceeding the floor by {gap}%, indicating the floor was leaving revenue unclaimed. Expected +${revenue}/day. Auto-reverts if fill falls more than 5pp.
action_catalogue.measurement: +24h fill, eCPM, revenue vs matched control geos

action_catalogue.description: Disable a dead instance or enable a pre-approved backfill instance.
action_catalogue.financial_limit: <= 0.25% of daily ad revenue at risk
preconditions: disable: win rate < 2% for 7 days; enable: the instance is on the pre-approved catalogue
at least 5 active instances remain per placement
mediation reporting fresh
action_catalogue.rollback_condition: Re-enable/disable if placement fill falls > 3pp or revenue falls > 2% within 24h.
action_catalogue.audit_fields: standard plus placement instance inventory before and after
action_catalogue.explanation_template: Disabled instance {id} ({network}) in {placement}: win rate {wr}% over 7 days at floor ${floor}, contributing {rev_share}% of placement revenue. {remaining} instances remain active. Expected effect: neutral to +${effect}/day from reduced auction latency.

action_catalogue.description: Revert a remote-config parameter to its immediately prior value.
action_catalogue.financial_limit: modeled revenue exposure <= 0.5% of daily revenue; affected users <= 25% of DAU
preconditions: the parameter is on the allowlist with blast-radius class low or medium
the metric changepoint aligns within 30 minutes of the config change and the affected population matches its targeting
the target value is a previous known-good value, never a new value
no other config change in the last 15 minutes
no running experiment on that parameter
action_catalogue.rollback_condition: Re-apply the original value if the reverted metric does not recover within 6 hours (the config change was not the cause, and the revert is itself a change that should not persist without justification).
action_catalogue.cooldown: 6 hours per parameter; max 2 autonomous reverts per title per day
action_catalogue.audit_fields: parameter, prior value, reverted-to value, template versions, changepoint alignment evidence, affected user estimate, owner notified
action_catalogue.explanation_template: Reverted {parameter} from {current} to {prior} (template version {v_from} -> {v_to}). {metric} dropped {delta} beginning {changepoint}, aligning within {minutes} minutes of the config publish at {publish_time} by {actor}, and the affected population matches the change's targeting ({match}%). Estimated impact of the regression: ${impact}/day. {owner} has been notified. Will re-apply if the metric does not recover within 6 hours.
action_catalogue.measurement: +1h propagation check; +6h metric recovery; +24h confirmation; +72h no side effects

action_catalogue.description: Stop an experiment variant breaching a pre-registered guardrail.
action_catalogue.financial_limit: unbounded in the protective direction (stopping harm has no upper limit)
preconditions: the guardrail was pre-registered with a threshold before the experiment started
p < 0.05 and the effect exceeds practical significance
the variant, not the whole experiment, is stopped so control is preserved
action_catalogue.rollback_condition: None - a protective stop is not rolled back automatically. Restarting requires human approval and a documented rationale.
action_catalogue.audit_fields: experiment, variant, guardrail metric, threshold, observed effect and CI, exposure count, users affected
action_catalogue.explanation_template: Stopped variant {variant} of experiment {id}. Guardrail {metric} is {observed} vs the pre-registered threshold {threshold} (p={p}, {n} users exposed). Estimated harm avoided: {harm}. Control and other variants continue.
action_catalogue.measurement: +24h confirmation that the guardrail metric recovers for the affected population

action_catalogue.description: Blocklist a fraudulent sub-publisher / site id.
action_catalogue.financial_limit: affected spend <= 0.5% of S_daily per action; max 10 blocklists per day
preconditions: >= 2 independent fraud signals (CTIT anomaly, device-ratio anomaly, retention collapse, conversion-rate outlier)
volume >= 200 installs/day (below this, it is noise)
the network supports blocklisting via API
action_catalogue.rollback_condition: Automatic 30-day review; unblock if the publisher's traffic profile normalizes in a re-test. Immediate unblock if the fraud finding is retracted.
action_catalogue.cooldown: none for distinct publishers; 30 days before re-blocking the same publisher after an unblock
action_catalogue.audit_fields: publisher id, fraud signals with values, affected spend and installs, estimated fraudulent spend, claw-back packet reference
action_catalogue.explanation_template: Blocklisted sub-publisher {id} on {network}. Evidence: CTIT distribution {ctit}% below 8s (baseline {baseline}%), new-device ratio {ndr}, D1 retention {ret}% vs {campaign_ret}% for the campaign's other publishers. Estimated fraudulent spend ${amount} over {days} days. A claw-back packet has been prepared for filing. Campaign budget has been reduced by ${budget} to prevent the network reallocating the same spend to other publishers.
action_catalogue.measurement: +7d campaign cohort quality; +14d displacement check (did fraud reappear elsewhere in the same campaign)

action_catalogue.description: Restore a previously approved offer that lapsed without a successor.
preconditions: the identical configuration ran within the last 45 days and was approved
no price change of any kind
no running experiment on that offer or paywall
the monetization PM is notified at execution
action_catalogue.rollback_condition: Disable if take rate is below 50% of its historical median at +48h (market conditions changed) or if any economy guardrail is breached.
action_catalogue.audit_fields: offer id, configuration hash matched against the prior approved version, lapse duration, revenue impact estimate
action_catalogue.explanation_template: Restored offer {id} (identical to the configuration approved on {date}). It lapsed at {lapse_time} with no successor and had been contributing {share}% of D0-D3 IAP revenue. First-purchase rate fell {from}% -> {to}% since the lapse. Estimated recovery ${amount} over 30 days. {pm} notified.
action_catalogue.measurement: +48h take rate and first-purchase rate; +7d IAP revenue vs pre-lapse baseline

action_catalogue.description: Mark a dataset degraded/quarantined and block dependent agent actions.
action_catalogue.financial_limit: n/a (protective; it prevents actions rather than taking them)
action_catalogue.preconditions: freshness, volume, schema or contract check failure
action_catalogue.rollback_condition: Automatic lift when the data passes all checks and completeness exceeds 97%.
action_catalogue.audit_fields: dataset, check failed, values, affected lineage, blocked actions list, duration
action_catalogue.explanation_template: {dataset} marked {state}: {check} failed ({observed} vs expected {expected}). Completeness estimated at {completeness}% (arrival curve suggests full arrival by {eta}). {n} agent actions held; {agents} gated. Dashboards showing this data are flagged.
action_catalogue.measurement: Recovery time; retrospective check of whether held actions would have been correct

action_catalogue.description: Publish MODEL_DEGRADED and suspend dependent autonomy for a scope.
action_catalogue.preconditions: MAPE, bias, PSI or coverage threshold breach sustained per its rule
action_catalogue.rollback_condition: Lifted after 5 days of clean calibration metrics or after a successful model promotion.
action_catalogue.audit_fields: model, version, metric breached, scope, affected agents and action types, retrospective review of decisions made on degraded outputs
action_catalogue.explanation_template: pLTV model {version} degraded for scope {scope}: {metric} is {value} (threshold {threshold}) for {days} days. Autonomous actions depending on pLTV in this scope are suspended pending retrain. {n} decisions from the last 30 days made on these outputs are under review.
action_catalogue.measurement: Post-retrain accuracy; outcome of the retrospective decision review

action_catalogue.description: Downgrade entity-specific findings explained by a market-wide movement.
preconditions: breadth test passes (>= 60% of unrelated entities in the same cells moved together)
the finding is not Sev-1 and not an invariant violation
no internal causal evidence (config alignment, intervention test) contradicts the market explanation
action_catalogue.rollback_condition: Suppression auto-expires after 7 days or when the market index normalizes; findings are restored, not deleted, and are re-evaluated.
action_catalogue.audit_fields: suppressed finding ids, index values, breadth statistics, expected duration, checkpoint date
action_catalogue.explanation_template: {n} findings on {metric} downgraded to informational: the market index for {cells} moved {pct}% and {breadth}% of unrelated campaigns in the same cells moved with it. This is auction pressure, not an entity-specific problem. Re-evaluation scheduled for {checkpoint}. {exceptions} campaigns remain actionable because their economics fall below target even at the elevated CPM.
action_catalogue.measurement: At the checkpoint: did the metric recover with the market (suppression correct) or persist (a real cause was missed)

action_catalogue.description: Demote an agent's execution mode on a safety trigger.
action_catalogue.preconditions: rollback storm, calibration failure, dependency degradation, anomalous behavior, or a caused incident
action_catalogue.rollback_condition: None automatic. Restoration requires the promotion gate to be re-passed plus human approval.
action_catalogue.audit_fields: agent, trigger, evidence, prior mode, new mode, affected action types, incident reference
action_catalogue.explanation_template: {agent} demoted from {prior_mode} to {new_mode}: {trigger} ({evidence}). Its findings continue to be published; its execution authority is suspended. Re-promotion requires {gate_criteria} plus approval from {roles}.
action_catalogue.measurement: Agent performance during the demotion period; whether the trigger condition resolves

actions_never_autonomous: Any action above 1.0% of S_daily in 30-day exposure, at any confidence.
Creating new campaigns, adsets, ads, or ad accounts.
Any IAP price change or new offer.
Any game economy parameter (currency rates, sink costs, reward values).
Any store listing, metadata, or app store submission.
Any app release, rollback, or staged-rollout change (recommendations only; engineering executes).
Attribution window, dedup rule, SKAN schema, or incrementality multiplier changes.
Adding or removing a network from mediation, or any partner contractual action.
Any action on a title in soft launch or within 14 days of a major release.
Any action during a declared change freeze.
Any action on an entity flagged strategic, partner-managed, or under contractual commitment.
Any autonomy grant, guardrail change, or kill-switch lift.

rollback_system.rollback_daemon: A service independent of the agents. It reads the action journal, evaluates every registered rollback trigger on schedule (+1h/+6h/+24h/+72h depending on the action type), and executes reversals without needing the originating agent to be alive or correct. An agent cannot suppress its own rollback.
trigger_types: metric threshold breach vs the pre-registered condition
finding retraction (the evidence that justified the action was invalidated)
data quality invalidation (the action was based on data later found partial)
human undo (one click, available for 72h on every autonomous action)
cascade protection (the action's entity or its parent shows an unexpected collapse in any core metric)
rollback_guarantees: prior_state is captured and verified before every action, so reversal always has a target
reversal uses the same idempotent gateway path with its own audit record
if reversal fails (the external API rejects it), the incident escalates to Sev-1 immediately and the agent's action type is disabled pending investigation
rollbacks are counted per agent and per fleet; storms trigger automatic demotion or a global pause
rollback_system.what_rollback_cannot_recover: Money already spent, users already acquired, and impressions already served. This is precisely why the guardrails on scaling and ad-load actions are tighter than on reversible configuration actions - the limits are set by what a mistake costs after reversal, not by how confident the model is.

fields: agent_id and version (code + prompt + model tier)
impact estimate with interval and method
policy_evaluation (every guardrail checked, its inputs, and its verdict)
approver (human id, role, timestamp) if Mode 2
external API request and response (redacted of credentials)
measurement schedule and results as they arrive
hash of the previous audit record (chain)
audit_record_schema.storage: Append-only Postgres table plus mirrored WORM object storage; 7-year retention; hash-chained with a daily anchor published to an internal notary so tampering is detectable.
audit_record_schema.access: Read access for all users with the auditor role; write access exclusively for the Action Gateway service account; no delete path exists in the schema or the application.

root_cause_analysis.principle: An alert without a cause is a request for someone else to do the work. Every finding in MART must answer ten questions before it is allowed to reach a human, and must say honestly when it cannot answer them.

ten_question_framework.question: 1. What changed?
ten_question_framework.method: Precise metric identification with the exact magnitude, expressed both relatively and in absolute business units. The metric is decomposed into its multiplicative or additive components so the change is attributed to a factor, not just observed (CPI = CPM x 1/CTR x 1/CVR; ad ARPDAU = imp/DAU x eCPM/1000; revenue = DAU x ARPDAU; ROAS = LTV/CPI).
techniques: multiplicative log decomposition with Shapley normalization for fair attribution among interacting factors
additive contribution for sums
identity invariant checks to catch structurally impossible changes (which indicate data problems, not business problems)
ten_question_framework.output: 'ad ARPDAU fell 8.7% ($186k/30d). Decomposition: impressions/DAU contributed -11.4% (dominant), eCPM +1.2%, fill 0.0%, show rate 0.0%, DAU mix +1.5%.'
ten_question_framework.failure_mode_avoided: Reporting a composite metric's movement without decomposition, which sends the wrong team to investigate.

ten_question_framework.question: 2. When did it change?
ten_question_framework.method: Bayesian online changepoint detection producing a changepoint posterior with a credible interval, not a single timestamp. The interval matters more than the point estimate because alignment against candidate causes is what identifies the cause.
techniques: BOCPD with a hazard rate tuned per metric family
CUSUM for gradual onset where there is no sharp changepoint
segmented regression to distinguish a level shift from a slope change - they have different causes
ten_question_framework.output: 'Changepoint 2026-08-26 13:00-14:00 UTC (posterior mode 13:20, 90% credible interval 12:40-14:10). Level shift, not a trend change.'
ten_question_framework.failure_mode_avoided: Assuming the change started when it was detected, which misaligns it against the deploy timeline and produces the wrong cause.

ten_question_framework.question: 3. Which cohorts or dimensions are affected?
ten_question_framework.method: Multi-dimensional contribution attribution that returns the MINIMAL dimension set explaining the majority of the change, with each value's contribution and surprise score.
techniques: Adtributor-style attribution combining explanatory power (share of the total change) and surprise (JS divergence from the expected distribution)
hierarchical drill: test each dimension independently, then the top combinations, avoiding a full combinatorial explosion
false discovery rate control across the dimension space, because testing thousands of slices guarantees spurious findings without it
mix vs within-slice decomposition, always
ten_question_framework.output: '82% of the change is carried by geo=US (contribution 0.61, surprise 0.44) and geo=CA (0.21) within format=rewarded. All other geos and formats are within band. This is not a mix effect: recomputing with the baseline composition preserves 91% of the change.'
ten_question_framework.failure_mode_avoided: Reporting an aggregate movement that is entirely a composition shift, which leads to fixing something that is not broken.

ten_question_framework.question: 4. What downstream metrics are affected?
ten_question_framework.method: Propagate the change through the causal DAG to its children, and quantify the downstream effect through the models that connect them.
techniques: DAG traversal from the affected node
pLTV model propagation (retention change -> LTV change -> allowable CPI change -> bid target implication)
lagged correlation checks to confirm the downstream effect is materializing on schedule
ten_question_framework.output: 'Downstream: cohort ad-LTV -$0.14/install for affected cohorts; allowable CPI for the slice falls from $2.40 to $2.11; 4 campaigns currently bid above the new allowable CPI.'
ten_question_framework.failure_mode_avoided: Treating an upstream metric change as a self-contained problem, which misses the fact that bid targets are now wrong.

ten_question_framework.question: 5. What upstream variables changed?
ten_question_framework.method: Examine every admissible parent in the causal DAG over the changepoint window, plus the complete change timeline (our changes and external changes).
techniques: change timeline join: app releases, staged rollout percentages, config publishes, campaign/bid/creative/targeting edits, experiment starts, network policy events, store listing changes, LiveOps events, holidays - anything that could have moved the parent
lagged cross-correlation with the appropriate lag per relationship (a budget change affects CPM within hours, cohort quality within days)
Granger causality as a screening test, never as proof
peer-relative test to separate internal from external causes
intervention evidence where available (was the candidate cause reverted, and did the effect reverse?)
ten_question_framework.output: 'Upstream candidates in window: (a) remote-config publish 2026-08-26 13:12 UTC changing interstitial_cooldown 45->75s, targeting matches the affected population at 94%; (b) app version 4.2.1 adoption crossing 60% - but its adoption curve is smooth through the changepoint, so it does not align; (c) no network policy events; (d) market index flat.'
ten_question_framework.failure_mode_avoided: Investigating a metric in ignorance of a change that trivially explains it - the single most common waste of analyst time.

ten_question_framework.question: 6. What is the likely root cause?
ten_question_framework.method: Bayesian hypothesis ranking with explicit refutation of the leading candidate, and a residual 'unknown' hypothesis that never leaves the list.
techniques: posterior = prior(cause class for this metric in this business) x likelihood(observed evidence | cause)
each hypothesis generates testable implications which are checked, not assumed
explicit refutation attempt on the leader: what evidence would falsify this, and is it present?
case-based retrieval of the k nearest historical incidents by evidence embedding, with their adjudicated causes
correlation-vs-causation guard: a hypothesis with only temporal coincidence and no DAG path is capped at 0.55 posterior and labeled correlational
ten_question_framework.output: 'Root cause (posterior 0.79): the remote-config change to interstitial_cooldown. Supporting: exact temporal alignment (8-minute offset), targeting-population match (94%), the mechanism is direct and modeled (cooldown -> impressions/DAU -> ad ARPDAU), the magnitude matches the frontier model prediction within 12%. Refutation attempt: if this were the cause, geos outside the targeting should be unaffected - confirmed, they are. Alternative (0.11): demand-side eCPM shift - refuted, eCPM is flat. Unknown residual: 0.10.'
ten_question_framework.failure_mode_avoided: Producing a confident narrative that fits the evidence without testing whether an alternative fits it equally well.

ten_question_framework.question: 7. What is the estimated business impact?
ten_question_framework.method: Convert the metric change into 30-day and 90-day P&L impact with an interval, accounting for persistence and for downstream propagation, and deduplicated against related findings.
techniques: daily effect x persistence distribution x affected volume
downstream propagation through pLTV where the effect is on an upstream metric
counterfactual baseline: what would have happened without the change (from the forecast or matched controls)
explicit separation of already-incurred loss from future loss, because they call for different urgency
ten_question_framework.output: 'Incurred to date: $47k over 4 days. Projected if unaddressed: $186k over the next 30 days (80% interval $131k-$247k). Of that, $41k is already locked in through cohorts acquired during the window whose LTV is permanently lower.'
ten_question_framework.failure_mode_avoided: Reporting impact in percentage points, which cannot be prioritized against other issues.

ten_question_framework.question: 8. What should be done?
ten_question_framework.method: Generate candidate actions including do-nothing, score each with the decision engine, apply the portfolio guard, and recommend the highest-EV option with its alternatives visible.
techniques: playbook retrieval by situation fingerprint, with the playbook's historical hit rate
cause-before-symptom ordering (fix the driver, do not compensate for it)
surgical-before-blunt preference (exclusion before budget cut, config revert before spend action)
reversibility preference when EVs are within 20%
explicit sequencing when multiple actions are needed, so effects remain measurable
ten_question_framework.output: 'Recommended: revert interstitial_cooldown to 45s (config revert, instant, fully reversible, EV +$171k/30d, confidence 0.79). Alternative considered and rejected: raise ad floors to compensate (+$12k/30d, does not address the cause, and would need reversing once the config is fixed). Do nothing: -$186k/30d.'
ten_question_framework.failure_mode_avoided: Recommending the action that is easiest for the recommending team rather than the one that addresses the cause.

ten_question_framework.question: 9. What confidence does the system have?
ten_question_framework.method: The calibrated composite confidence with all components exposed, plus the specific evidence gaps that limit it.
techniques: the shared confidence model
explicit listing of untested implications
