explicit statement of what would raise confidence and how long it would take
ten_question_framework.output: 'Confidence 0.79 (calibrated). Limiting factors: no intervention test yet (reverting and observing recovery would raise this to about 0.95 within 6 hours); one confounding change in the window (app version adoption) that we ruled out on alignment grounds but cannot fully exclude.'
ten_question_framework.failure_mode_avoided: Presenting a conclusion as certain, which destroys trust the first time it is wrong.

ten_question_framework.question: 10. How should the outcome be measured?
ten_question_framework.method: Pre-register the prediction, the counterfactual method, the measurement schedule, and the criteria that would declare the action a failure - all before acting.
techniques: prediction registry entry with expected direction, magnitude, horizon and interval
counterfactual: synthetic control from matched entities, a geo/version holdout, or the pre-change forecast
rollback trigger thresholds derived from the prediction interval, so failure is detected automatically
measurement at +1h/+24h/+72h/+7d/+30d as appropriate to the action's effect latency
ten_question_framework.output: 'Prediction: ad ARPDAU recovers to within 3% of its pre-change baseline within 6 hours of config propagation (80% interval 4-9 hours). Counterfactual: geos outside the config targeting serve as controls. Failure criterion: if recovery is under 50% at +6h, the config was not the cause and the revert will itself be reverted. Full measurement at +24h and +7d.'
ten_question_framework.failure_mode_avoided: Declaring victory because the metric recovered, when it would have recovered anyway.

cause_taxonomy.purpose: A closed, versioned vocabulary of cause classes. Hypotheses must map to a node; a cause that does not fit triggers a taxonomy-extension proposal rather than a free-text guess. This is what makes cause statistics (priors, frequencies, agent accuracy) computable at all.

classes.note: always tested first - it is the most common cause of dramatic-looking movements
not a root cause in itself but a distinct explanation class that demands a different response - and the class most often misdiagnosed as a performance change
a first-class, permanently available answer; used when no hypothesis exceeds 0.35 posterior

fields: effect (metric, entity, magnitude, units, absolute business impact)
hypotheses (ranked: class, subclass, posterior, supporting evidence, refuting evidence, testable implications tested and untested)
recommended_actions (ranked with EV, alternatives considered and why rejected, including do-nothing)
confidence (calibrated, with components and limiting factors)
measurement_plan (predictions, counterfactual method, schedule, failure criteria)
investigation_output_schema.validation: The event bus rejects any finding missing hypotheses, impact, recommended_actions or measurement_plan. A finding that cannot fill these fields is by definition not ready to consume a human's attention.

quality_standards: No finding is emitted without a hypothesis set, even if the top hypothesis is UNKNOWN.
Correlation is never reported as causation. A hypothesis without a DAG path or intervention evidence is explicitly labeled correlational and capped in confidence.
Every number in the narrative must exist in the evidence bundle; a numeric-grounding validator rejects LLM output that invents or miscopies figures.
The refutation attempt is mandatory and its result is reported, including when refutation failed to find contrary evidence (which is itself informative).
Mix effects are always separated from within-slice effects before any causal claim.
Data causes are ruled out before business causes, always, because acting on a data artifact is both wasteful and trust-destroying.
The counterfactual is stated explicitly: what would have happened without intervention.
'Unknown' is an acceptable and expected verdict in at least 10% of investigations. A system that always has an answer is producing narratives, not analysis.

worked_end_to_end_example.q1_what: T1 ad ARPDAU fell from $0.0412 to $0.0376 (-8.7%), equal to -$6,200/day at current DAU. Decomposition: impressions/DAU -11.4% (contribution 1.31 of the change), eCPM +1.2% (-0.14), fill 0.0%, show rate 0.0%, DAU mix +1.5% (-0.17).
worked_end_to_end_example.q2_when: Changepoint 2026-08-26 13:00-14:00 UTC, posterior mode 13:20, 90% CI 12:40-14:10. Level shift.
worked_end_to_end_example.q3_where: geo=US contributes 0.61, geo=CA 0.21, both concentrated in format=rewarded and interstitial. Mix-adjusted recomputation preserves 91% of the change, so this is a real within-slice effect. Affected population: 38% of T1 DAU.
worked_end_to_end_example.q4_downstream: Cohort ad-LTV for cohorts acquired since the change is tracking -$0.14/install; allowable CPI for T1 US falls $2.40 -> $2.11; 4 campaigns currently bid above the new allowable CPI and are now unprofitable at the margin.
worked_end_to_end_example.q5_upstream: Config publish at 13:12 UTC changed interstitial_cooldown_seconds from 45 to 75, targeted at US/CA (targeting-population match 94%). App version 4.2.1 adoption was smooth through the window (no alignment). No network policy events. Market demand index flat (+0.4%). No experiment on this parameter.
worked_end_to_end_example.q6_cause: PRODUCT/config change, posterior 0.79. Mechanism is direct and modeled. Refutation attempt: geos outside targeting should be unaffected - confirmed unaffected. Alternative MONETIZATION/demand shift at 0.11, refuted by flat eCPM and flat fill. UNKNOWN residual 0.10.
worked_end_to_end_example.q7_impact: Incurred $24.8k over 4 days. Projected $186k over 30 days (80% interval $131k-$247k) if unaddressed. $41k is already locked into acquired cohorts. Offsetting consideration: the longer cooldown may improve retention; the frontier model estimates a +0.6pp D7 gain worth about $1.1k/day, so the net is -$5.1k/day, not -$6.2k/day - and this offset is included in the recommendation rather than ignored.
worked_end_to_end_example.q8_action: Revert interstitial_cooldown to 55s (a midpoint, not the original 45s - the retention offset is real and worth partially keeping). EV +$1.7k/day net. Alternative rejected: full revert to 45s (+$5.1k/day gross but sacrifices the retention gain, net +$1.4k/day after the LTV effect). Alternative rejected: raise ad floors to compensate (+$0.4k/day, does not address the cause, would require reversal later). Do nothing: -$5.1k/day.
worked_end_to_end_example.q9_confidence: 0.79 calibrated. Limiting: no intervention test yet; one unexcludable confounder (version adoption) ruled out on alignment grounds only.
worked_end_to_end_example.q10_measurement: Predict impressions/DAU recovers to within 4% of baseline within 6 hours of propagation; ad ARPDAU to within 3%; D7 retention for post-change cohorts remains at least 0.3pp above the pre-change baseline. Controls: geos outside the config targeting. Failure criterion: under 50% recovery at +6h means the config was not the cause and the change is itself reverted. Measurement at +6h, +24h, +7d, +30d.
worked_end_to_end_example.outcome: Config reverted to 55s autonomously (Pulse, config-revert grant, confidence 0.85 after the targeting-match evidence). At +6h impressions/DAU recovered 94% of the gap; at +7d ad ARPDAU was within 1.8% of baseline and D7 retention held +0.5pp. Hypothesis confirmed; Pulse's precedent prior for config-alignment findings updated upward; the incident became a template playbook for 'config-aligned metric regression'.

governance.philosophy: Autonomy is a privilege granted narrowly, earned by evidence, enforced mechanically, and revocable instantly. Governance is implemented as code (policy bundles in version control, evaluated in the execution path) rather than as documentation, because a control that is not evaluated on every action is not a control.

permissions: no actions, no approvals, no settings
approve actions on entities they own up to 0.10% of S_daily per action and 0.5% cumulative per day
mute alerts on their entities for up to 24h
approve monetization actions up to 0.5% of daily ad revenue per action
approve config changes within blast-radius class low/medium
all UA Manager across all networks/titles
approve up to 0.5% of S_daily per action
approve reallocation packages up to 5% of S_daily
approve DAG and metric definition changes
approve up to 2% of S_daily per action
override a Warden denial with a typed justification
approve payback policy and target ROAS changes
approve rev-share and net-revenue parameter changes
read-only access to the complete audit ledger, policy history, and all agent decisions
modify policy bundles via reviewed pull request
roles.cannot: approve business actions or grant autonomy through the application

principles: Least privilege by default; every grant is scoped to entities, not just to action types.
Separation of duties: nobody can both grant autonomy and be the sole approver of actions taken under it (autonomy grants require dual approval from two different role families).
Every permission is evaluated server-side at the gateway; the UI hides what a user cannot do, but hiding is never the control.
All role assignments are versioned and reviewed quarterly.

approval_workflows.routing: Determined by (action type, exposure, entity ownership, risk score). The system routes to the lowest-authority role whose limit covers the action, with escalation on SLA breach.

sla_by_severity.on_breach: escalate one level; at two breaches escalate two levels and notify the original approver's manager

approval_workflows.expiry: Every proposal carries a TTL (default 24h, 4h for time-sensitive actions). An expired proposal is not executed - it is re-evaluated from scratch against current data, because acting on yesterday's analysis is a common and avoidable failure.
dual_approval_required_for: changes to the objective function weights
approval_workflows.bulk_approval: Permitted only within one action type, only when every item is individually under the approver's per-item cap, and only after the UI displays the aggregate blast radius and total exposure. The aggregate is what gets approved, and it is audited as a single decision with its constituent items.
approval_workflows.rejection_handling: Rejection requires a reason code (Wrong data / Wrong cause / Right cause wrong action / Bad timing / Business context the system lacks / Too risky / Other with text). Reason codes are training signal: a pattern of 'Business context the system lacks' means the global context store is incomplete, which is a fixable platform gap rather than an agent failure.
approval_workflows.delegation: Approvers can delegate for a defined period with a defined cap; delegation is audited and expires automatically.
approval_workflows.emergency_path: For Sev-1 with exposure above 1% of S_daily, any of VP Growth, Head of Data or CMO can approve unilaterally with a post-hoc review requirement within 24 hours.

layers.limit: shared across all agents: 35% cumulative parameter change per campaign per day, 50% per rolling 7 days
agent-specific budget in S_daily percentage terms (Hunter 3.0%, Ledger 4.0% gross movement, Muse 1.5% affected spend, Vault 1.5% of ad revenue, others lower)
10% of weekly portfolio spend for spend-acting agents
6% of S_daily in cumulative authorized exposure; on approach, Atlas authorizes strictly in priority order and reports what it deferred
rate limits per hour to prevent a cascade (e.g. max 12 budget changes fleet-wide per hour)

agent_action_limits.enforcement: All counters are maintained by Warden in a transactional store and checked synchronously at the gateway. Counters reset at 00:00 UTC. A counter check failure is a hard deny, never a warning.
agent_action_limits.limit_review: Monthly: which limits actually bound decisions, what value was blocked, and what would have happened. A limit that never binds is probably too loose; one that binds constantly is probably costing money. Both are reviewed with data, and changing one requires dual approval.

what_is_logged: every finding with its complete evidence bundle reference
every proposal, authorization, denial (with the binding constraint), approval and rejection (with reason code)
every execution with prior state, requested state, realized state, and the raw external API exchange
every rollback with its trigger and outcome
every policy evaluation including the inputs
every autonomy change, kill switch activation, freeze, and override
every model version promotion and every metric definition change
every human login, permission change, and data access to user-level tables
every LLM call with prompt hash, model tier, tokens and cost
properties: append-only: the schema has no UPDATE or DELETE path
hash-chained: each record includes the hash of the previous, with a daily anchor published internally so tampering is detectable
mirrored to WORM object storage within 60 seconds
queryable by entity, agent, actor, time, action type, and outcome
audit_logging.reconstruction_guarantee: For any action ever taken, an auditor can reconstruct: what data the system saw (with as-of timestamps and completeness), what it concluded and with what confidence, which policy permitted it, who or what authorized it, what it did, and what happened next. This is the operative definition of accountability in this system.
audit_logging.reporting: Daily autonomous-action digest; weekly governance review pack; monthly compliance export; on-demand entity history.

properties: Every autonomous action registers a rollback plan and trigger conditions BEFORE execution; an action without a valid rollback plan cannot execute.
The Rollback Daemon is independent of the agents - an agent cannot suppress or delay its own rollback.
Human one-click undo is available on every autonomous action for 72 hours, requires no justification, and is not treated as a failure of the human.
Rollback failures are Sev-1 and disable the action type immediately.
Rollback rate is a tracked KPI per agent and per action type, drives automatic demotion, and is reported weekly.

explainability.requirement: Every finding and every action carries a structured explanation artifact. The artifact is the record of truth; prose is rendered from it and is never the source.
explanation_artifact_schema: why (ranked hypotheses with posteriors, supporting and refuting evidence)
impact (incurred and projected with intervals and method)
what_we_did or what_we_recommend with the EV computation
alternatives considered and why they were rejected (including do-nothing)
confidence with all components and limiting factors
what_would_change_our_mind (the specific evidence that would falsify this)
data_provenance (datasets, as-of timestamps, completeness, model versions)
explainability.numeric_grounding: An automated validator checks that every number appearing in the rendered prose exists in the evidence bundle within float tolerance or is derivable by a whitelisted formula. Failures block publication and are logged as a model-quality incident.
audience_layers: full structured artifact for the drill-down
raw evidence and SQL for the analyst
explainability.counterfactual_requirement: Every explanation must state what would have happened without the action. An explanation without a counterfactual is a description, not an explanation.

matrix.definition: projected impact > 1.5% of S_daily/day, or any safety/data-integrity event, or an agent-caused incident
projected impact 0.3-1.5% of S_daily/day, or a guardrail breach, or a model/measurement degradation
projected impact < 0.3% of S_daily/day, or informational findings

anti_fatigue_controls: correlated findings merged into one incident before routing
per-channel budget of 6 non-Sev-1 messages/hour with overflow batched
repeat suppression by fingerprint within cooldown
auto-demotion of message types a recipient has ignored 10 consecutive times
a 'not useful' button on every alert that decrements the detector's routing weight
quiet hours per recipient for non-Sev-1
alert_routing.guarantee: Sev-1 is never rate-limited, batched, demoted, or subject to quiet hours.

levels.scope: one action type for one agent
levels.effect: that action type is denied; the agent continues everything else
the agent drops to Observe; it keeps detecting and publishing findings

levels.who: Head of UA, Head of Data, VP Growth
levels.effect: all agents in the module drop to Recommend

levels.who: Head of Data, VP Growth, CMO
levels.effect: every agent drops to Recommend; nothing executes without a human
every agent drops to Observe; all pending actions cancelled; all in-flight reversible actions rolled back
levels.restore: dual approval + a completed post-incident review

properties: Activation takes effect fleet-wide within 5 seconds.
Safety switches never require a quorum - waiting for a second approver during an incident is itself a risk.
Automatic activation: Warden triggers L1/L2 on safety conditions and L5 on a fleet-wide rollback storm.
Every activation notifies all stakeholders immediately and opens an incident record.
A quarterly drill exercises L4 and L5 in production to verify they actually work - an untested kill switch is a belief, not a control.

per_agent_autonomy_settings.structure: A matrix of (agent x action_type) cells. Each granted cell specifies: entity_scope (which titles/networks/campaign classes), dollar_band (min and max exposure), confidence_threshold, rate_limits (per entity, per day), cooldown, required_preconditions, rollback_triggers, and an expiry date (all grants expire and must be renewed - no permanent grants).
per_agent_autonomy_settings.defaults: Every cell starts denied. A new agent has zero granted cells regardless of how good it looks in testing.
promotion_gates: Observe -> Recommend: 30 days in Observe, >= 50 findings emitted, precision >= 0.70, calibration fittable.
Recommend -> Autonomous: 30 days in Recommend, >= 30 human decisions on that action type, approval rate >= 0.80, realized-vs-predicted MAPE <= 0.35, zero Sev-1 caused, Brier <= 0.20, dual approval.
automatic_demotion_triggers: 3 rollbacks on one action type within 24h
realized impact sign wrong on >= 30% of the last 20 actions
consumer lag > 30 minutes on a realtime topic
per_agent_autonomy_settings.change_control: Grants are stored as version-controlled policy (Rego bundles in git), changed only by reviewed pull request plus dual approval in the console. Every proposed change is accompanied by a historical simulation: how many actions would this have permitted in the last 90 days, with what estimated value and what estimated risk.
per_agent_autonomy_settings.expiry_and_review: All grants expire after 90 days and require explicit renewal with a performance review. This prevents the slow accumulation of unexamined autonomy, which is how automated systems become dangerous.

production_safety_controls.detail: The policy engine denies anything not explicitly granted; unknown action types, unknown entities, and unknown scopes are all denials.
Policy engine unavailable, data health unknown, orchestrator unavailable, or audit write failure -> no autonomous execution. The system degrades to human-in-the-loop, never to uncontrolled autonomy.
Every write verifies that the entity's current state matches the prior_state the decision was based on; a mismatch aborts (someone else changed it).
Every write is verified 60 seconds later; a mismatch triggers retry, then rollback, then alert.
Every new action type runs against a sandbox/staging ad account for 14 days before any production grant.
New agents and model versions run in shadow for 30 days, producing decisions that are logged and scored but not executed.
New grants start on the smallest title or lowest geo tier and expand only after 30 days of clean operation.

Automatic freezes: the last 2 business days of a financial period, major holidays per geo, the 14 days after a major app release, during a declared incident, and during any period of degraded core data. Freezes force Observe mode.
Per-action, per-entity, per-agent, and fleet-wide, enforced synchronously.
Entities touched by a human in the last 4 hours are off-limits to autonomous action.

Monthly: inject stale data, partial partitions, model drift, contradictory findings, and API failures into a production-mirror environment and verify that every gate holds and every kill switch works.
Quarterly adversarial review: given the current grants, what is the worst outcome an attacker or a bad model could produce, and which control stops it? Findings become policy changes.
Per-agent LLM and compute budgets with hard caps; an agent exceeding budget degrades to cheaper detection rather than stopping, and alerts the platform team.

levels.L4: VP Growth / Head of Data / Finance

triggers.level: L4 + L5 if impact > 2% of S_daily/day

triggers.condition: Data integrity or measurement failure gating decisions
Guardrail violation attempt above 1% of S_daily
Holdout shows the platform underperforming manual management over a quarter
triggers.level: L5 - and it is reported openly, not buried

privacy_and_compliance.data_minimization: User-level data is pseudonymous by default; direct identifiers live only in the account system and are never joined into analytical tables. Agents operate on aggregates; user-level access requires an explicit permission and is logged per query.
privacy_and_compliance.consent_propagation: ATT/GDPR/CCPA consent state is a first-class dimension. Users in a restricted consent state are excluded from user-level modeling and from any audience export, and this exclusion is enforced in the semantic layer rather than left to query authors.
privacy_and_compliance.deletion: Deletion requests propagate to the warehouse, feature store, agent memory and backups within the documented SLA, with a verifiable deletion record. Agent episodic memory stores only aggregates and entity references, never user-level rows, specifically so that deletion does not require rewriting agent memory.
privacy_and_compliance.regional: Regional data residency where required; cross-border transfer follows the documented legal basis.
privacy_and_compliance.financial_controls: Spend-affecting actions are subject to the same segregation-of-duties and audit standards as any financial system; the audit ledger is designed to satisfy an external auditor's walkthrough of any single action.
privacy_and_compliance.model_governance: Every model in the decision path is registered with its training data window, validation results, known limitations, drift monitors, and an accountable owner. Models are reviewed quarterly.

learning_loop.principle: A recommendation that is never scored is an opinion. MART registers a falsifiable prediction before every action and every finding, measures the realized outcome against an explicit counterfactual, and feeds the error back into the confidence, the playbooks, the models and the thresholds. Nothing in the system is allowed to claim accuracy it has not demonstrated on held-out reality.

prediction_registry.what_is_registered: Every finding and every action writes one or more prediction records BEFORE the action is taken - pre-registration is what prevents retroactive rationalization.
record_schema: failure criteria (what would make this wrong)
confidence at prediction time with all components
prediction_registry.immutability: Prediction records are append-only. A revised prediction is a new record referencing the prior; the original is never edited. The revision history itself is a signal - an agent that constantly revises is either learning fast or unstable, and the distinction is measurable.
prediction_registry.coverage_requirement: 100% of executed actions and >= 95% of emitted findings must carry a prediction. Coverage is a tracked platform KPI; a finding type that cannot be predicted is a finding type that cannot be evaluated, and is a design defect.

counterfactual_measurement.why: Comparing after to before is not measurement - it confuses the action's effect with everything else that changed. Every measurement needs an estimate of what would have happened anyway.

methods_in_priority_order.when: The gold standard, used wherever it is operationally possible
implementations: a persistent 10% of (title x geo) cells managed manually, refreshed quarterly, as the platform-level control
offer holdouts: 5% of users permanently excluded from offers
geo-holdouts for incrementality (matched DMAs, 2-4 week flights)
randomized action assignment across matched campaign pairs where a portfolio has enough similar entities
methods_in_priority_order.cost: the holdout's opportunity cost, accepted deliberately as the price of knowing whether any of this works

methods_in_priority_order.when: For actions that cannot be split by unit but can be split by time (floor changes, pacing rules)
methods_in_priority_order.implementation: randomize the treatment on/off in alternating windows long enough to avoid carryover, then compare within-unit
methods_in_priority_order.weakness: vulnerable to temporal confounding and carryover

methods_in_priority_order.when: The workhorse for one-off actions on a single entity
methods_in_priority_order.implementation: build a weighted composite of 5-15 matched untreated entities (same network, geo tier, objective, spend band) fitted on 14+ days of pre-period, then compare post-period trajectories; report the pre-period fit quality and reject the measurement if it is poor
methods_in_priority_order.weakness: assumes no spillover between treated and control units - explicitly checked for auction cannibalization

methods_in_priority_order.when: When a clean comparable group exists and parallel trends hold
methods_in_priority_order.implementation: test the parallel-trends assumption on the pre-period and report the test result alongside the estimate

methods_in_priority_order.when: When no control group exists at all
methods_in_priority_order.implementation: compare against Prophet's pre-action forecast with its interval
methods_in_priority_order.weakness: weakest evidence class - inherits all forecast error, and is labeled as such so it is never mistaken for experimental evidence

methods_in_priority_order.when: Opportunistic - version holdouts during staged rollouts, config targeting boundaries, geos outside a change's scope
methods_in_priority_order.note: the version-holdout during a staged rollout is the single best control group available in mobile product analytics and is used systematically

measurement_schedule.+1h: propagation and technical verification (did the change actually take effect)
measurement_schedule.+72h: short-run effects (CPI, early cohort quality, eCPM stabilization)
measurement_schedule.+90d: long-run validation for a sampled subset, which is what keeps the pLTV models honest

verdicts: CORRECT: realized effect inside the prediction interval and in the predicted direction
PARTIALLY CORRECT: right direction, magnitude outside the interval
WRONG: opposite direction, or no effect when a material one was predicted

INCONCLUSIVE: the counterfactual is too noisy to distinguish (reported honestly rather than being forced into a verdict - and a high inconclusive rate is itself a finding about the measurement design)

what_gets_updated.mechanism: Weekly isotonic regression per (agent, finding type) mapping raw confidence to empirical correctness over the trailing 180 days. Applied as a post-hoc transform.
what_gets_updated.effect: After calibration, 'confidence 0.8' means approximately 80% of such findings are correct. Before calibration, it means nothing.
what_gets_updated.guardrail: Adjustments are bounded to +/-0.2 per refit so no single week can radically change fleet behavior; combinations with insufficient samples remain uncalibrated and are capped at Mode 2.

what_gets_updated.mechanism: Beta posterior updated per (agent, finding type, entity class) from every adjudicated outcome.
what_gets_updated.effect: An agent that is repeatedly right about creative fatigue on Meta but repeatedly wrong about it on TikTok develops different confidence in each - which is correct, and is invisible to any single global accuracy number.

what_gets_updated.mechanism: Each playbook (a named action recipe attached to a situation fingerprint) tracks applications and successes. Promoted above 0.75 over >= 20 applications; demoted or retired below 0.5 over the last 10.
what_gets_updated.effect: The system accumulates institutional knowledge about what works in this specific business, which is exactly what a good UA manager has and a generic tool does not.
what_gets_updated.creation: New playbooks are proposed by Scholar from clusters of successful ad-hoc actions sharing a situation fingerprint, and require human approval before entering the library.

what_gets_updated.mechanism: Every budget change is an experiment on the response curve. Realized (spend, installs, revenue) points update the fit, weighted by recency and by how clean the measurement was.
what_gets_updated.effect: The curves improve fastest exactly where the system acts most, which is where accuracy matters most. This is the highest-value learning in the platform because these curves drive every allocation decision.
what_gets_updated.note: Observational curve fitting is biased by the fact that budgets were set for reasons correlated with performance. Deliberate randomized budget perturbations (a small, bounded exploration budget of about 1% of spend) are run monthly to de-bias the curves - the explicit price of knowing the curve rather than assuming it.

what_gets_updated.mechanism: Weekly retraining with recency weighting; champion/challenger with a 30-day shadow; promotion requires better calibrated accuracy on a time-based holdout plus no regression in any material slice.
what_gets_updated.effect: Models track a business that changes; the promotion gate stops them from tracking noise.

what_gets_updated.mechanism: Cost-weighted optimization per detector: cost(FP) = attention cost + downstream wrong-action risk; cost(FN) = the realized impact of missed incidents (measurable from post-hoc-identified incidents). The optimal threshold minimizes total expected cost, computed monthly on the historical distribution.
what_gets_updated.effect: Thresholds become an explicit economic decision rather than a taste judgment, and the tradeoff is visible to the humans who bear it.
what_gets_updated.guardrail: A proposed threshold is simulated against 90 days of history and against the known-incident set; any threshold that would have missed a past material incident is rejected regardless of its FP improvement.

what_gets_updated.target: The causal DAG and cause priors
what_gets_updated.mechanism: Adjudicated incident causes update the prior frequency of each cause class per metric. Newly confirmed causal pathways (validated by an intervention) are proposed as DAG edges for human approval.
what_gets_updated.effect: Root-cause analysis gets faster and more accurate as the system accumulates confirmed mechanisms specific to this business.

what_gets_updated.mechanism: Engagement and action rates per recipient per message type update Herald's routing weights.
what_gets_updated.effect: The system learns who actually acts on what, and stops sending the rest.

what_gets_updated.mechanism: Deliberately NOT automated. Scholar produces the analysis (which limits bound, what value was blocked, what the realized risk was) and humans decide.
what_gets_updated.rationale: A safety system that loosens its own limits based on a run of good outcomes is not a safety system. The asymmetry is intentional: tightening can be automatic, loosening cannot.

worked_learning_example.action: Hunter throttles campaign 23851 by 30% on a cohort-quality finding (2026-08-14)
worked_learning_example.prediction_registered: CPI +8% to +15%; installs -28% to -34%; cohort D7 ROAS for post-action cohorts +0.06 to +0.14; 30-day margin +$18.4k [+$9.1k, +$27.8k]. Counterfactual: synthetic control from 8 matched Meta US iOS campaigns. Failure criterion: D7 ROAS unchanged or worse at +7d.
worked_learning_example.measurement_+24h: Spend -29% (as intended); CPI +11% (inside interval); installs -31% (inside interval).
worked_learning_example.measurement_+7d: Post-action cohorts' D7 ROAS +0.09 vs the synthetic control's +0.01 -> treatment effect +0.08, inside the predicted range. Pre-period fit quality of the synthetic control: RMSE 0.014, acceptable.
worked_learning_example.measurement_+30d: Realized margin effect +$21.2k vs predicted +$18.4k. Error +15%, well inside the interval.
updates_applied: Hunter's S_precedent for cohort-quality findings on Meta: 18/24 -> 19/25 (0.71 -> 0.72).
Calibration: this prediction lands in the 0.70-0.75 confidence bucket, which now shows 22 correct of 29 (0.76) - slightly under-confident, so the isotonic transform shifts that bucket up marginally.
The spend-response curve for campaign 23851 gains a real observed point at the lower spend level, tightening its fit.
The situation fingerprint (cohort-quality decline localized to placement x device tier, with stable CPI) is added to the case archive and will be retrieved for future similar incidents.

counter_example_for_contrast.action: Muse rotates a creative on a campaign during an undetected market CPM spike (a real failure mode from the shadow period)
counter_example_for_contrast.realized: IPM flat; the decline was auction-driven, not fatigue
updates: Muse's precedent prior for fatigue findings decreases
the peer-relative check requirement is strengthened from 'recommended' to 'mandatory' before any fatigue action
Scout's market context becomes a hard precondition rather than an advisory input for ACT-CREATIVE-PAUSE
a regression test case is added so future threshold changes are validated against this scenario
counter_example_for_contrast.note: This is the more valuable kind of learning. Failures change the system's structure; successes only adjust its numbers.

value_attribution.question: Is MART actually making the business more money than the humans it assists?
value_attribution.method: A persistent 10% manually-managed holdout at (title x geo) level, refreshed quarterly to avoid drift in what the holdout represents, plus switchback designs where a holdout is impractical. Contribution margin per dollar of spend is compared between the managed and holdout populations, with confidence intervals.
honesty_requirements: Reported monthly with intervals and sample sizes.
Negative or null results are reported with the same prominence as positive ones, within 7 days of detection.
The holdout is never quietly shrunk or cancelled when results are good - that is how organizations lose the ability to know.
Attribution of specific wins to specific agents is reported as an estimate with its method, never as a precise number.
value_attribution.escalation: If the holdout shows the platform underperforming manual management over a full quarter, that goes to the CMO as an L5 finding. The platform's purpose is business value, not its own continuation.

what_the_system_learns_about_itself: which finding types are worth emitting at all (some detectors produce findings nobody ever acts on - they are retired)
which agents earn their compute cost (cost per dollar of realized impact, reported per agent)
where the global context store is incomplete (from the 'business context the system lacks' rejection reason code)
which measurement methods produce usable estimates for which action types (a high inconclusive rate means the measurement design is wrong, not that the action was neutral)
where humans consistently disagree with the system and are right (the highest-value signal in the entire loop, because it points at a structural blind spot rather than a parameter error)
meta_learning.quarterly_system_review: Agent-by-agent: findings emitted, precision, actions taken, realized value, compute cost, human override rate and who was right. Agents that do not earn their cost are rescoped or retired. This review is presented to leadership with the holdout results, and it is the mechanism that keeps the fleet from accumulating dead weight.

technical_architecture.architecture_style: Event-driven lakehouse with a serving layer split by latency class. Batch and streaming converge on one semantic layer so no metric has two definitions. Agents are stateful services on top of that layer, never direct consumers of raw sources.

end_to_end_flow.narrative: Data Source -> Ingestion -> Normalization -> Metrics/Cohorts -> Detection -> Agent Analysis -> Orchestrator -> Recommendation/Action -> Measurement -> Learning Loop

stages.detail: 21 external and internal systems (see data_integration). Each has a declared contract, an owner, and an SLO.

Four patterns - streaming (Kafka), file delivery (object storage notifications), API pull (scheduled connectors with rate-limit budgets), and webhooks. Raw payloads land immutably in bronze with source, fetch timestamp, and a payload hash.
stages.output: bronze tables, append-only, never transformed in place

stages.detail: dbt staging models map every source into canonical schemas: canonical network names, ISO geo codes, USD with the FX rate stamped at ingest, canonical event taxonomy, canonical campaign hierarchy. Contract tests run on every materialization; failures quarantine the model and gate downstream agents.
stages.output: silver tables (fct_installs, fct_events, fct_spend, fct_ad_revenue, fct_purchases, dim_campaign, dim_creative, dim_user)

stages.detail: dbt mart models build fct_cohort_daily, fct_campaign_daily, fct_user_daily and the metric layer. pLTV, churn and retention models score cohorts. The semantic layer exposes governed metrics with their grain declarations, and physically prevents invalid joins (report-date spend to event-date revenue) and invalid comparisons (unequal cohort age).
stages.latency: 15 min for D0 cohorts, 6h for maturing, daily for full
stages.output: gold marts + the semantic layer + ClickHouse projections for serving

stages.detail: Sentinel's tiered detector ensemble runs over the metric series; rule-engine checks run over entity states; data-quality checks run over datasets. Materiality, peer-relative, suppression and dedup filters apply before anything is emitted.
stages.output: KPI_ANOMALY and rule-trigger events with localization payloads

stages.detail: Domain agents consume detections, assemble deterministic evidence bundles, reason (LLM) within a bounded tool budget, verify numerically, score deterministically, and emit structured findings with hypotheses, impact and recommendations.

Atlas merges findings into incidents, resolves conflicts, ranks by priority, applies the portfolio guard with cross-effects, dispatches multi-agent investigations, and issues or withholds execution tokens.
stages.latency: 30 seconds triage; 15 minutes for a Tier A investigation

stages.detail: The Action Gateway performs policy evaluation (Warden), dry-run, prior-state verification, audit pre-write, idempotent execution against the external API, and read-back verification. Mode 2 actions pass through the approvals queue first.
stages.output: external system changes + immutable audit records

stages.detail: Scheduled jobs compute realized outcomes and counterfactuals at +1h/+24h/+72h/+7d/+30d, evaluate rollback triggers, and produce verdicts.
Scholar consumes outcomes, refits calibration, updates precedent priors and playbook hit rates, retrains models, optimizes thresholds, and produces agent scorecards and the value report.
stages.output: updated calibration, priors, playbooks, models, thresholds - which flow back into stages 5 and 6

feedback_edges: Actions -> Metrics (the system's own changes become data it must reason about, tagged so they are never mistaken for exogenous change)
Data health -> every stage (a hard gate, not advice)

data_ingestion_layer.responsibility: Reliable, contract-checked, rate-limit-aware acquisition of every source with restatement handling.
data_ingestion_layer.technology: Dagster (orchestration, chosen over Airflow for asset-based lineage and better partition/backfill semantics) + custom Python connectors + Airbyte for commodity sources + Debezium for CDC
key_design: one connector per source with declarative config for endpoints, rate limits, retry policy, restatement window
token-bucket rate limiting with a shared budget per provider account and priority queues so backfills never starve realtime
checkpointed incremental windows with automatic trailing re-pull (7d cost, 30d conversions, 3d revenue)
file-level and partition-level idempotency
payload hashing to detect silent source changes
connector health and quota consumption are first-class monitored metrics
data_ingestion_layer.scale: ~180 connector runs/hour; ~2TB/day raw ingest at the stated portfolio scale (dominated by ULAR and internal telemetry)

event_streaming.responsibility: Real-time transport for telemetry and for the agent event bus.
event_streaming.technology: Kafka (or Redpanda for lower operational overhead) + Apache Flink for stateful stream processing + Schema Registry
key_design: separate clusters/namespaces for high-volume telemetry and for the low-volume, high-value agent bus, so a telemetry flood cannot delay a kill switch
Flink jobs for sessionization, real-time metric aggregation, windowed correlation, and ULAR enrichment
exactly-once semantics into the warehouse via transactional sinks; at-least-once with idempotent consumers on the agent bus
transactional outbox pattern for agent event emission
event_streaming.scale: ~4B events/day telemetry; ~2k events/day on the agent bus (the value density difference is the point)

data_warehouse_lakehouse.responsibility: The durable, queryable record of truth.
data_warehouse_lakehouse.technology: BigQuery or Snowflake as the primary warehouse; Apache Iceberg tables on object storage for the bronze/raw layer and for cheap long-term retention; dbt for all transformations
key_design: medallion layering (bronze/silver/gold) with dbt tests at every boundary
partitioning by date, clustering by the highest-selectivity dimensions
cohort tables partitioned by install_date and clustered by title/source/geo/age
all transformations version-controlled and CI-tested; no manual DDL in production
column-level lineage exposed to the UI and to agents (so an agent knows exactly what its decision depends on)
cost controls: query cost budgets per team and per agent, materialized aggregates for hot paths, partition pruning enforced by policy
data_warehouse_lakehouse.scale: ~400TB active, ~3PB with history; ~50k queries/day of which the majority are agent-issued

real_time_analytics.responsibility: Sub-second serving of realtime tiles and of the detection substrate.
real_time_analytics.technology: ClickHouse (primary; chosen for ingestion throughput plus aggregation speed on wide dimension tables) with pre-aggregated materialized views; optionally Apache Pinot for the highest-QPS tiles
key_design: materialized views maintaining rollups at the exact grains the dashboard and detectors need, so no query aggregates raw rows at read time
TTL policies moving cold data to the warehouse

the same metric definitions as the warehouse, generated from one dbt/semantic source to prevent definitional drift between realtime and batch - two definitions of ARPDAU is a governance failure, not a technical convenience
real_time_analytics.scale: p95 < 300ms on realtime tiles; ~7M series scanned per detection pass

feature_store.responsibility: Consistent features for training and for online scoring, with point-in-time correctness.
feature_store.technology: Feast (offline store: the warehouse; online store: Redis) or a managed equivalent
key_design: point-in-time-correct joins for training (no leakage from the future - the most common and most damaging modeling bug)
feature versioning with the definition stored alongside
online serving for churn and pLTV scoring at p99 < 20ms
feature drift monitoring (PSI) wired directly into the model health interlocks
the same feature definitions used by agents for evidence assembly, so 'D0 sessions' means one thing everywhere

agent_memory.responsibility: Working, episodic, semantic and procedural memory for 22 agents.
agent_memory.technology: Redis (working, TTL 24h) + Postgres with pgvector (episodic and semantic, with embedding search) + object storage (immutable evidence bundles, content-addressed) + a graph representation of the causal DAG and entity relationships (Postgres with recursive CTEs at this scale; a dedicated graph store only if traversal depth grows)
key_design: episodic memory stores findings, actions and outcomes as structured records plus an embedding of the evidence summary, enabling 'have we seen this before' retrieval
semantic memory is curated and versioned: metric definitions, causal DAG, network behavior notes, seasonal priors, per-slice baselines
procedural memory holds versioned playbooks with hit rates
strict aggregate-only policy: agent memory never contains user-level rows, which keeps deletion requests from requiring memory rewrites
memory writes are append-only and attributable to an agent version

llm_layer.responsibility: Hypothesis generation, cross-source synthesis, narrative rendering, unstructured input processing (creative content, store reviews, network changelogs), and natural-language interrogation.
llm_layer.technology: A model gateway service in front of the model provider, providing tiering, caching, structured-output enforcement, cost accounting and fallback

tiering.usage: event triage, classification, summarization, routine narrative - roughly 90% of call volume
standard agent reasoning and evidence interpretation
orchestrator synthesis, conflict resolution, Tier A root-cause investigations, any decision above 0.5% of S_daily

hard_constraints: structured output enforced via tool schemas with retry on schema violation
numeric grounding validator: every number in the output must exist in the evidence bundle within tolerance or be derivable by a whitelisted formula
no action authorization: the model proposes an action object; deterministic code and the policy engine decide
bounded tool budget per investigation (<= 6 extra evidence queries for a domain agent, <= 40 for a Tier A investigation)
prompt caching on the static portion (charter, taxonomy, schemas, guardrails) with only the evidence bundle varying
full observability: every call logs prompt hash, tier, tokens, latency, cost, and outcome

prompt injection defense: all external text (store reviews, network changelogs, competitor copy, creative text) is wrapped as untrusted data with explicit instructions that it is content to analyze, never instructions to follow, and is never placed in a system-instruction position
llm_layer.evaluation: A regression suite of ~200 historical incidents with adjudicated causes runs against every prompt or model change before deployment; changes that reduce cause-attribution accuracy or increase numeric-grounding failures are blocked.
llm_layer.cost_control: Per-agent budgets with hard caps; tier is selected from the investigation's dollar impact before reasoning begins; estimated fleet cost at the stated scale is roughly $6-12k/month, which is small against a $7.5M/month media budget and is reported alongside agent value.

rules_engine.responsibility: Deterministic policy evaluation for guardrails, autonomy grants, alert routing and threshold rules.
rules_engine.technology: Open Policy Agent (Rego bundles, version-controlled in git, deployed via CI) for authorization; a lightweight expression evaluator (CEL) for threshold and routing rules editable in the console with review
key_design: default deny
synchronous evaluation in the execution path at p99 < 50ms
every evaluation logs its inputs and the binding constraint on denial
policy changes go through pull request review plus dual approval in the console, and every change ships with a historical simulation of its effect
policy bundles are signed and their version is recorded on every action

forecasting_models.responsibility: Spend, installs, revenue, DAU, margin and cash forecasts; spend-response curves; pLTV; retention curves; churn.
forecasting_models.technology: Python (LightGBM/XGBoost, statsmodels, Prophet/NeuralProphet, PyMC or NumPyro for hierarchical Bayesian models, lifelines for survival), trained on managed compute, registered in MLflow

model_inventory.type: two-stage GBT (payer classifier + conditional revenue) + survival retention + ad-revenue component, with hierarchical shrinkage for small slices
GBT on D0-D2 behavioral features with slice priors

model_inventory.usage: cohort aggregates and CRM segments only, never UA decisions

model_inventory.type: Hill/log-response with Bayesian uncertainty, fitted per campaign on a rolling 90-day window with recency weighting plus randomized perturbation data

ensemble (SARIMAX with exogenous regressors, GBT on calendar/lag features, a structural cohort-accumulation model, seasonal naive baseline) with MinT hierarchical reconciliation and conformal prediction intervals
Bayesian time-series with adstock and saturation, geo-hierarchical
model_inventory.usage: channel-level ROI cross-check against MMP attribution

model_inventory.type: causal dose-response on impressions/DAU vs retention, estimated from experiments plus matched observational data
mixed-effects model of attributes on IPM and downstream ROAS, with multimodal attribute extraction from the assets
supervised composite of D0 features against realized D30 ROAS

forecasting_models.governance: Every model registered with training window, validation results, known limitations, drift monitors, and an owner. Champion/challenger with shadow periods. Every downstream decision records the model version used.

anomaly_detection_engine.responsibility: Tiered detection across ~7.2M series with bounded cost.
anomaly_detection_engine.technology: Flink jobs for streaming detectors on T1 series; scheduled Python/Spark jobs for T2/T3; models served from a shared library so the same detector code runs in both paths
key_design: tiered cost control: cheap screening on the long tail, full ensemble only on candidates
per-series adaptive baselines stored in ClickHouse
peer-group definitions maintained as a first-class dataset
suppression calendar integration
fingerprint-based dedup with per-fingerprint cooldowns
threshold simulation harness for safe tuning
anomaly_detection_engine.scale: ~15k raw detector fires/day reduced to 80-200 emitted findings

agent_orchestrator.responsibility: Atlas: incident graph, conflict resolution, prioritization, dispatch, portfolio guard, authorization tokens.
agent_orchestrator.technology: A stateful service (Kubernetes, leader-elected) with the incident graph in Postgres, working state in Redis, and reasoning through the model gateway's frontier tier
key_design: deterministic scoring, ranking and constraint checks in code; judgment and synthesis in the model
signed, short-TTL execution tokens
graceful degradation: if Atlas is unavailable, all agents fall back to Recommend automatically
investigation choreography with tiered budgets and parallel dispatch

action_execution_layer.responsibility: The single, audited, idempotent path to every external write.
action_execution_layer.technology: The Action Gateway service plus per-network adapter modules
key_design: one gateway for all writes - no agent ever calls a network API directly, which is what makes the audit complete
adapter per external system encapsulating auth, rate limits, retries, error taxonomy and idempotency semantics
two-phase: dry-run with prior-state verification, then commit
audit pre-write before execution; an unauditable action cannot execute
read-back verification 60 seconds after every write
credential management via a secrets manager with short-lived tokens and per-adapter scoping
circuit breakers per external system: repeated failures disable that adapter and alert rather than retrying into a rate-limit ban
a complete replay log of every request and response for debugging and for disputes with networks
action_execution_layer.scale: 30-90 autonomous actions/day plus human-initiated changes; designed for 10x headroom

audit_event_log.responsibility: The immutable record of everything the system saw, concluded, and did.
audit_event_log.technology: Append-only Postgres tables with hash chaining, mirrored to WORM object storage (S3 Object Lock / GCS retention policy), 7-year retention, with a daily anchor hash published to an internal notary
key_design: no UPDATE or DELETE path exists in the schema or the application
write path exclusively through the gateway service account
queryable by entity, agent, actor, time, type and outcome
evidence bundles are content-addressed in object storage so an event's evidence can never drift from what the agent actually saw
auditor role with isolated read-only access

api_bff_layer.responsibility: Serve the frontend and external consumers with governed, permission-checked, latency-appropriate data.
api_bff_layer.technology: TypeScript BFF (Node/Fastify) with tRPC or GraphQL; SSE/WebSocket for realtime push; REST for external integrations
key_design: queries route by latency class (ClickHouse for realtime, warehouse for deep analysis) transparently to the client
the semantic layer is the only source of metrics - the BFF cannot compute a metric itself, which is what prevents dashboard-specific definitions
row- and column-level permission enforcement server-side
response caching with metric-aware TTLs and cache busting on materialization
query cost guards that reject or downgrade expensive requests with a clear message rather than timing out

dashboard_frontend.responsibility: The human interface described in dashboard_layout.
dashboard_frontend.technology: Next.js + React + TypeScript; TanStack Query for server state; ECharts/visx for charts (canvas rendering for large series); TanStack Virtual for large tables; Apache Arrow + DuckDB-WASM for client-side slicing of already-loaded data
key_design: deep-linkable state (filters, date range, grain, attribution model, comparison) so any view is shareable
the noise-band significance rule applied at render, so insignificant deltas are visually neutral
streaming updates via SSE for realtime tiles
optimistic UI for approvals with server confirmation
WCAG 2.2 AA compliance including screen-reader summaries generated from the underlying series
performance budget enforced in CI (bundle size, tile payload size, render timing)

cross_cutting_concerns.observability: OpenTelemetry traces across ingestion, agents, gateway and frontend; a single correlation_id follows a finding from the raw data through to the executed action and its measurement. Dashboards for pipeline health, agent health, model health, gateway health and cost. Alerting on SLO breaches.
security: secrets in a managed secrets manager, rotated, never in config or code
per-adapter least-privilege API credentials with separate read and write credentials where the provider supports it
network isolation: the Action Gateway is the only service with write credentials to external ad platforms
SSO with MFA; SCIM provisioning; quarterly access review
encryption at rest and in transit; column-level encryption for any sensitive field
audit logging of all data access to user-level tables
prompt injection defenses in the model gateway (untrusted content wrapping, no instruction-position external text)
supply chain: pinned dependencies, SBOM, image scanning
reliability: multi-AZ for stateful services; RPO 15 minutes, RTO 2 hours for the warehouse; RPO ~0 for the audit log

graceful degradation ladder: model gateway down -> agents run detection-only and queue findings; orchestrator down -> agents drop to Recommend; gateway down -> no autonomous execution, actions queue; warehouse down -> realtime tiles continue from ClickHouse with a degraded banner
chaos testing monthly against a production mirror

cost_envelope.total_estimate: $55-95k/month at the stated portfolio scale, roughly 0.7-1.3% of media spend - the threshold the value report must clear.

environments: staging (mirrors production data with a 24h lag, used for agent shadow runs and connector testing)
sandbox ad accounts for action-path testing with real APIs and trivial budgets

build: the cohort and semantic layer (this is the differentiating asset and no vendor's definition of cohort ROAS will match the business)
connectors for the high-value marketing sources where control over restatement and rate limits matters
the entire agent fleet and orchestrator
the Action Gateway and policy layer
the decision engine and learning loop
the dashboard (a generic BI tool cannot express the agent-integrated, action-oriented interface this design requires)
build_vs_buy.rationale: Buy anything where a vendor's definition is acceptable; build anything where the definition is the product.

implementation_phases.name: Foundation & Truth
implementation_phases.objective: Establish a single, trustworthy, cohort-grain view of the business. Nothing else in this plan is buildable on unreliable data, and every attempt to skip this phase produces an agent fleet that confidently acts on garbage.

workstreams.scope: Connectors for AppsFlyer, Meta, Google, TikTok, Unity, AppLovin (including ULAR), LevelPlay, Firebase/BigQuery export, RevenueCat, internal backend CDC, App Store Connect, Google Play. Contract definitions and restatement handling for each.
Medallion layering in dbt; canonical dimension normalization (networks, geos, currencies, events); identity resolution; the cohort key and fct_cohort_daily; fct_campaign_daily; fct_user_daily.
The metric dictionary implemented as governed metrics with grain enforcement; the physical prohibition on invalid joins and unequal-age comparisons.
Janitor v1: freshness, volume, schema, contract tests, arrival-curve learning, lineage graph, health state publication.
Four-way install reconciliation and revenue reconciliation with tolerance bands.

deliverables: A warehouse where cohort ROAS at any slice is correct and defensible
The data quality module and its health-state feed
Reconciliation dashboards
Documented contracts and SLOs for all 12 initial sources
exit_criteria: Install counts reconcile within tolerance across all four systems for 14 consecutive days
Revenue reconciles within 1% of settled store reports for a full month
Cohort tables materialize within SLO for 14 consecutive days
A named analyst can reproduce every number in a manual monthly report from the warehouse in under an hour
implementation_phases.team: 2 data engineers, 1 analytics engineer, 1 platform engineer

key_risks.risk: Connector rate limits and undocumented API behavior consume more time than estimated
key_risks.mitigation: Start with the three highest-spend networks; treat the rest as a parallel, lower-priority stream

key_risks.risk: Identity resolution gaps (customer_user_id not set in Firebase/RevenueCat/mediation SDKs) block cohort joins
key_risks.mitigation: Audit SDK integrations in week 1; this is a client-side change with a release cycle, so it must be discovered early or it becomes a 6-week blocker

implementation_phases.value_milestone: Reporting time cut; the first defensible cohort ROAS numbers the whole organization agrees on.

implementation_phases.name: Dashboard & Observability
implementation_phases.objective: Ship the human-facing platform: the Command Center and the first six module cockpits, so the organization gets value before any agent exists and so the team learns what questions people actually ask.

workstreams.scope: ClickHouse projections; the BFF; realtime streaming tiles; the query-cost guard.

Global shell (grain toggle, attribution model selector, comparison modes, data health pill); Command Center; cockpits for Executive, UA, Ad Monetization, Retention/Cohorts, LTV/ROAS, Creative; the Cohort Explorer.
Drill-down paths, annotations, the noise-band significance rule, export and scheduled digests.

deliverables: A production dashboard replacing the majority of manual reporting
The Cohort Explorer
Scheduled digests
exit_criteria: p95 tile load within budget
80% of the previous manual reporting workflow retired
Daily active usage by the UA, monetization and product teams
Zero definitional disputes open for more than 48 hours (a proxy for the semantic layer actually being trusted)
implementation_phases.team: 2 frontend engineers, 1 backend engineer, 1 analytics engineer, 1 designer

key_risks.risk: Building what the team says it wants rather than what it needs, producing a prettier version of the spreadsheets
key_risks.mitigation: Ship the Command Center's decision-oriented framing first and iterate against observed usage, not requests

implementation_phases.value_milestone: Analyst hours redeployed; the first shared source of truth.

implementation_phases.name: Models & Detection
implementation_phases.objective: Build the predictive and detection substrate that agents will reason on, and prove it is accurate before anything acts on it.

workstreams.scope: Two-stage model with survival retention and ad-revenue components, hierarchical shrinkage, prediction intervals, SHAP attribution, the prediction registry, and the model health interlock.
Early-signal D7/D30 prediction from D0-D2 behavior; curve fitting; churn scoring.
The hierarchical ensemble with MinT reconciliation and conformal intervals; the forecast registry.
The seven-detector ensemble; tiering; materiality, peer-relative, suppression and dedup filters; the threshold simulation harness.
Point-in-time-correct offline store; online serving; drift monitoring.

deliverables: pLTV in production with a published accuracy badge
The anomaly engine running in Observe with human adjudication of every emission
Forecasts with measured interval coverage
exit_criteria: pLTV D30 MAPE <= 0.20 on a time-based holdout with |bias| <= 5%
Forecast interval coverage within 4pp of nominal
Anomaly precision >= 0.70 on 30 days of human-adjudicated emissions
Alert volume within the fatigue budget
implementation_phases.team: 2 data scientists, 1 ML engineer, 1 data engineer

key_risks.risk: pLTV accuracy insufficient for decision-making, which blocks the entire economics-gated agent design
key_risks.mitigation: Ship the analogue-based (model-free) cohort comparison first as a fallback decision aid; it is worse but usable, and it keeps Phase 3 unblocked
The peer-relative test and materiality gate are built in from day one rather than added after the first alert storm burns credibility

implementation_phases.value_milestone: Forward-looking cohort economics; the first automated detections, human-adjudicated.

implementation_phases.name: First Agents in Observe
implementation_phases.objective: Deploy the first agent cohort in Observe mode, prove they produce findings humans agree with, and build the shared agent infrastructure properly the first time.

workstreams.scope: The common runtime (gate -> detect -> localize -> assemble -> reason -> verify -> score -> decide -> emit), memory architecture, the model gateway with tiering and numeric grounding, evidence bundle construction, the finding schema and event bus.
Janitor (already partly built), Sentinel, Prism, Anchor, Oracle, Hunter (Observe), Vault (Observe), Muse (Observe).
Confidence, impact, priority, EV and risk scoring, with all components persisted.
Prediction registry, measurement jobs, human adjudication UI, initial calibration.

deliverables: 8 agents in Observe with findings surfacing in the dashboard
The agent event bus
The decision engine
Agent scorecards with 30 days of adjudicated precision
exit_criteria: Finding precision >= 0.70 across the fleet on human adjudication
Every finding carries hypotheses, impact, recommendation and measurement plan (schema-enforced)
Numeric-grounding validator failure rate < 1%
Calibration fittable for at least 5 agent/finding-type combinations
The UA team reports that agent findings surface things they would have missed (a qualitative gate, deliberately - if the humans do not find them useful, precision numbers are irrelevant)
implementation_phases.team: 2 backend engineers, 1 ML engineer, 1 data scientist, 1 frontend engineer

key_risks.risk: Agents produce plausible narratives that are wrong, which is worse than no narrative because it is trusted
key_risks.mitigation: Mandatory refutation step, numeric grounding, DAG-constrained hypotheses, and an honest UNKNOWN verdict path that is monitored (an UNKNOWN rate near zero is a red flag, not a success)

key_risks.risk: LLM cost or latency exceeds budget
key_risks.mitigation: Tiering by impact and prompt caching from day one; per-agent hard budgets

implementation_phases.value_milestone: Detection latency drops from days to hours; root-cause analysis time drops sharply.

implementation_phases.name: Orchestration & Recommend Mode
implementation_phases.objective: Stand up Atlas, add the remaining agents, and move the fleet to Recommend - producing fully specified, approvable actions with a real approval workflow.

workstreams.scope: Incident graph and merging, conflict resolution with the precedence hierarchy, priority ranking, the portfolio guard and cross-effect matrix, investigation choreography with tiers, the global context store.
Ledger, Merchant, Compass, Prophet, Pulse, Lab, Beacon, Scout, Abacus, Sherlock, Herald, Warden, Scholar.
The approvals queue, RBAC, routing, SLAs, rejection reason codes, dry-run diffs.
Adapters, dry-run, prior-state verification, audit pre-write, idempotency - built and exercised against sandbox accounts without production writes.
The policy engine, autonomy matrix (all cells denied), audit log, kill switches, Agent Ops console.

deliverables: All 22 agents live in Recommend
The full approval workflow in production
The Action Gateway validated against sandbox accounts
The complete governance layer
exit_criteria: Recommendation approval rate >= 0.75
Zero conflicting recommendations reaching humans (the orchestrator resolves or escalates them)
Approval SLA compliance >= 90%
Every action type has >= 30 human decisions recorded
Realized-vs-predicted MAPE <= 0.35 on approved-and-executed actions
Kill switch drill passes at L4 and L5
Chaos test passes: stale data, partial partitions, drift and contradictory findings all correctly gated
implementation_phases.team: 3 backend engineers, 1 ML engineer, 1 data scientist, 1 frontend engineer, 1 platform engineer

key_risks.risk: Approval fatigue - too many proposals, humans rubber-stamp them, and the approval control becomes theatre
key_risks.mitigation: Strict recommendation-strength gating (weak recommendations are never surfaced), aggressive merging, and monitoring of approval latency and rubber-stamp patterns (approvals faster than could plausibly involve reading)

key_risks.risk: The orchestrator becomes a bottleneck or a black box
key_risks.mitigation: Deterministic scoring in code, full decision transparency in the UI, and graceful degradation to Recommend if it is unavailable

implementation_phases.value_milestone: Time-to-action drops from days to hours; the first measurable margin improvement attributable to faster, better-informed decisions.

implementation_phases.name: Controlled Autonomy
implementation_phases.objective: Grant the first narrow autonomy on protective, reversible actions, prove safety in production, then expand cell by cell.

workstreams.scope: Grant in strict order of reversibility and blast radius: (1) protective and non-financial (data gating, model interlocks, guardrail experiment stops, market suppression); (2) reversible configuration (config reverts, floor adjustments, dead-instance disabling); (3) protective financial (budget decreases, fraud blocklists, creative pauses); (4) expansionary financial (budget increases, creative promotion, reallocation steps) - last, and with the tightest thresholds.
The independent Rollback Daemon, trigger evaluation, human one-click undo, storm detection.
Counterfactual infrastructure: synthetic control, the manual-managed holdout, switchback capability, offer holdouts.
Full calibration, playbook management, threshold optimization, spend-response curve learning from the system's own actions, randomized exploration budget.

deliverables: Autonomy live on the graduated action set
The rollback system with drilled procedures
The 10% manual-managed holdout established
The first value attribution report
exit_criteria: Zero actions executed outside their granted bounds
Rollback rate <= 5%
Realized impact sign correct on >= 70% of autonomous actions
Fleet Brier score <= 0.20
Zero Sev-1 incidents caused by an autonomous action
The holdout comparison shows non-negative platform contribution with a defensible interval
implementation_phases.team: 3 backend engineers, 1 data scientist, 1 platform engineer, 1 growth ops lead (embedded, not consulted)

key_risks.risk: The first autonomous mistake destroys organizational trust regardless of its size
key_risks.mitigation: Start with protective actions only; canary on the smallest title; make every action visible in the action feed within 30 seconds; a one-click undo that nobody is criticized for using; and communicate the first month's actions proactively rather than letting people discover them

key_risks.risk: Guardrails are set so tight that autonomy delivers no value and the effort looks wasted
key_risks.mitigation: The monthly binding-limit review with the estimated value of blocked actions, so loosening is a data-driven decision rather than a nerve-driven one

implementation_phases.value_milestone: 24/7 response on the actions that most need speed; the first measured autonomous margin contribution.

implementation_phases.name: Expansion & Maturity
implementation_phases.objective: Broaden coverage, deepen intelligence, and make the system durable - so it survives team turnover, portfolio changes and provider API changes.

workstreams.scope: Remaining networks and data sources; additional titles; the remaining module cockpits (Product, Experimentation, IAP, ASO, Competitive, Attribution, Marketing Analytics, Agent Ops).
MMM and incrementality integration; the causal DAG maturation from confirmed mechanisms; multimodal creative attribute extraction; natural-language interrogation across the full semantic layer.
Cell-by-cell expansion based on demonstrated performance, each with a historical simulation and dual approval.
Runbooks, onboarding materials, connector resilience to provider API changes, quarterly red-team reviews, the quarterly agent review process.

deliverables: Full portfolio coverage
MMM-calibrated attribution multipliers
A mature playbook library with measured hit rates
The institutionalized quarterly review process
exit_criteria: 12-month targets met: D30 ROAS +8% vs holdout, wasted spend -35%, >= 40% of eligible action volume autonomous with < 5% rollback
Finding precision >= 0.80
The value attribution report shows a defensible positive contribution with a narrowing interval
The system operates through a full quarter without a platform-team intervention outside normal maintenance
implementation_phases.team: Steady state: 2 backend, 1 frontend, 1 data engineer, 1 data scientist, 0.5 platform, plus an embedded growth ops owner

key_risks.risk: Scope creep into adjacent domains (CRM, creative generation, pricing) before the core is durable
key_risks.mitigation: The explicit non-goals list, revisited quarterly and changed deliberately rather than by drift

key_risks.risk: Model and playbook decay as the business changes, silently degrading decisions
key_risks.mitigation: The drift monitors, automatic demotion triggers and quarterly reviews exist precisely for this and are treated as load-bearing, not as reporting

implementation_phases.value_milestone: The platform is a durable competitive capability rather than a project.

rituals.activity: Atlas portfolio review; approvals triage; overnight autonomous action digest reviewed by growth ops.
Scholar's fleet review: precision, calibration, rollbacks, playbook hit rates, cost per agent. Incident retrospectives. Guardrail firing analysis.
Value attribution report with the holdout comparison, published with intervals. Binding-limit review. Threshold re-optimization. Autonomy grant reviews for expiring cells.
Objective function and weight review with leadership. Red-team review. Agent portfolio review (rescope or retire underperformers). Access review. Model governance review. Holdout refresh.
Post-mortem producing either a control improvement, a detector improvement, or a documented decision not to change - never nothing.
